beans.name: Venus House Espresso
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, macadamia, red fruit, lemon
beans.desc: A dependable everyday espresso for black coffee and flat whites yet rich in lattes. Beans change by season, currently Colombian and Brazilian. Black it shows dark chocolate, macadamia, red fruit and lemon; with milk, chocolate, nut and a biscuit finish.

beans.desc: A full-bodied natural with rum-and-raisin depth, bright citrus peel, sweet pear-drop notes and a touch of cocoa. Processing brings a gentle fruity tang. Enjoyable on its own or with milk.

beans.name: Muki Fruity

beans.name: Groove Is In The Heart

beans.name: Decaf Brazil
beans.desc: This sugarcane-decaffeinated Brazilian coffee, grown by Vale de Grama smallholders and roasted in London, offers sweet notes of hazelnut, milk chocolate and caramel with a creamy body. Suited to any time of day, it performs well as espresso, pour-over or filter brew.
beans.priceBasis: Listing "from" price, size not shown (likely 250g); unconfirmed

beans.name: Rwanda Jonathan Ngoga Year 2
beans.desc: A washed Rwandan coffee from producer Jonathan Ngoga, grown near Lake Kivu, returning for a second year. Expect a lively, bright cup with honeycomb sweetness and citrusy yuzu notes. Suits pour-over, ideally with a conical dripper.
beans.priceBasis: Listing "from" price, size not shown (likely 250g); unconfirmed

beans.name: Broadway Blend: The Seasonal One
beans.desc: The roaster's seasonal espresso, a blend of two Central American coffees and the go-to for flat whites at Broadway Market; designed to be balanced and sweet, with El Salvador adding acidity and balance.

beans.name: The Estate
beans.desc: The roaster's signature espresso, showcasing the best of Ethiopian coffee: bright, balanced and complex; good as smooth black coffee and, with milk, like a creamy jaffa cake-like drink.

beans.name: The Baron
beans.desc: A testament to relationships in specialty coffee, from Fazenda Inhame in Campos Altos, Minas Gerais; made for espresso, good in milk drinks or black, with chocolate, nuts and a smooth, dependable sweetness.

beans.name: Niguse Jilo
beans.listedNotes: Dark berry, stone fruit, violet, hibiscus

beans.name: Maria Elena Pulgarin
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, forest berry jam, fruit gummies

beans.name: Colombia La Esmeralda
beans.producer: Buenavista family farm, Quindio; Cesar Buesaquillo; Chiroso
beans.roastNote: Not shown on roaster page (aggregator said Medium)
beans.listedNotes: Jasmine, apricot yoghurt, lychee, persimmon; intense sweetness
beans.desc: A soft, floral Colombian with lively tropical fruit from a six-hectare family farm in Quindío. This natural Chiroso ferments 45 hours in oxygen before drying, giving lychee, apricot and persimmon.

beans.name: Elixir Rwanda Kirunga
beans.listedNotes: Black tea (description adds white grape, kiwi)

beans.name: Kenya Nandi AB
beans.producer: Lot 20 (Sidney Kibet), west Kenya; Batian, Ruiru 11
beans.desc: Sidney Kibet's Lot 20 from Kenya. After pulping, cherries had several half-day water soaks before traditional wet processing, giving layered depth, a lively wine-like tang and crisp, lingering fresh fruit.

beans.name: Heavy Bag Espresso
beans.listedNotes: Sticky nougat, marzipan, ripe blackberries; cocoa nibs aftertaste
beans.desc: A rich, smooth espresso with chewy nougat and almond paste, a hint of fresh blackberry and slowly emerging cacao nibs. Indulgent yet everyday.

beans.name: Off-Trend Espresso
beans.producer: Same components as Heavy Bag, roasted darker
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, black treacle, digestive biscuits

beans.name: Brisbane • Brazil • Espresso
beans.producer: Fazenda Faxina, Edmar de Souza Rezende, Sao Sebastiao do Paraiso, Minas Gerais; Mundo Novo and Yellow Catuai peaberry
beans.listedNotes: Almond toffee, Bakewell tart, cacao nibs
beans.desc: Opens with almond toffee and Bakewell tart sweetness, then smooth nougat and buttery hazelnut, ending in deep cacao. In milk it turns mildly malty and comforting.

beans.name: Count Chocula • Brazil • Espresso & Filter
beans.producer: Fazenda Limeira, Bruno Spuri Silvestrini, Minas Gerais; Mundo Novo

beans.name: Jaffa The Hutt • Brazil • Filter
beans.producer: Nossa Senhora de Fatima, Thiago Henrique Maingoli Muniz, Minas Gerais; Red and Yellow Catuai
beans.listedNotes: Orange, boozy, caramel (description adds florals, deep berry sweetness)

beans.name: Rarities • Lactic & Milk Co-Ferment • Colombia • Filter
beans.processFull: Lactic and yeast co-ferment with milk
beans.desc: A Colombian co-fermented with milk: creamy, sweet coconut aroma, with buttery, cocoa and biscuit-like dairy flavours. Juicy and rich with lively tang, plus floral, dark-fruit and tropical notes.

beans.name: Bellavista Social Club • Peru • Filter
beans.producer: Bellavista, Jaen, Cajamarca; smallholders; Marshell, Geisha, Catuai

beans.name: Chameleon • Uganda • Espresso & Filter

beans.name: Manor Born • Costa Rica • Espresso & Filter
beans.producer: Coop Tarrazu, San Lorenzo community lot, Tarrazu
beans.desc: A silky, rich-bodied coffee layering milk chocolate and caramelised sugar, with gentle marshmallow and almond paste beneath. In a small latte it mellows toward biscuit.

beans.name: Siesta Decaf • Mexico • Espresso & Filter

beans.name: India
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, spices, roasted nuts, earthy finish

beans.name: Bukonzo Dream
beans.desc: A sweet Ugandan with fruity and chocolatey notes, grown high in the Rwenzori range, where altitude lends sharper, brighter flavour. Beans also naturally contain less caffeine. The roaster was won over in tasting.

beans.name: Hope Street Espresso
beans.desc: Named for the street of the brand's first café, this is its longest-running signature espresso and the base of every drink. Berry and salted caramel over a rich chocolate core; the recipe shifts each harvest, with a darker roast.

beans.name: California Calling
beans.desc: A blend inspired by California's coffee culture and the brand's American influences, aiming for bright, fruity flavours with a subtle dark chocolate finish, like espresso in a Bay Area specialty café.

beans.name: Sugarcane Decaf
beans.desc: A decaf made to dispel the idea that decaf is bland: a Colombian blend keeping the depth of regular coffee. Medium-light roasted with toffee, green apple and pecan; good as espresso or filter.

beans.name: Chill 50% Caffeine
beans.desc: A limited in-house roasted blend with about half the caffeine of regular coffee, suiting iced lattes and flat whites while keeping the depth of a double espresso.

beans.name: #1 Indian | Indonesian | Ethiopian
beans.listedNotes: Intense, smoky, notes of toffee and chocolate
beans.source: A Big O Coffee product page
beans.desc: A bold, smoky blend with toffee and chocolate flavours, versatile enough for lattes and cappuccinos. Combines Indian, Indonesian and Ethiopian beans, roasted fresh daily.

beans.name: #1965 Central America
beans.listedNotes: Silky smooth, balanced, full-bodied, slightly sweet, rich and creamy; compared to Blue Mountain
beans.source: A Big O Coffee product page
beans.desc: A coffee that tastes much like the well-regarded Caribbean Blue Mountain: smooth and even, with hearty mouthfeel, a polished flavour and faint sweetness. Central American beans, roasted fresh daily.

beans.name: #2008 Brazilian | Ethiopian
beans.listedNotes: Deep spice, wine or chocolate-like taste, floral aroma
beans.source: A Big O Coffee product page
beans.desc: A bestseller roasted fresh daily with a nutty, smooth profile suiting all coffee types. Warm notes of spice, wine or cocoa and a floral scent, blending Brazilian and Ethiopian beans.

beans.name: #2015 Brazilian | Central America | Ethiopian
beans.listedNotes: Sweetness and acidity, chocolatey and fruity note from mocha coffee
beans.source: A Big O Coffee product page
beans.desc: A classic American-style blend with steady body, rich crema and bright sweetness. Its mocha component adds chocolate and fruit, a strong pick for espresso fans. Brazilian, Central American and Ethiopian beans.

beans.name: #2018 Indian Robusta | Ethiopian | Brazilian
beans.listedNotes: Big body, earthy, nutty tones, smooth
beans.source: A Big O Coffee product page
beans.desc: A blend roasted fresh daily with a strong caffeine kick and gentle, mellow finish. Full-bodied with earthy, nutty notes, good for espresso, lattes and cappuccinos; beans from India, Ethiopia and Brazil.

beans.desc: A natural from Fazenda Santa Catarina in Minas Gerais, Red and Yellow Catuaí at about 1,100 metres. Cocoa depth, nutty sweetness and molasses-like sugar; best as espresso.

beans.name: Vietnam Dalat
beans.producer: Zanya Co-operation (K'ho smallholders), Langbiang plateau, Dalat, 1,500-1,650m; Catimor, Bourbon, Typica, Caturra
beans.processFull: Double washed (36 hour ferment, 24 hour soak)
beans.desc: Arabica from smallholders on Vietnam's Langbiang Plateau near Dalat, double washed in two fermentation stages for clarity. Red apple, black tea and nectarine.

beans.name: Peru La Coipa
beans.producer: La Palma and Los Gentiles farms (Luis Garcia, Noriel Mendoza), La Coipa, Cajamarca, 1,800-1,850m; Typica, Caturra, Bourbon
beans.desc: A washed Peruvian from La Coipa in Cajamarca, grown at 1,800-1,850 metres by Luis García and Noriel Mendoza. Cantaloupe, red grape and maple syrup.

beans.name: Uganda Muki Fruity
beans.desc: Grown by Norman Mukuru at 1,800-2,000 metres in Uganda, with a natural anaerobic fermentation of 36 to 100 hours. Bright papaya and lime with a boozy, liqueur-like edge.

beans.name: Sunset Decaf Brazil
beans.producer: Cerrado, Minas Gerais (Volcafe Brazil, many farms), 900m; Catuai, Mundo Novo
beans.processFull: Natural / pulped natural; ethyl acetate (sugarcane) decaf, done in Bremen
beans.brew: Espresso; black or with milk (19g in, 28g out)
beans.desc: A decaf from Brazil's Cerrado, grown at 900 metres and decaffeinated with sugarcane-derived ethyl acetate. Milk chocolate, pecan and caramel with a dense, sweet body that suits espresso and milk.

beans.name: Half-Caff Blend
beans.desc: A seasonal half-caff of equal parts Brazilian decaf (ethyl acetate) and Peruvian, both washed. Pecan, milk chocolate and golden syrup; for espresso or filter.

beans.name: Decaf Mexico Finca Nueva Linda
beans.producer: Finca Nueva Linda (Juan Jose Moguel Orantes), La Concordia, Chiapas, 1,250-1,550m; Mundo Novo, Catuai, Caturra, Catimor
beans.processFull: Fully washed; decaf method not stated
beans.desc: A decaf from Chiapas, Mexico, next to a biosphere reserve, fully washed, fermented 14-18 hours and dried on patios or solar driers. Careful farming by owners long committed to coffee.

beans.name: Tarrazu
beans.desc: From Costa Rica's Tarrazú at 1,250-1,800 metres, Catuaí and Caturra, washed and drum dried. Crisp bright tang with nutty, spiced notes and a velvety, balanced finish.

beans.name: Brazil Santos
beans.producer: Mogiana, Sul de Minas; many farms, 800-1,350m; Mundo Novo, Icatu, Acacia
beans.desc: A specialty Brazilian dried on patios in the cherry, taking on sugary pulp for a heavy, sweet, smooth, complex cup. Larger beans avoid the sharp fruit notes of uneven ripeness.

beans.name: Haff Caff
beans.processFull: Natural (Santos); Colombian decaf method not stated
beans.desc: A half-caff of equal parts decaffeinated Huila Colombian and natural Brazilian Santos from Mogiana, Sul de Minas and São Paulo farms, grown at similar elevations.

beans.name: Autumn Blend
beans.producer: Brazil Santos 75%, Peru 25% (description); page also lists Nicaragua Sajonia Reserva
beans.listedNotes: Sweet, Caramel, Chocolate, Nutty, Praline, Apricot, Vanilla
beans.desc: An autumn blend of roughly a quarter Peruvian and three-quarters natural Brazilian Santos, with chocolate, nutty praline and apricot.

beans.name: Belfast Blend
beans.producer: Rafiki Mill, Moshi (Kent, Bourbon), 1,450-1,700m 50%; Brazil Santos 50%
beans.desc: A blend of 80% Brazilian Santos and 20% Costa Rican Tarrazu beans; the page also gives background on each origin and its growing region.

beans.name: Christmas Blend
beans.desc: A medium-roast mix of Ethiopian and Brazilian beans with a Christmas flavour, a cinnamon aroma and hints of walnut, chocolate and nutmeg; pitched as a festive gift or stocking filler.

beans.name: Colombian Supremo
beans.producer: Antioquia, many farms, 1,200-2,000m; Caturra, Typica, Bourbon
beans.desc: From a single Colombian region and meant to give a consistent cup: balanced and smooth with fruit, chocolate and caramel, a medium body, lively acidity and a clean finish.

beans.name: Ethiopian Gold
beans.desc: From Sidamo, a high-altitude region south of Addis Ababa with ample rainfall and rich soil; a medium-bodied cup with low acidity and a bright finish.

beans.name: Ipanema Gold
beans.producer: Mogiana, Sul de Minas, near Nova Resende; small producers, 800-1,350m; Mundo Novo, Icatu, Acacia
beans.desc: From Nova Resende in the hills of South Minas, Brazil, at about 1,300m, where small producers pool resources to aim for top quality and support their communities.

beans.name: Monte Cristo Honduras
beans.producer: Monte Cristo Estate (Hacienda Montecristo), Veracruz, Copan, 1,100-1,200m
beans.desc: From the family-run Hacienda Montecristo, known for coffee with balanced body, deep flavour, rich aroma and medium acidity; chocolate and nutty notes with a sweet finish.

beans.name: The Painter
beans.producer: Colombia: Huila (Castillo, Caturra, Colombia), washed. Brazil: San Rafael, Cerrado Mineiro (Catuai, Mundo Novo), natural. Guatemala: Rigel, Volcanic San Marcos, washed
beans.listedNotes: Roasted hazelnuts, Chocolate; with milk: Black forest gateau (dark chocolate, black cherry)
beans.desc: A washed Colombian from Huila, natural Brazilian from Cerrado Mineiro and washed Guatemalan from San Marcos. Black: hazelnut and chocolate; with milk: dark chocolate and black cherry.

beans.name: The Rock
beans.producer: Brazil: San Rafael, Cerrado Mineiro (Catuai, Mundo Novo), natural. Guatemala: Rigel, Volcanic San Marcos, washed. Ethiopia: Salomon, Sidama, washed
beans.listedNotes: Liquorice, Blueberries, Praline; with milk: Creme brulee
beans.desc: Three Arabicas: natural Brazilian from Cerrado plus washed Guatemalan and Ethiopian Sidama. Black: liquorice, blueberry and praline; with milk: crème brûlée.

beans.name: The Lovebirds
beans.producer: Colombia: Huila (Castillo, Caturra, Colombia), washed. Brazil: San Rafael, Cerrado Mineiro (Catuai, Mundo Novo), natural. Mexico: Ara Macau, Oaxaca (Catimar, Catuai), washed
beans.listedNotes: Marzipan, Cinnamon, Plums; with milk: Christmas pudding (dried fruits, dark molasses, warm spices, orange peel)
beans.source: Text pasted by user (Blue Monday product page)
beans.desc: A blend of Colombian, Brazilian and Mexican Arabica beans; the roaster lists marzipan, cinnamon and plums without milk and Christmas pudding with milk.

beans.name: Colombia Golden Huila
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, Caramel, Orange, Red apple, Panela
beans.source: Text pasted by user (Blue Monday product page)

beans.name: Nicaragua Xarisma
beans.producer: Nueva Segovia; family-owned exporter, farm not named
beans.listedNotes: Deep dark chocolate, Red plum, Orange, Citrus acidity, Creamy, Nutty, Floral
beans.desc: A washed single origin from Nueva Segovia, Nicaragua. Dark cocoa with plum and orange behind, gentle citrus brightness and a creamy medium-to-full texture.

beans.name: The Macaw (Decaf)
beans.producer: Chiapas; exporter Chabela, founded 1980; Bourbon, Catimor, Garnica, Typica
beans.listedNotes: Spicy, Cinnamon, Dark chocolate, Citric acidity, Buttery
beans.desc: A mountain-water decaf from Chiapas, Mexico, from an exporter that pioneered decaffeination in Latin America; over 99% of caffeine removed and organic certified since 2003. Warm spice, cinnamon, dark chocolate, citrus and a buttery body.

beans.name: Breasted Roller
beans.producer: Colombia: Huila (Castillo, Caturra, Colombia). Kenya: Ibutiti, Murang'a (SL34, SL28). Mexico: Ara Macau, Oaxaca (Catimor, Catuai)
beans.listedNotes: Orange, Cherries, Maple syrup; with milk: Chocolate mousse (chocolate, vanilla)
beans.desc: A washed blend of Colombian (Huila), Mexican (Oaxaca) and Kenyan (Murang'a) Arabica. Black: citrus orange, cherry and maple; with milk: chocolate and vanilla mousse.

beans.name: Aracari
beans.producer: Colombia: Huila (Castillo, Caturra, Colombia), washed. Brazil: San Rafael, Cerrado Mineiro (Catuai, Mundo Novo), natural. Kenya: Ibutiti, Murang'a (SL34, SL28), washed. Ethiopia: Sidamo, details not given
beans.listedNotes: Spiced apples, Ginger, Cream; with milk: Tiramisu (espresso, cocoa, vanilla)
beans.desc: A blend of Brazil (natural), Colombia and Kenya (washed) and Ethiopia. Black: spiced apple, ginger and cream; with milk it resembles tiramisu with espresso, cocoa and vanilla.

beans.name: Ethiopia Salomon
beans.listedNotes: Peach, Lemon, Caramel, Dark chocolate, Jasmine, Silky body
beans.desc: A washed heirloom single origin from Sidama, Ethiopia. Bright, citrus-led with jasmine florals, ripe peach and caramel sweetness; silky, tea-like body and a clean finish with a touch of dark chocolate.

beans.name: Kenyan Ibutiti
beans.producer: Murang'a; Ibutiti (from product name); SL34, SL28
beans.listedNotes: Blackberry, Blackcurrant, Concord grape, Brown sugar, Baking spices
beans.source: Text pasted by user (Blue Monday product page)

beans.name: Bohemia Roast (100% Arabica Blend)
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, Macadamia nuts, Citrus, Black tea
beans.desc: An all-Arabica blend from India, Nicaragua and Brazil. Chocolate, macadamia, citrus and black tea; suits espresso and filter. The roaster rates its strength 4.

beans.name: Chamundi
beans.listedNotes: Cocoa, Black tea, Fudge, Orange, Berries
beans.desc: An Indian Arabica from Catuaí and Chandragiri varieties with chocolate, black tea, fudge, citrus and berry. Best for espresso and moka pot; strength 5.

beans.name: Santos Sunshine
beans.producer: Santos, 800-1,350m; Mundo Novo, Icatu, Acaia, Catuai, Tupi
beans.desc: A single-origin Brazilian Arabica from Santos, blending several cultivars grown at 800-1,350 metres. Peanut, chocolate and caramel; for cafetière or filter; strength 2.

beans.name: Organic Tinto Parce
beans.desc: An organic Colombian Arabica from Ataco, Tolima, grown at about 1,600 metres from Castillo. Swiss chocolate, butter, florals and nectarine; espresso or filter; strength 4.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf
beans.producer: 1,000m+; Castillo, Caturra, Colombia, Typica (varieties look Colombian)
beans.desc: A Brazilian Swiss Water decaf Arabica of Castillo, Caturra and Typica above 1,000 metres. Green apple, sugarcane and praline; espresso or filter; strength 3.

beans.name: Alto Mist
beans.desc: An organic Arabica with Guatemalan character, roasted in St Neots, from Bourbon, Caturra and Catuaí. Chocolate, cherry, toffee and apple; for cafetière and filter; strength 3.

beans.name: House Espresso
beans.producer: Cerrado and Sul de Minas (many farms, Volcafe Excellence); Mundo Novo, Catuai
beans.desc: The roaster calls it a balanced, everyday classic: a medium-light, natural-processed Brazilian blend of Mundo Novo and Catuai from Cerrado and Sul de Minas, with a rich, comforting cup of hazelnut, caramel and chocolate.

beans.name: Finca La Clarita - Don Hector
beans.producer: Finca La Clarita (Hector Arango), Betulia, Antioquia, 1,630-2,000m; Castillo Rosario, Cenicafe 1
beans.listedNotes: Green apple, Cherry, Winey finish, Vanilla, Strawberry, Hibiscus tea
beans.desc: The roaster's Direct Trade offering, a meticulously crafted light-medium roast; fully washed to show the region's terroir, with a clean, vibrant cup of green apple, cherry and a wine-like finish.

beans.name: Finca Las Laderas
beans.producer: Finca Las Laderas (Lima family), Apaneca-Ilamatepec, Santa Ana; Pacamara
beans.desc: A medium-light roast, honey-processed (dried with the sweet mucilage on) for a rich, vibrant cup with peach, caramel and maple syrup.

beans.name: Rwanda Cyahinda
beans.producer: Nyamasheke, Southern Province, 1,800-2,000m; community lot (600 farmers); Red Bourbon
beans.listedNotes: Baked apple, Strawberry jam, White sugar, Peach, Caramel, Maple syrup
beans.desc: A medium-light, natural-processed community lot of Red Bourbon from 600 farmers in Nyamasheke, grown at 1,800-2,000m; fruity sweetness with baked apple, strawberry jam and white sugar.

beans.name: Happy Capybara (House Decaf)
beans.producer: Cerrado and Minas Gerais; Mundo Novo, Catuai
beans.processFull: Natural and pulped natural; ethyl acetate (sugarcane) decaf
beans.desc: A balanced medium-dark decaf, a Brazilian blend from Cerrado and Minas Gerais decaffeinated by the sugarcane (ethyl acetate) process; praline, marzipan and baker's chocolate.

beans.name: Papua New Guinea (Goroka Valley)
beans.producer: Highlands, 1,500-1,800m, via Bruhouse Coffee; coops and smallholders
beans.desc: From Highland cooperatives and smallholder farms in Papua New Guinea, sourced through Bruhouse and grown at 1,500-1,800 metres. Slow-ripened cherries give a clear, layered medium-roast cup of cocoa, spice and earthy notes.
beans.priceBasis: Listing/metadata price, size not confirmed; product page shows £19.99

beans.name: Uganda Mukuru Natural
beans.producer: Mount Elgon (Sironko, Mbale, Bulambuli, Kapchorwa); Norman Mukuru, The Coffee Yard
beans.desc: Sourced by Norman Mukuru, a Ugandan coffee veteran, from smallholders on Mount Elgon's slopes via his large drying centre. Dried in the fruit as a natural, with ripe berries over a rich toffee sweetness.
beans.priceBasis: Listing/metadata price, size not confirmed; product page shows £19.99

beans.name: Colombia El Silencio Anaerobic Natural
beans.producer: Finca El Silencio (Robinson Rivera Muelas), Piendamo, Cauca, 1,740m; Caturra
beans.desc: Grown by Robinson Rivera Muelas, 38, in Piendamó, Cauca, from Caturra at around 1,740 metres. Two-stage fermentation, first without oxygen then with it. Strawberry, cherry and cooked berries.
beans.priceBasis: Listing/metadata price, size not confirmed; product page shows £19.99

beans.name: Colombia Supremo La Manuela
beans.producer: Tolima per details; description says Caldas near Aranzazu (La Manuela Estate); Caturra, Castillo, Colombia
beans.desc: A Colombian Supremo blended from several farms, washed and medium roasted so it suits any brew method. Full body with chocolate, nut and toffee notes; Caturra, Castillo and Colombia varieties.
beans.priceBasis: Listing/metadata price, size not confirmed; product page shows £19.99

beans.name: Guatemala Antigua Los Volcanes
beans.producer: Details say Huehuetenango, description La Antigua, metadata Baja Verapaz (Finca Bremen); ADESCAFE members; Bourbon, Catuai
beans.desc: A washed Arabica from near La Antigua, Guatemala, at about 1,500 metres, from Bourbon and Catuaí. Medium roasted with layered cocoa and sweet caramel; a dependable everyday coffee.
beans.priceBasis: Listing/metadata price, size not confirmed; product page shows £19.99

beans.name: Peru Huabal
beans.producer: Huabal, Cajamarca, 1,700-2,100m; various farms (Falcon Coffee); Caturra, Typica
beans.listedNotes: Tropical fruit, Caramel, Creamy, Black cherry
beans.desc: Washed coffee from multiple farms in Peru's Huabal area, with varied climates and soils from damp red earth to dry, baked land. Juicy dark cherry, toffee sweetness and a velvety texture.
beans.priceBasis: Listing/metadata price, size not confirmed; product page shows £19.99

beans.name: Brazil Ipanema Reserva
beans.producer: Ipanema Estate, Tres Pontas, Sul de Minas (metadata: Finca Rio Verde); mixed varieties
beans.desc: A Brazilian from the Ipanema estate in Minas Gerais, grown on its smaller Rio Verde plantation and dried with the mucilage intact. Medium roast with gentle acidity, sweetness and nutty, creamy cocoa.
beans.priceBasis: Listing/metadata price, size not confirmed; product page shows £19.99

beans.name: Carnival Espresso
beans.listedNotes: Praline, Milk chocolate, Toffee, Tropical fruit
beans.desc: An espresso blend of Brazilian and Peruvian beans, named for the festive energy of the producing countries. Praline, milk chocolate and a touch of tropical fruit; sweet and smooth, and good without an espresso machine.
beans.priceBasis: Listing/metadata price, size not confirmed; product page shows £19.99

beans.name: Indonesia Mandheling (Fairtrade)
beans.producer: Takengon, Gayo highlands, Aceh, Sumatra; UtamaGro Tani Gayo Cooperative; Catimor, Tim Tim, Abyssinia
beans.desc: A wet-hulled coffee from a cooperative in the Takengon highlands of Aceh, Sumatra. Robust and punchy, for fans of deep roasts, in a French press or as strong espresso.
beans.priceBasis: Listing/metadata price, size not confirmed; product page shows £19.99

beans.name: Decaf Colombia El Buho
beans.desc: A Colombian decaf called El Buho from Huila and Tolima, decaffeinated with sugarcane-derived ethyl acetate and spring water. Notes of chocolate, vanilla and rum.
beans.priceBasis: Listing/metadata price, size not confirmed; product page shows £19.99

beans.name: Tullu Demtu (Ethiopia, Organic)
beans.producer: Meti kebele, Gera, Jimma Zone (Abdo Abamecha), 2,050m; Heirloom
beans.desc: A great organic coffee, perfect with or without milk. Natural-process heirloom grown at about 2,050m in Meti kebele, Jimma Zone, with apricot, caramel and milk chocolate.

beans.name: Dama Da Noite (Brazil)
beans.producer: Southern Minas Gerais, Minasul cooperative reserve program; mixed varieties
beans.desc: A versatile coffee for any time of day, selected from Minasul's reserve programme in Southern Minas Gerais and natural-processed; cherry, raisin, milk chocolate and caramel.

beans.name: Poda (Indonesia)
beans.listedNotes: Smoked pineapple, Orange, Tamarind, Cedar, Dark chocolate
beans.desc: Bosk's first from Indonesia, enjoyed for its delicate flavour. It comes from a project led by Samuel Sihombing in Sidikalang that gives farmers agronomy training and pays above market rate.

beans.name: Nafuna (Uganda)
beans.listedNotes: Orange, Lime, Black tea, Caramel, Milk chocolate
beans.desc: Bosk's first from Uganda: rich and full-bodied, with orange, lime, black tea, caramel and milk chocolate. It comes from The Coffee Gardens, a farm set up in 2017 for ethical specialty coffee with a direct link between farmers and consumers.

beans.name: Kegeyo (Rwanda)
beans.producer: Kageyo washing station and smallholder co-op, 1,800-2,000m; Red Bourbon
beans.desc: A smooth, medium-bodied coffee of fruity berries, lime, cocoa and peach from smallholder farmers at 1,800-2,000m, washed at the Kageyo cooperative station, which won the Rwanda Cup of Excellence in 2011.

beans.name: Bani Al-Nahimie (Yemen)
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry, Peach, Black tea, Bergamot, Milk chocolate
beans.desc: Medium-strength Yemeni Jaadi coffee sourced through Mocha Mill, with strawberry, peach and black tea with bergamot and a smooth milk chocolate body.

beans.name: Beloya, Ethiopia (Limited Edition)
beans.producer: Beloya washing station, Kochere, Gedeo Zone, 1,699-1,719m; Heirloom
beans.listedNotes: Peach, Citrus, Floral; listing: Dried raspberry, Blueberry, Lavender, Chocolate
beans.desc: Grown at altitude around the Beloya station in Ethiopia's Gedeo Zone, dried on raised beds for nearly three weeks. A light-to-medium roast tasting of peach, citrus and sweet florals.
beans.priceBasis: From price, bag size not stated

beans.name: Coffee of the Month: Mexico El Cuarenteno (October)
beans.desc: The October selection: a washed Mexican grown at 900-1,100 metres and lightly roasted to order in Somerset, fully traceable. Almond, apple and caramel.
beans.priceBasis: From price, bag size not stated

beans.name: 'Altitude' Signature Blend
beans.desc: A Somerset-blended mix of Brazil, Guatemala and Ethiopia with a high share of naturals, giving a rich, liqueur-like character. A lighter roast keeps bright acidity and natural sweetness.
beans.priceBasis: From price, bag size not stated

beans.name: 'Campbell Street' Antipodean Blend
beans.desc: A medium-light blend with a Colombian base plus Brazilian and Guatemalan coffees for body and smoothness. Marzipan, cocoa and hazelnut; small-batch roasted, adjusted with new harvests, for filter or espresso.
beans.priceBasis: From price, bag size not stated

beans.name: Mill Town Dark Roast Blend
beans.desc: A dark roast of Brazilian and Colombian beans: sturdy and heavy-bodied with cocoa, treacle and fudge. The recipe shifts with fresh harvests; roasted in small lots in Wellington, Somerset.
beans.priceBasis: From price, bag size not stated

beans.name: Tres Dragones, Colombia
beans.producer: Cafe Granja La Esperanza (Rigoberto and Luis Potosi), Caldas, 1,860m; Colombia cultivar
beans.desc: An award-winning natural Colombian from Café Granja La Esperanza in Caldas at 1,860 metres, lightly roasted. Guava, cocoa and blueberry; the Potosí brothers have farmed organically since the late nineties.
beans.priceBasis: From price, bag size not stated

beans.name: Peruvian Decaf (Swiss Water)
beans.desc: A Peruvian from Cajamarca, washed at the station and decaffeinated with water only by the Swiss Water method. Roasted in Somerset for a smooth, rich cup that tastes like regular coffee.
beans.priceBasis: From price, bag size not stated

beans.name: Honduran Organic
beans.desc: An organic Honduran from Celaque Mountain at around 2,000 metres, from the Capucas Cooperative. Hand-picked, washed in local water and solar-dried, then lightly roasted for peach, hazelnut and cocoa.
beans.priceBasis: From price, bag size not stated

beans.name: Local Blend
beans.listedNotes: Smooth, Balanced, Mild caramelisation, Slightly sweet
beans.desc: An everyday blend with a smooth, well-rounded taste. Gentle caramel with a touch of brightness and a soft, subtly sweet aftertaste.

beans.name: Breakfast Blend
beans.listedNotes: Intense, Bold, Nutty, Smoky, Earthy finish
beans.desc: A strong, lively blend for the first cup of the morning, brewed from dark, glossy beans. Bold with nutty notes and a hint of smokiness.

beans.name: Italian Blend
beans.desc: A deep-coloured, Continental-style cup with cocoa flavours, an earthy aroma and bittersweet hints; smooth and indulgent.

beans.name: Espresso Blend
beans.listedNotes: Roasted nut, Dark cocoa, Forest fruits, Bittersweet finish
beans.desc: An espresso blend of firm, high-grown Peruvian, Colombian and Brazilian Arabica chosen to stand up to a dark roast. Roasted nuts, dark cocoa and forest fruit with a lingering bittersweet finish.

beans.name: Bro House / Sketrick
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Hazelnut, Fruit, Malt, Plum
beans.desc: A bold blend with a rich, full mouthfeel and a grainy fragrance. Malt, cocoa and plum, moderate tang, a lingering nutty finish and vivid dark chocolate, hazelnut and fruit.

beans.name: Bro Plus
beans.desc: A dark-roasted, naturally processed Vietnamese Robusta: potent and weighty with an earthy character that stays surprisingly mellow. Its caffeine punch suits a pre-training or cycling boost.

beans.name: Go Bro / Isle O'Valla
beans.origin: Brazil / El Salvador / Ethiopia / Honduras / India
beans.desc: A popular blend of vanilla, hazelnut and deep Belgian chocolate richness. Balanced enough for hot or iced drinks, from Irish coffee to a chilled latte.

beans.name: Single Bro
beans.desc: A Guatemalan single origin with a silky mouthfeel and crisp finish: dark cocoa, berries and caramel. Grown on volcanic soil in Santa Rosa at height, where cool, long ripening deepens flavour.

beans.name: Co Bro
beans.brew: Filter or espresso (grinds: whole beans, filter, espresso)
beans.desc: A smooth, layered coffee with lively, fruit-forward flavour and a full body, from small two-hectare farms on volcanic soil. Good black or with milk.

beans.name: Phersons
beans.desc: A twist on the roaster's Sketrick blend, roasted differently and lighter to bring out more caramel. Mellow and smooth, with chocolate, fruit and nut notes most noticeable.

beans.name: De Bro Decaf
beans.desc: A decaf recognised with several 2024 awards, with honey and hazelnut notes. Caffeine is drawn out of unroasted beans by soaking in water, relying on gradual diffusion.

beans.name: Darcan
beans.desc: A velvety blend of Brazilian, Colombian and Vietnamese Arabica and Robusta with dark cocoa and stone fruit, given a deeper roast for bold, lively flavours.

beans.name: Costa Rican
beans.desc: A medium-roast Arabica from San Isidro, Costa Rica: balanced with moderate body and layered dark chocolate and molasses.

beans.name: Bro orB
beans.listedNotes: Honey, Hazelnut, Smooth chocolate, Rum, Citrus
beans.desc: A medium roast of Brazilian, Kenyan and Salvadoran Arabica with earthy character and chocolate, rum and citrus. Lighter than the house and Go Bró blends but with the range's silky body.

beans.name: Bro Slow / Boretree
beans.desc: A blend roasted gently over an extended time to show each origin's character: lively, fruit-forward and citrusy with a rich, pleasant texture.

beans.name: Bro Fine and Rare Single Origin
beans.desc: An outstanding Peruvian Arabica with a clearly defined cup: strawberry, cherry and caramel. A gentle light roast brings out the seasonal crop's richness.

beans.name: Bro Fine and Rare Blend
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Orange, Berry jam, Cream
beans.desc: A blend built as a rich, chocolate-tinged citrus treat: juicy orange sweetness first, then soft berry-like fruits, with dark cocoa and creamy notes through the finish.

beans.name: Bro-Jangles Christmas Blend
beans.listedNotes: Orange, Red currant, Nuts, White chocolate
beans.desc: A seasonal blend of Brazil, Guatemala, Ethiopia and Rwanda, roasted light-to-medium. Bright citrus and tart berry, nutty character and a creamy white chocolate finish.

beans.name: Larrost
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Caramel, Granny Smith apple
beans.desc: A contemporary, well-rounded blend with dark chocolate, caramel and light nuttiness. Its Ethiopian component adds vivid green apple tartness and a juicy zing.
beans.priceBasis: 1kg page only; smaller size not checked

beans.name: Jingle Berry Christmas
beans.desc: A festive Kenyan single-origin peaberry, lightly roasted. Tangy blackcurrant and berries softened by brown-sugar-like sweetness.

beans.name: 21 Ten (Roy Ireland Memorial Blend)
beans.producer: Brazil: San Coffee, Minas Gerais. Costa Rica: Coopelibertad SHB
beans.listedNotes: Brazil nut, Vanilla pod, Fruit chocolate
beans.desc: A medium espresso blend honouring the company's late founder, Roy Ireland, mixing Brazilian and Costa Rican beans. Silky and rich with a lingering finish; each pack supports a Bristol hospital charity.

beans.name: Copan-Cabana
beans.producer: Brazil: San Coffee. Honduras: Cafesmo SHG, above 1,350m
beans.listedNotes: Cinnamon, Dark chocolate, Cocoa, Caramel, Toffee, Raisin, Date
beans.desc: The roaster's original and still best-selling espresso blend: 100% Arabica from Brazil and Honduras, medium-dark roasted. Full, rich body, smooth finish, cinnamon hints and dark chocolate; for espresso or filter.

beans.name: Formula 318
beans.producer: Brazil: San Coffee. Costa Rica: Coopelibertad SHG
beans.desc: A medium-roast espresso blend of Brazil (gentle sweetness), Costa Rica (brightness) and Ethiopia (wine-like fruitiness), delicate yet rich.

beans.name: Half Caff
beans.producer: Brazil: San Coffee, Minas Gerais. Honduras decaf component
beans.listedNotes: Brown sugar, Honey, Toffee, Ripe fruit, Nutty
beans.desc: A Brazilian single-origin Arabica blended with a Honduran decaf made with sugarcane-derived ethyl acetate, giving about half the usual caffeine. Cinnamon and dark chocolate with a smooth, low-acid finish.

beans.name: Heritage
beans.producer: Brazil: San Coffee (Yellow Catucai). Guatemala: Conebosque SHB. Small amount of Guinea Robusta
beans.listedNotes: Brazil nut, Chocolate, Citrus, Praline, Caramel, Tangerine
beans.desc: A dark roast made for milky drinks, with Brazil and Guatemala as the base and a little Guinea Robusta. Bold enough to cut through milk, and also good for espresso and americano.

beans.name: Buena Decada
beans.desc: A dark espresso blend of Brazilian, Ethiopian and Salvadoran beans, honouring the company's history while opening a new chapter. Balanced for straight espresso or milk drinks.

beans.name: Colombia La Casiana Estate
beans.producer: La Casiana (Esteban Uriba), Jardin, Antioquia, 1,800m; Castillo, Colombia, Cenicafe 1
beans.listedNotes: Red berries, Orange, Caramel, Milk chocolate, Dark chocolate, Molasses
beans.desc: From a family estate in Antioquia, Colombia, at about 1,800 metres, farmed across three generations. Lively medium acidity, smooth rounded body, dark chocolate, caramel and molasses with a sweet floral finish.

beans.name: Latina
beans.origin: Honduras (plus small amount of washed Robusta)
beans.listedNotes: Creamy chocolate, Sugar cane, Toffee, Cocoa, Lime
beans.desc: An espresso of high-grown Honduran beans with a small share of carefully washed Robusta for a bold, traditional Italian style. Potent, full-bodied, with a velvety sweetness that lingers.

beans.name: Formula 442 (Triple Certified)
beans.producer: El Salvador SHB, Sumatra Mandheling Grade 1, Ethiopia Yirgacheffe; Fairtrade, Organic, Rainforest Alliance
beans.desc: A dark-roast espresso blend of Fairtrade, organic and Rainforest Alliance coffees from El Salvador, Sumatra and Ethiopia, roasted in limited batches to protect flavour.

beans.name: Honduras Sugar Cane Decaf
beans.processFull: Sugar cane (EA) decaf; producer section says fully washed
beans.listedNotes: Cacao, Nutty, Brown sugar, Creamy, Milk chocolate, Caramel
beans.desc: A Honduran decaf made by a sugarcane-derived ethyl acetate method that keeps flavour intact. Balanced cocoa, nut and brown sugar with a silky mouthfeel and crisp sweet ending.

beans.name: La Selva (Rainforest Alliance)
beans.producer: Brazil: San Coffee. Colombia: La Casiana. Honduras: Cafesmo SHG
beans.desc: An espresso blend of Rainforest Alliance certified Arabica from Brazil, Honduras and Colombia. Even and lively, with a rounded finish and warm, fragrant spice.

beans.name: Machu Picchu Swiss Water Decaf
beans.producer: Chanchamayo, 1,200-1,350m; Caturra, Typica, Pache, Bourbon (small producers)
beans.desc: A Peruvian Swiss Water decaf from Chanchamayo, where small growers farm under two hectares in high-altitude shade. Dense, complex beans, small-batch roasted, with pineapple, lemon, lime and pomegranate.

beans.name: Polar Espresso
beans.desc: A festive blend of Colombian, Ethiopian and monsooned Malabar beans with chocolatey, fruity and spicy notes. A cosy, aromatic cup for cold mornings and winter evenings.

beans.name: Ethiopian Yirgacheffe
beans.desc: Ethiopian Yirgacheffe, highly regarded worldwide and in Ethiopia, thought to taste closest to the plant's wild ancestor. A gentle profile with a faint, slightly gamey finish.

beans.name: Finca San Antonio
beans.producer: Finca San Antonio (family farm, since 1890); Sarchimor
beans.processFull: Washed (3 days patio, 12 days African beds)
beans.desc: A washed Sarchimor from a century-old family estate, valued for crispness and liveliness. Removing the fruit before drying lets the bean's own flavours show, with rare berry-like notes and tangy acidity.

beans.name: Guatemala Conebosque
beans.producer: Conebosque co-op, Santa Rosa, 1,485-1,610m; Red and Yellow Catuai, hybrid
beans.desc: A lot combined from smallholders in the Conebosque cooperative in Guatemala. A citrusy, sweet profile of lemon, chocolate, almond and caramel.

beans.name: Guinea Koumalassi
beans.producer: Macenta Beans washing station, Macenta, 600-1,100m; Robusta (canephora)
beans.listedNotes: Black cherry, Brown sugar, Cacao nibs, Dark chocolate, Marzipan, Pecan
beans.desc: From Macenta Beans, a newer washing station in southeastern Guinea aiming to grow some of the world's finest Robusta. Grown among trees near the Ziama Massif in rich soil with heavy rain, with a sweet, complex character.

beans.name: Honduras Reinaldo Mena
beans.producer: Reinaldo Mena (5.5 ha), 1,150-1,220m; Parainema, Paca, Catuai, Lempira, Catimoro
beans.listedNotes: Orange, Tangerine, Cane sugar, Chocolate, Honey, Vanilla
beans.desc: A fresh main-crop Honduran from returning favourite producer Reinaldo Mena, scoring near 83 on cupping. It launches the new Central American season.

beans.name: Costa Rica Libertad Especial Corralillo Los Santos
beans.listedNotes: Green apple, Pear, Tropical fruit, Chocolate, Caramel, Orange, Almond, Hazelnut
beans.desc: A Costa Rican from the Coopelibertad cooperative opening with green apple and pear aroma. Tropical fruit and cocoa, weighty mouthfeel, crisp finish and a bright, velvety character.

beans.name: Tanzania Ngila Estate
beans.producer: Ngila Estate (Vera Stucker), slopes of Ngorongoro, 1,500-1,600m; Kent P2
beans.desc: From a 100-hectare farm founded in 1920 near the Ngorongoro Crater in northern Tanzania. The producer farms eco-consciously, focuses on quality and supports the local community.

beans.name: Papua New Guinea Goroka Valley
beans.producer: Eastern Highlands, Goroka Valley, smallholders; Typica
beans.desc: From the mountainous highlands around Goroka in Papua New Guinea, where volcanic soil, tropical climate and altitude let cherries ripen slowly. Smallholder-grown, giving a balanced, gently acidic cup.

beans.name: Brazil San Coffee Chocolate Recipe
beans.producer: San Coffee co-op (20 farms), Santo Antonio do Amparo, Minas Gerais, 940-1,010m; Mundo Novo, Catuai, Catucai
beans.listedNotes: Peach, Tartaric and citric acidity, Creamy body
beans.desc: A signature San Coffee blend made each year from beans from member farms. Bright but gentle acidity, juicy peach sweetness, a velvety mouthfeel and a sweet, tea-like finish.

beans.name: Sumatra Gayo Natural
beans.producer: Sumatra Permata Gayo co-op, Gayo Highlands, Aceh, 1,300-1,550m; Ateng Super
beans.listedNotes: Nectarine, Stone fruit, Red apple, Berry, Strawberry, Vanilla
beans.desc: An Ateng Super natural from a cooperative founded in 2014 supporting over 1,300 smallholders in the Gayo Highlands, scoring 85.25. Sun-dried, with bright nectarine and stone fruit and a lush, juicy mouthfeel.

beans.name: Uganda Sironko Station
beans.producer: Mountain Harvest, Mount Elgon, 1,600-2,200m; Nyasaland, SL14, SL28
beans.desc: A Ugandan lot supervised by Ibrahim Kiganda and Ruth Chebet, processed at Mountain Harvest's central site below Mount Elgon. Cherries from remote villages get two days of sealed anaerobic fermentation, then sun and shade drying.

beans.name: Formula 442 Filter Sachets (50 x 75g)
beans.producer: El Salvador SHB, Sumatra Mandheling, Ethiopia Yirgacheffe
beans.desc: Filter sachets of the dark-roast Formula 442 blend of Fairtrade, organic and Rainforest Alliance coffees from El Salvador, Sumatra and Ethiopia. Opens with floral berry, ending in smoky treacle and walnut.

beans.desc: A blend of Guatemalan coffee from smallholders in Huehuetenango and Antigua, good as espresso for those who like a rounder Guatemalan. Citrus, brown sugar and milk chocolate with gentle acidity.

beans.desc: An espresso blending two Central and South American coffees, with bittersweet cocoa and toffee and a dense, velvety texture. Shines straight, and steamed milk brings out more depth.

beans.name: Latino Blend

beans.name: Peru Inca Gold
beans.producer: Prosperidad de Chirinos co-op, La Prosperidad, Cajamarca, 1,200-1,900m
beans.listedNotes: Apricot, Toffee apple, Hazelnut, Milk chocolate
beans.desc: A washed Peruvian from the Prosperidad de Chirinos cooperative, founded 1968 with 817 members, a quarter of them women, on about 2,200 hectares in San Ignacio. Apricot, apple, toasted nuts and milk chocolate.

beans.name: Colombia Aztec Gold
beans.producer: Tolima and Huila smallholders, 1,300-2,000m; Castillo, Caturra
beans.listedNotes: Candy apple, Sweet orange, Hazelnut, Marshmallow, Chocolate ganache
beans.desc: Fully washed Colombian from smallholders in well-known regions; cherries are pulped on the farm, fermented, rinsed and dried on raised beds. Candy apple, sweet orange, hazelnut, marshmallow and chocolate ganache.

beans.name: Guatemala Tikal Gold
beans.listedNotes: Apricot, White grape, Praline, Milk chocolate
beans.desc: Ten small growers pooled their best harvests into a larger lot to secure higher prices, with extra income going to farm and wet mill improvements.

beans.name: Decaf Blend
beans.desc: A decaf of washed Latin American beans, rich and balanced for any brew method. Pear, apricot, praline and brioche with a sweet, creamy finish; a trace of caffeine remains.

beans.name: Decaf Colombia
beans.producer: Tolima and Huila smallholders, 1,600-1,750m; Castillo, Caturra, Colombia
beans.desc: A single-origin decaf from many small Colombian farmers, cupped as green samples and decaffeinated in Colombia. Ethyl acetate, a natural solvent from fermented sugar, removes caffeine, followed by low-pressure steaming.

beans.name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe Wubanchi
beans.producer: Aricha Wubanchi washing station, Yirgacheffe, 2,200m; heirloom
beans.listedNotes: Earl Grey, Orange blossom, Candied pecan
beans.desc: A Yirgacheffe from the Aricha Wubanchi washing station at 2,200 metres. Washed, density-sorted and sun-dried 10-12 days on raised African beds; a roastery favourite.

beans.name: Kenya Maasai Gold
beans.producer: Karii wetmill (Mutira co-op), Kiambu, 1,400-1,600m; SL28, Ruiru 11, K7
beans.listedNotes: Cloudy lemonade, Cherry bakewell, Earl Grey
beans.desc: A freshly roasted Kenyan Arabica from small-scale highland farmers, washed at a cooperative mill. Yellow fruit, citrus marmalade and creamy vanilla with a sugary finish and crisp brightness.

beans.name: Mexico Olmec Gold
beans.producer: Santa Maria Ozolotepec, Oaxaca, 1,450-1,650m; Pluma (community lot)
beans.listedNotes: White grape, Raspberry, Golden syrup, Milk chocolate, Nougat
beans.desc: A collective lot from cooperating farming families in Oaxaca's Sierra Sur, washed and fermented under control and dried on patios and rooftops, some on raised beds. Knowledge passes down the generations.

beans.name: Colombia La Providencia Pink Bourbon
beans.producer: La Providencia (Fabian Acevedo), Huila; Pink Bourbon
beans.listedNotes: White grape, Lychee, Bramble fruit, Almond, Golden syrup
beans.desc: From fourth-generation grower Fabian Acevedo at La Providencia, Colombia. White grape, lychee and dark berries with almond and golden syrup; pronounced sweetness and a velvety body.

beans.name: Peru Cusco Pukamocco
beans.listedNotes: Apricot, Flaked almonds, Brown sugar, Milk chocolate, Fudge
beans.desc: From a 40-hectare family farm in Colca, Yanatile, Peru, at about 1,800 metres with cool air and reliable streams. The Quechua name evokes a reddish hill covered by flowering shade trees.

beans.name: Peru Cusco Geisha
beans.producer: La Margarita farm (Solorzano family), Carmen Alto, 1,900m; Geisha
beans.listedNotes: Poached pear, Baked banana, Strawberry jam, Hazelnut, Cinnamon, 85% chocolate
beans.desc: A Peruvian Geisha from Cusco with stewed pear, roasted banana and strawberry preserve, hazelnut, true cinnamon and dark chocolate. Layered sweetness and a velvety, creamy body.

beans.name: Kenya Kiambu Eaagads PB
beans.producer: Eaagads Estate, Kiambu, 1,400-1,600m; Peaberry (Acaia, K7, Ruiru 11, SL28)
beans.listedNotes: Mango coulis, Peach, Blackcurrant, Cardamom, Butterscotch
beans.desc: A Kenyan peaberry from Eaagads in Kiambu, grown high and washed. Rich, velvety sweetness with mango, peach, blackcurrant, cardamom and butterscotch.

beans.name: Between Trees Autumn Coffee
beans.desc: A seasonal blend inspired by early woodland walks as foliage turns amber. Sugared chestnut, deep chocolate and tart wild berries.

beans.name: Guatemala La Esperanza Washed
beans.producer: La Esperanza (Francisco Morales), Huehuetenango, 1,700m; Caturra, Bourbon, Pache, Catuai
beans.listedNotes: Lemon meringue pie, Dried apricot, Black tea, Chocolate hazelnut
beans.desc: A washed Guatemalan from La Esperanza with tangy lemon dessert, dried apricot, black tea and chocolate-hazelnut. Velvety, silky texture.

beans.name: Guatemala La Colina Pacamara
beans.listedNotes: Picpoul de Pinet, Hibiscus, Almond, Golden syrup
beans.desc: A Pacamara grown by Antonio, a demanding variety. Cherries are picked fully ripe and processed the same day, with 32 hours of slow dry fermentation, washing and ten days on a patio.

beans.name: Guatemala La Esperanza Natural
beans.producer: La Esperanza (Francisco Morales), Cipresales, Huehuetenango, 1,700m; Caturra, Bourbon, Pache, Catuai
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry, Hibiscus, Sencha green tea, Fudge brownie
beans.desc: A natural from the La Esperanza estate in Cipresales, run for over four decades by Francisco Morales and his wife, whose family business employs many neighbours.

beans.name: Decaf Mexico
beans.producer: Chiapas smallholders (lot Ki-Saya); Caturra, Costa Rica, Marsellesa, Typica
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, Flapjack, Sweetened condensed milk
beans.desc: A Chiapas, Mexico decaf from small-scale farmers, named Ki-Saya after a Mayan term linking flavour and nature. Decaffeinated by the mountain water method.

beans.name: Mexico Oaxaca Smooth and Steady

beans.desc: A Oaxaca coffee from Mexico's fourth-largest coffee state, where Indigenous smallholders tend heritage Typica and Bourbon under native shade that protects habitat and soil.

beans.name: Mexico Oaxaca Rich and Hearty

beans.name: Colombia Aztec Gold Instant Coffee
beans.desc: A freeze-dried instant from 100% Colombian Arabica with cocoa, golden raisin and sweet honey notes; silky and full, good plain or with milk.

beans.name: Costa Rica Tarrazu San Rafael

beans.desc: A Kenyan Arabica grown high on the Samburu estate in acidic soil. AA is the largest bean-size grade; a blend of SL34 and SL28, mostly harvested in Kirinyaga.

beans.name: Five Cloud
beans.desc: A blend made by growers in Colombia's mountains from Planadas, Tolima, where thousands of small farms grow micro-lots, and roasted in Buxton's hills. Promotes traceability, sustainable growing and profit-sharing with the community.

beans.name: Ethiopia Sidamo Amaro Farm

beans.desc: Strawberry and fig with delicate florals and a creamy, balanced body, exported via Asnakech Thomas, one of Ethiopia's few women exporters, who returned in 2005 to raise quality. Her farm trains growers and supports local youth.

beans.name: Brazilian Swiss Water Decaffeinated

beans.name: Peang Thai

beans.desc: Single-serve bags made from freshly ground 100% Arabica, Rainforest Alliance certified. The bags break down naturally.

beans.name: Coffee in a Bag Decaffeinated
beans.desc: A pack of 100 biodegradable bags of freshly ground, decaffeinated 100% Arabica, Rainforest Alliance certified.

beans.name: Service en Chambre Cafetiere Coffee Bag (100)
beans.desc: Coffee bags that avoid brewing mess, each yielding two cups. Aimed at hotel-room and guest use for a quick, simple, good-tasting cup.

beans.name: Mexican Bean
beans.listedNotes: Cocoa, Almond, Dried fruit, Soft sweet finish
beans.desc: A calm, velvety roast with subtle depth. Chocolate and nut lead, with faint dried fruit adding sweetness to the finish; works for pour-over and espresso.
beans.priceBasis: Page price, size not shown (filters list 227g and 1kg); unconfirmed

beans.name: House Blend
beans.desc: A blend born from a happy accident, mixing leftover Ethiopian and El Salvador beans from roasting. Smooth and well rounded, with biscuit and caramel, a creamy mouthfeel and a faint ashy finish.
beans.priceBasis: Page price, size not shown (filters list 227g and 1kg); unconfirmed

beans.name: Ethiopian Djimma
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Treacle, Roasted hazelnut, Smoky edge
beans.desc: A single-origin Ethiopian espresso with a bold, intense character and smoky undertone. Deep cocoa, molasses sweetness and toasted nuts, powerful yet silky.
beans.priceBasis: Page price, size not shown (filters list 227g and 1kg); unconfirmed

beans.name: El Salvador San Ernesto
beans.desc: A well-rounded filter coffee with deep, earthy character and layered sweetness. Maple and cherry with a soft smoky note; strength 4.
beans.priceBasis: Page price, size not shown (filters list 227g and 1kg); unconfirmed

beans.name: Machu Picchu
beans.producer: Huadquina cooperative, Santa Teresa, Cusco (288 farmers); Organic Fairtrade
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Roasted nuts, Hazelnut, Subtle citrus
beans.brew: Bean-to-cup, espresso, moka, AeroPress, pour over, filter, cafetiere
beans.desc: A Peruvian-style coffee inspired by Machu Picchu and the Andes: hearty and cosy. Dark chocolate, toasted nuts and gentle fruity sweetness with a smooth finish.

beans.name: Mayan Gold
beans.producer: Chiapas, CESMACH cooperative, El Triunfo reserve; Organic Fairtrade
beans.brew: Bean-to-cup, espresso, moka, AeroPress, pour over, filter, cafetiere
beans.desc: From the uplands of southern Mexico, where cloud forests and jungle suit coffee. A mellow, gently sweet cup dominated by caramel with a harmonious aftertaste.

beans.name: Colombia Reserva
beans.desc: From high-altitude farms in Huila, Colombia: sweet milk chocolate, zesty citrus and hints of stone fruit with a silky mouthfeel and crisp, polished finish.

beans.name: Machu Picchu Decaf
beans.producer: Huadquina cooperative, Santa Teresa, Cusco; Fairtrade
beans.desc: A caffeine-free blend, smooth and comforting, with malt-like sweetness, soft cocoa, light tartness and a silky texture. Balanced rather than heavy.

beans.name: House Espresso
beans.desc: An intense espresso of Central and South American Arabica with Robusta. Cocoa and dark chocolate layers; milk brings out a rounded sweetness, so it works as a shot or in milk drinks.

beans.name: Honduras Arabica
beans.desc: A mild, easygoing Honduran Arabica with gentle sweetness: milky chocolate and subtle, mellow nuttiness, a lighter mouthfeel and crisp ending.

beans.name: Arabica Espresso
beans.listedNotes: Dark toffee, Gentle acidity, Velvety body
beans.desc: A silky, naturally sweet Central and South American Arabica blend with solid but not heavy intensity. Deep toffee brightened by a subtle tang; a round body for everyday espresso.

beans.name: Familia Espresso
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Treacle, Caramel, Vanilla, Bright citrus finish
beans.desc: A slow-roasted espresso of high-grade Central and South American Arabica for full, rich body. Caramel and vanilla sweetness, dark chocolate and molasses, a zesty citrus finish and golden crema.

beans.name: House Decaf
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Rounded body, Mellow sweetness
beans.desc: A caffeine-free Peruvian blend: hearty and full-flavoured with dark cocoa, smooth balance and gentle sweetness. Good for espresso or milky drinks.

beans.name: Machu Picchu Instant
beans.desc: An instant coffee from Peru's Andean highlands, full and bold: dark chocolate, toasted hazelnut and a touch of red-berry sweetness, smooth and well rounded.

beans.name: Mayan Gold Instant
beans.desc: An instant coffee from southern Mexico, velvety and full-bodied with caramel undertones. All Arabica, inherently sweet and mellow.

beans.name: Smooth Instant
beans.desc: A Mexican-sourced instant blend, velvety and easygoing with a calm, understated richness and a soft, well-rounded aftertaste.

beans.name: equinox
beans.producer: Hobe Coffee Co, Nyamasheke Hills washing station; Red Bourbon; 1,750-1,900m
beans.desc: Designed to be sweet, balanced and comforting: a natural Red Bourbon from western Rwanda. Milk chocolate base, raisin-like sweetness, a gentle raspberry lift and a clean, well-bodied finish.

beans.name: solstice
beans.producer: Tarrazu; Luis Anastasio Castro, Juanachute micromill; Caturra, Catuai
beans.desc: A bright, juicy but approachable red honey Caturra and Catuaí from Juanachute Micromill, Costa Rica. Milk chocolate sweetness with raspberry, orange and blackcurrant; lively with a tidy finish.

beans.name: J.R. Bourbon Rojo
beans.producer: Huila; John Rodriguez Acevedo, Rio Negro; Bourbon Rojo; 2,000m
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry ice cream, Blackcurrant, Blackberry lollipop, Cherry, Candy-like
beans.desc: Colombia, Huila (producer John Rodriguez Acevedo, Rio Negro farm, Bourbon Rojo, 2,000m, advanced washed). No product-specific description on the roaster's page; it lists origin and process details only (omni roast).

beans.name: La Rosi Ombligon
beans.producer: Huila; Tatiana Pete, La Rosi; Ombligon; 1,700m
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate cherries, Strawberry cake, Apple, Candy-like
beans.desc: Colombia, Huila (producer Tatiana Pete, La Rosi farm, Ombligon, 1,700m, advanced natural). No product-specific description on the roaster's page; it lists origin and process details only (omni roast).

beans.name: La Mandarina
beans.producer: San Ignacio, Cajamarca; Irene Herrera, La Mandarina; Marshell; 2,000m
beans.listedNotes: Dark jams, Fig, Cacao powder, Caramelised brown sugar, Bright, Berry
beans.desc: Peru, San Ignacio (producer Irene Herrera, La Mandarina farm, Marshell, 2,000m, washed). No product-specific description on the roaster's page; it lists origin and process details only (omni roast).

beans.name: El Silencio Ombligon
beans.producer: Huila; Nixon Echeverry and Fernanda Benavides, El Silencio; Ombligon; 2,200m
beans.desc: Colombia, Huila (Nixon Echeverry and Fernanda Benavides, El Silencio farm, Ombligon, 2,200m, advanced washed). No product-specific description on the roaster's page; it lists origin and process details only (omni roast).

beans.name: Guji Shakiso Red Honey
beans.producer: Guji, Shakiso; Kebir Coffee smallholders; local landrace; 2,150m
beans.desc: Produced by Kebir Coffee and smallholders in Shakiso, Ethiopia, at about 2,150 metres. Orange sweetness opens into papaya and pineapple with a honeyed finish; Ethiopian clarity with added body from the red honey process.

beans.name: Kahawa Endelevu Yellow Honey
beans.producer: Githunguri, Kiambu; Steve Mbugua Waruhiu, Kahawa Endelevu; SL28; 1,760m
beans.listedNotes: Sweet stewed berries, Ripe apricot, Juicy, Silky, Lingering finish
beans.desc: A honey-processed Kenyan SL28 with gentle, rich sweetness and a multi-layered character. Soft cooked berries and ripe apricot, with a juicy, fruit-driven cup and smooth, velvety body.

beans.name: Tributos del Ota Lactic
beans.producer: Tarrazu; Jose Enrique Romero Chacon, Finca Don Joaquin; Milenio; 2,500m
beans.listedNotes: Peach, Grape, Green apple, Vanilla, Cacao nibs, Brown sugar
beans.desc: Bright and layered with fruit, centred on sweet peach, with grape and green apple. Eases into vanilla, cacao nibs and brown sugar; rich, creamy and intricate with depth from lactic fermentation.

beans.name: Cafe Ceres
beans.producer: Tarrazu; Alexandra Elizondo Madrigal, El Llano; Catuai, Typica; 1,500m
beans.listedNotes: Blackberry, Mandarin orange, Cashew, Cherry liqueur
beans.desc: Costa Rica, Tarrazu, natural process at 1,500m. No product-specific description on the roaster's page; it lists origin and process details only (omni roast).

beans.name: Simon Brown Sudan Rume
beans.producer: Cajamarca; Simon Brown, Las Etiopes; Wush Wush, Sudan Rume; 1,950-2,050m
beans.desc: Peru, Cajamarca (producer Simon Brown, Las Etiopes farm, Wush Wush and Sudan Rume, 1,950-2,050m, washed anaerobic). No product-specific description on the roaster's page; it lists origin and process details only (omni roast).

beans.name: Kafipamba Heirloom
beans.producer: Pichincha; Jhon Ortiz and Nelly Morales, Kafipamba; Heirloom; 1,345m
beans.listedNotes: Orange, Peach, Prune, Milk chocolate, Honeyed sweetness, Clean finish
beans.desc: A returning roastery favourite: washed heirloom from Finca Kafipamba. Citrusy sweetness and lively acidity, mellow peach and dried plum, then milk chocolate and lingering honey, ending clean and sweet.

beans.name: Winter Blend
beans.producer: Colombia Bolivar (Racafe); Costa Rica El Llano; India (Coffea canephora); Ethiopia Yirgacheffe
beans.listedNotes: Subtle dried fruits, Molasses, Dark chocolate
beans.desc: A winter blend of Colombian, Costa Rican, Indian and Ethiopian coffee, medium-dark with hearty body. Gentle dried fruit, treacle and dark cocoa.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (listing price, 'from' for most); per-size price not shown; sold out

beans.name: Cooling Towers
beans.producer: Colombia Bolivar (Racafe); Costa Rica El Llano (Roberto Mata)
beans.listedNotes: Citrus acidity, Chocolate, Creamy, Rich, Lasting mouthfeel
beans.desc: Roastology's flagship blend, named after a landmark beside the roastery. Balanced medium roast with bright citrus acidity and chocolate; cuts through milk as espresso and works as an evening filter.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (listing price, 'from' for most); per-size price not shown; sold out

beans.name: Supernova
beans.producer: Nova Resende (Vinte); Jinotega (Aldea Global); Copan (Hacienda Montecristo)
beans.listedNotes: Stone fruit, Cocoa, Hazelnut, Chocolate fudge
beans.desc: A decadent, darker-roasted blend with drupe fruits, cacao, toasted nuts and creamy milk chocolate, for a traditional espresso shot or a robust, heavy filter brew.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (listing price, 'from' for most); per-size price not shown; sold out

beans.name: Aviator
beans.producer: Yirgacheffe (Abera Teshome); Jinotega (Aldea Global); Copan (Hacienda Montecristo)
beans.desc: A medium-light blend with delicate flowers and red berries and a sweet, lively finish, with Central American Arabica added for richness. Three stars at the Great Taste Awards.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (listing price, 'from' for most); per-size price not shown; sold out

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf
beans.producer: Racafe producer group; 1,000m; Castillo, Caturra, Colombia, Typica
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, Caramel sweetness, Gentle apple, Lemon acidity
beans.desc: Swiss Water decaf chosen because the water-based method preserves the coffee's character. A 100% Arabica blend with chocolate and caramel sweetness, subtle apple and a bright lemony tang.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (listing price, 'from' for most); per-size price not shown; sold out

beans.name: Colombia
beans.producer: Ciudad Bolivar, Antioquia; Racafe; 1,450-2,300m; Castillo, Catimor, Caturra
beans.desc: A light, graceful Colombian with gentle citrus and wide flavour range for a washed coffee. The premium paid to Racafé growers supports sustainable farming and bean quality.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (listing price, 'from' for most); per-size price not shown; sold out

beans.name: Costa Rica
beans.producer: Tarrazu; El Llano farm (Roberto Mata); 1,550m; Caturra, Catuai
beans.listedNotes: Good acidity, Liquorice, Tangy aroma, Full-bodied
beans.desc: A Costa Rican blend of Caturra and Catuaí roasted medium. Bright acidity, liquorice-like flavours and a zesty aroma with a rich, heavy mouthfeel.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (listing price, 'from' for most); per-size price not shown; sold out

beans.name: Sumatra
beans.producer: Dolok Sanggul, North Sumatra; PT Musfaha Niaga Mandiri; 1,300-1,500m; Ateng Super, Catimor, Bourbon
beans.listedNotes: Deep chocolate, Herbal, Earthy, Peppery, Spicy body, Creamy mild acidity
beans.desc: Ateng Super, Catimor and Bourbon in a full-bodied, medium-dark roast showing traditional wet-hulled processing. Sweet depth, chocolate, herbal and earthy undertones, peppery spice and gentle creamy acidity.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (listing price, 'from' for most); per-size price not shown; sold out

beans.name: Miscela Special
beans.listedNotes: Strong, Smooth, Rich crema (no flavour notes)
beans.desc: A house favourite made only from Robusta beans from three estates, blended to recreate a traditional Italian espresso: rich thick crema, lingering aroma and a bold yet mellow flavour. Supplied in airtight valved packaging.

beans.name: Miscela Silver
beans.desc: A taste of northern Italian character with a higher share of Arabica for a mellow, easy finish. Beans come in one-kilogram bags, and ground orders are milled fresh; suits espresso, cappuccino, latte and cafetière.

beans.name: Miscela Selezionata
beans.listedNotes: Smooth, Refined, Complex aroma (no flavour notes)
beans.desc: A signature blend with a velvety, polished cup and layered aromas. Mostly Arabica for a northern Italian feel, with a little Robusta for a Sicilian touch. Works as espresso or filter; intensity 3.8/5.

beans.name: Espresso Bar
beans.desc: A blend of Central American and Asian beans, giving a rich, strong flavour and aroma with the character of coffee roasted in southern Italy and Sicily.

beans.name: Bianco Blend
beans.desc: Bianco is a subtle, fragrant blend best brewed in a drip filter or French press. Sold pre-ground in 250g packaging; one of two blends the roaster launched in 2016.

beans.name: The Prudhoe Blend
beans.desc: A blend honouring the roaster's roots in Prudhoe, where its first café opened in 2013. The tin shows local landmarks; each 250g tin holds the Silver blend, roasted in Caltanissetta, Italy.

beans.name: The Blyth Blend
beans.desc: A blend marking the roaster's busy seafront shop in Blyth, Northumberland, with a tin showing the town's beach huts. Each 250g tin holds the Silver blend, roasted in Italy.

beans.name: The Pilgrim Blend
beans.desc: A blend marking the roaster's city-centre shop on Pilgrim Street, Newcastle, with a tin showing the skyline and Tyne Bridge. Aims to bring a touch of Sicilian warmth.

beans.name: Super Crema
beans.producer: Honduras SHG; Mysore Plantation A; Mocha Sidamo; Uganda Screen 18 Robusta
beans.listedNotes: Sweet, Nutty, Marzipan, Vanilla, Dark berry, Earthy
beans.desc: An award-winning top seller, a medium roast of Honduran, Indian and Ethiopian beans with a robust Ugandan Robusta. Balanced, for milk-based drinks and short espressos.

beans.name: Supremo Espresso
beans.producer: Cooxupe (Minas Gerais); La Central SHG; Vietnam WP GR1 Robusta
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, Nut, Citric brightness, Milk chocolate body, Low acidity
beans.desc: An espresso blend with rich chocolate and nutty notes, heavy mouthfeel and little sharpness. Mellow enough for lattes, cappuccinos and flat whites.

beans.name: Triple Certified Grand Cru
beans.producer: Aceh Java (PPKGO); Cauca (COSURCA); La Central; Fairtrade
beans.desc: A blend of smoky Indonesian Java, floral Colombian and milder Honduran beans, carrying three ethical certifications — the roaster's most ethical offering. Nutty and spicy; good as espresso.

beans.name: Elly
beans.origin: Brazil / Colombia / Costa Rica / Guatemala / Uganda (Robusta)
beans.processFull: Pulped natural (Brazil); washed (Colombia, Costa Rica, Guatemala); natural (Uganda)
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, Toffee, Hazelnut, Sugared almond, Fruity finish, Biscuit, Milk chocolate
beans.desc: A versatile blend of Brazilian Arabica with other Central and South American Arabicas, plus Robusta for depth. Fruity and slightly tart with a velvety cocoa finish; for espresso and milky drinks.

beans.name: Primo
beans.origin: Brazil / Colombia / Indonesia / Ethiopia / India / Uganda (Robusta)
beans.producer: Six components incl. Sumatra Blue Lintong, Mysore Plantation A
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, Cream, Hazelnut, Subtle citrus, Cocoa
beans.desc: A worldwide espresso blend where zesty South American notes fade into a deep cocoa finish from Indonesian and Ethiopian coffees. An adaptable, reliable all-purpose espresso for cafés.

beans.name: Espresso Milanese
beans.producer: Santos; La Central SHG; Djimmah; Screen 18
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, Spice, Nutty, Malty, Smoky fruit
beans.desc: An archetypal Italian-style Milanese espresso, deeply roasted with rich mouthfeel. Smooth, with cocoa and a touch of warmth; suits intense solo shots and creamy milk drinks.

beans.name: Fairtrade Espresso
beans.producer: COSURCA (Cauca); Cafe Libertad Flamingo SHB; shade grown; Fairtrade
beans.listedNotes: Soft toffee, Sugared almond, Caramel, Hazelnut, Slight fruitiness
beans.desc: A Fairtrade espresso of Colombian beans with high-altitude Costa Rican Arabica: mildly sweet, fruit-tinged and nutty. Works as a concentrated shot or in milk drinks such as flat whites.

beans.name: Fairtrade Organic Java
beans.producer: PPKGO cooperative, Aceh, Sumatra (Blue Lintong); shade grown; Fairtrade and organic
beans.listedNotes: Smoke, Spice, Liquorice, Earthy, Dark red-wine fruit
beans.desc: Organically grown, Fairtrade coffee from a group of farmers in Aceh, Sumatra. A hearty, striking cup with smoky, peppery notes, some earthiness and rich wine-like fruitiness.

beans.name: Fairtrade Creme Supreme
beans.listedNotes: Malty, Walnut, Peanut, Hazelnut, Full body
beans.desc: A Fairtrade blend of Brazilian and Tanzanian beans roasted dark for a balanced espresso with hazelnut and walnut. Sweetness comes out with milk, so it suits flat whites and cappuccinos.

beans.name: Latin American Decaffeinated
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, Biscuit, Balanced fruity acidity, Sweet
beans.desc: A medium-roast decaf from high-altitude Colombia, Nicaragua and Brazil with gentle sweetness and fruity brightness. Toffee and cookie notes appear especially with milk; pack shots slightly firmer.

beans.name: Fairtrade Decaffeinated Espresso
beans.listedNotes: Brown sugar, Caramel, Biscuit with milk, Fruity acidity
beans.desc: A light-roast decaf from Brazil and Colombia: a mellow, sweet espresso with caramel, brown sugar, biscuit and gentle fruity brightness, good solo or in a flat white.

beans.name: Lavazza Super Crema
beans.listedNotes: Honey, Almond, Nut, Dried fruit, Velvety, Creamy
beans.desc: A classic Italian-style Lavazza blend of premium Arabica and Robusta. Medium roast with a silky, creamy texture and a honey-and-almond aroma; as espresso, mild with nut, honey and dried fruit.

beans.name: Boxha Blend
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, Toast, Vanilla, Floral aroma, Silky, Clean finish
beans.brew: Aeropress, cafetiere, espresso, pour over, stovetop
beans.desc: A blend of Brazilian and Honduran beans giving a velvety, easygoing cup with vanilla and caramel and a crisp ending. The Honduran portion adds fullness and balance, making an excellent espresso.

beans.name: Ban be Blend
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Toast, Spicy aroma, Full body
beans.desc: A bold, high-caffeine blend of Arabica and Robusta for lovers of deep, dark espresso. The Robusta is grown in Vietnam's Lâm Đồng area.

beans.name: Single Origin Colombian
beans.listedNotes: Almond, Caramel, Syrupy sweetness, Earthy aroma, Low acidity
beans.desc: A single-origin Colombian for connoisseurs, with thick, syrupy sweetness, nutty flavours and earthy, rustic aromas. Layered, gentle on acidity and long-lasting.

beans.name: Mexican Decaf
beans.brew: Aeropress, cafetiere, espresso, pour over, stovetop
beans.desc: A Mexican decaf at a medium roast suited to many brew methods. Caffeine is removed with spring water only, no chemicals, and the water can later be reused for irrigation.

beans.name: Guilty Pleasure
beans.producer: Santa Barbara small farms; Benjamin Paz (Honduras Cup of Excellence 2024)
beans.desc: A blend built for a consistent profile even as its components change: rich chocolate and caramel with a weighty, sweet mouthfeel and hints of citrus. Holds up in milk and shines as espresso.

beans.name: Sweetdrop (Brazil)
beans.producer: Cerrado; Tereza Cristina; CARPEC co-op; Red Catuai, IAC-99
beans.desc: A dependable blend for bold, smooth cups that stand up to milk, leaning on body over acidity. Cocoa richness and caramel sweetness; the producers may change but the goal stays the same.

beans.name: Decaf
beans.desc: The latest decaf from smallholder growers, silky and mellow for filter or espresso, sourced via Langdon Coffee Merchants, as is Guilty Pleasure. Rotated every few months, so taste may change.

beans.name: Niguse Jilo
beans.producer: Yirgacheffe, Halo Bariti; Niguse Jilo; Kurume; 2,150m
beans.desc: A natural Yirgacheffe with a gentle, flowery character and candy-like sweetness of watermelon and raspberry. A good example of Ethiopian natural processing.

beans.name: Negash Aberago
beans.producer: Gomma, Jimma; Oma Funtule; Negash Aberago; about 2,100m
beans.desc: A sweet, flower-forward washed Ethiopian from Negash Aberago, offered for a second year. Mild acidity, delicate florals and a lively, juicy character.

beans.name: Pedro Moreno
beans.producer: Santa Barbara above Lake Yojoa; Don Pedro Moreno
beans.desc: A lot from Don Pedro Moreno, an early specialty pioneer in Santa Bárbara, Honduras. At 94 he began growing quality coffee before the area was famous and has taught his family the craft over six decades.

beans.name: Cordillera Del Fuego
beans.producer: Piedades Sur, San Ramon, Alajuela; Cordillera del Fuego SA; Catuai, Caturra; 1,275-1,350m
beans.desc: An autumn favourite returning after its debut at the Belfast Coffee Festival. A cosy, flavourful cup with cinnamon, cooked apple and vanilla.

beans.name: Catarina Ramirez Mendez
beans.desc: From Catarina Ramírez Méndez, a first-generation grower in Huehuetenango who built Finca Gomez into a 4.3-hectare estate. Caturra and Bourbon under shade, dry-fermented and sun-dried on site.

beans.name: Primavera Sisterhood
beans.desc: A returning Guatemalan sourced for years through Primavera Green Coffee and grown by women producers. A soothing cup with creamy cocoa and bright berry notes.

beans.name: Migoti Hill
beans.producer: Mutambu Commune, Bujumbura Rural; Migoti washing station; 173 smallholders; Red Bourbon
beans.listedNotes: Black tea, Brown sugar, Green apple
beans.desc: A coffee from the people behind Mutambu Commune, sourced via Migoti Hill, which the roaster buys from every year for crispness and sweetness. Tea-like black notes, tart green apple and dried fruit.

beans.name: Nola Wonga
beans.producer: Bajawa, Flores, East Nusa Tenggara; Nola Wonga Farmers Group
beans.desc: One of two coffees this year from the Nola Wonga farmers group in Indonesia. This washed version is sweet and lively with elderflower, pomelo and agave; a natural version is fruitier.

beans.name: Wilder Lazo
beans.desc: The second coffee from Wilder Lazo, whom the roaster calls one of Colombia's most innovative producers; a limited release in its Wonder Series that may be rested up to three weeks after roasting because supply is limited.

beans.name: Eucalyptus Co-Fermentation
beans.producer: Turrialba; Aquiares Estate (Robelo family); F1 Hybrid
beans.desc: From Aquiares Estate, a long-time favourite of the roaster, this eucalyptus-fermented lot has gentle floral notes of eucalyptus and candied sage with lemon-like acidity. Limited supply; may rest up to three weeks after roasting.

beans.name: Pot Luck Coffee
beans.desc: A mystery bag from the current range at a reduced price: a coffee roasted in the two months before dispatch with no choice of variety, possibly an unreleased test roast or a pricier coffee. Bags may arrive unlabelled or misprinted, but the roaster promises to share what's inside.

beans.name: Brazilian Sunrise
beans.producer: Page also says pure Cerrado blend (conflict)
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, Nutty, Fruity aftertaste, Light acidity, Sweet, Full body
beans.source: Cairngorm Leaf and Bean product page
beans.desc: A Brazilian blend using only Cerrado beans: chocolatey, nutty notes with a fruity finish, gentle acidity, natural sweetness and a rich, weighty mouthfeel.
beans.priceBasis: Low end of listing range, likely 250g; unconfirmed

beans.name: The Backyard Bothy Blend
beans.producer: Sumatran Mandheling, Indian Monsoon Malabar, Brazilian Ipanema Topazio
beans.listedNotes: Earthy sweetness, Creamy molasses, Dark chocolate aftertaste
beans.source: Cairngorm Leaf and Bean product page
beans.desc: Blended at the roastery, The Coffee Bothy in Boat of Garten, from gently roasted Sumatran, Indian and Brazilian beans. Balanced earthy sweetness, creamy molasses and a lingering dark chocolate finish.
beans.priceBasis: Low end of listing range, likely 250g; unconfirmed

beans.name: Cafe Blend
beans.source: Cairngorm Leaf and Bean product page
beans.desc: A smooth, full-bodied South American blend of Mexican and Brazilian beans with vanilla, caramel and roasted nut. Whole bean or ground; best brewed within three months of roasting.
beans.priceBasis: Low end of listing range, likely 250g; unconfirmed

beans.name: Dava Blend
beans.source: Cairngorm Leaf and Bean product page
beans.desc: Recommended for cafetière or filter, lightly roasted for a silky texture, rich mouthfeel and a very appealing aroma.
beans.priceBasis: Low end of listing range, likely 250g; unconfirmed

beans.name: Peru Washed SHB
beans.listedNotes: Almond, Citrus, Sweet biscuit, Light milk chocolate
beans.source: Cairngorm Leaf and Bean product page
beans.desc: A lively yet balanced Peruvian that is silky and easy to sip: mild citrus, gentle sweetness and a faint milk chocolate finish. Fully washed, grown high in the Andes for a dense bean.
beans.priceBasis: Low end of listing range, likely 250g; unconfirmed

beans.name: Sumatra Mandheling
beans.listedNotes: Herbal, Chocolate, Earthy, Woody, Spicy, Cedar, Sweet tobacco
beans.source: Cairngorm Leaf and Bean product page
beans.desc: A Sumatran made by removing the parchment while beans hold about half their moisture. Full-bodied, herbal and spicy, with cedar, chocolate and spice and wine-like brightness.
beans.priceBasis: Low end of listing range, likely 250g; unconfirmed

beans.name: Colombia Excelso
beans.producer: High-altitude farms 1,400-2,000m; page table says Apaneca, Auchapan (El Salvador)
beans.source: Cairngorm Leaf and Bean product page
beans.desc: A smooth, full-bodied Colombian Excelso, grown high and washed. Milk chocolate and caramel with a subtle citrus lift, gentle sweetness and a crisp finish.
beans.priceBasis: Low end of listing range, likely 250g; unconfirmed

beans.name: Mountain Water Wash Decaf
beans.source: Cairngorm Leaf and Bean product page
beans.desc: The roaster believes decaf drinkers still want flavour, so this Colombian is decaffeinated by the Mountain Water Process. Whole bean or ground; best around ninety days after roasting.
beans.priceBasis: Low end of listing range, likely 250g; unconfirmed

beans.name: Kenya Kamavindi Geisha (Washed)
beans.desc: A rare washed Geisha from producer Peter Mbature in Embu County, Kenya, with light citrus and tea-like notes, honey sweetness and a subtle floral close.

beans.name: Panama Sophia FS15525 Geisha (Natural)
beans.producer: Finca Sophia, Nueva Suiza, Volcan; Willem Boot, David Pohl, Kelly Hartmann; Geisha; 1,900-2,200m
beans.listedNotes: Red grapes, Blood orange, Blackberry, Jasmine
beans.desc: A natural Geisha grown high on Finca Sophia by Willem Boot, David Pohl and Kelly Hartmann. Crimson grape and blood orange with sweet blackberry and a jasmine finish.

beans.name: Kenya Gatura x Kamavindi Lab SL28 & SL34
beans.desc: Exclusive to Calico, developed with Kamavindi Lab. Double-fermentation washed, bringing out Nyeri's brightness with blackcurrant, plum, ginger tea and a sweet prune finish.

beans.name: Ethiopia Demelash K72 Experimental Double Washed
beans.desc: Washed with running water for a cleaner cup, in the K72 style: three days of fermentation with cool water swapped in on night two, then over two weeks drying. Floral, bergamot, blueberry and orange.

beans.name: Ethiopia Luna Hambella 72hr Anaerobic Natural
beans.producer: Buku, Hambela, Guji; Demelash (with Hansun Coffee, Red Tenth Project); 74158; 2,450m
beans.desc: A micro-lot from award-winning producer Demelash with Hansun Coffee: only fully ripe cherries, chilled, fermented three days in sealed tanks and dried over three weeks on shaded beds for layered, clear flavour.

beans.name: Kenya Tatu Estate AA (Calico Lot)
