beans.producer: Tatu Estate, Kiambu; SL28, SL34, Batian, K7; 1,570-1,700m; Rainforest Alliance
beans.desc: The roaster calls it a classic expression of Kenyan coffee, grown at 1,570-1,700m in red volcanic soil in Kiambu County; a clean, lively cup with bright acidity, juicy blackcurrant, lemon, rosehip and lasting honey sweetness.

beans.name: Ethiopia Gotiti Honey Moon
beans.desc: From Gotiti Cooperative, a producer of premium cherries using refined traditional washed and natural methods said to preserve the region's terroir; the roaster recommends resting the beans roughly 10 days to two months.

beans.name: Kenya Thunguri (Natural)
beans.desc: Natural coffees are rare in Kenya, where producers favour washed processing for crisp acidity. This natural pairs Kenya's brightness with deep fruit sweetness and sugary notes.

beans.name: China Yunlan Estate Purple Leaf Typica
beans.producer: Yunlan Estate, Xishuangbanna; Purple Leaf Typica; 1,800m
beans.listedNotes: Red plum, Rooibos, Dried pineapple, Berries
beans.desc: A Purple Leaf Typica from Yunlan Estate in Xishuangbanna, China, grown high and dried in the cherry. Red plum and dried pineapple with a warm tea-like touch and a sweet berry finish.

beans.name: BOP 2026 Panama Feryen Estate SL28 Natural VAR-04
beans.producer: Feryen Estate, Boquete; SL28; Best of Panama 2026 lot VAR-04
beans.listedNotes: Black cherry, Dried dates, Tropical fruit, Floral, Mango, Passionfruit, Raspberry, Peach
beans.desc: A natural SL28 from a family farm in Boquete, Panama, from the Best of Panama 2026 auction. Dark cherry, dried dates, tropical fruit and soft florals; rich sweetness and a juicy body.

beans.name: Panama Finca Feryen Estate Geisha (Washed) 2026
beans.desc: A washed Geisha from Finca Feryen in Volcancito, Boquete, grown at 1,600 metres, sold as 60g of whole beans. Citrus, stone fruit, sweet honey and jasmine.

beans.name: DECAF Colombia Jairo Arcila
beans.producer: Quindio; Santa Monica; Jairo Arcila; Caturra; 1,450-1,500m
beans.processFull: Honey + co-ferment (72h anaerobic with strawberries and grapes); sugarcane EA decaf (Descafecol)
beans.desc: A decaf from Jairo Arcila in Quindío, Colombia. Cherries fermented three days with fresh strawberries and grapes, then dried with some sticky fruit residue on the beans for added sweetness and depth.
beans.priceBasis: 250g; shown sold out when checked (roastery on break until 17 Nov)

beans.name: DECAF Colombia Zarza
beans.producer: Huila; Bella Vista, Zarza Coffee (Jhonatan Gasca); Pacamara; 1,800m
beans.roastNote: Lighter than their usual decaf (not graded)
beans.listedNotes: Floral, Rose, Ripe fruit, Chocolate finish, Syrupy body
beans.desc: A daring decaf from a celebrated family farm in Huila. Blossom and rose aromas give way to riper fruit, finishing with lingering cocoa and syrupy sweetness. Roasted lighter than usual but developed enough to stay harmonious.
beans.priceBasis: 250g; shown sold out when checked (roastery on break until 17 Nov)

beans.name: DECAF Peru Las Damas
beans.producer: Cajamarca; Las Damas group, COOPAFSI cooperative; Bourbon, Caturra, others; 1,100-2,000m
beans.desc: A decaf from the COOPAFSI co-op, grown by women producers in northern Peru's highlands, hand-picked and natural. Decaffeinated in Canada with water only, leaving it almost caffeine-free.
beans.priceBasis: 250g; shown sold out when checked (roastery on break until 17 Nov)

beans.name: LOW CAF Brazil Daterra TB13
beans.listedNotes: Blueberry, Citrus, Sparkling acidity, Herbal and mint as it cools
beans.desc: A low-caf micro-lot from Daterra, which spent over ten years refining the difficult Laurina variety. Cryo-fermented at about 5°C, with blueberry aroma, citrus, lively acidity and minty, herbal notes as it cools.

beans.name: LOW CAF South Sudan Equatoria
beans.producer: Nzara, Western Equatoria; Equatoria Coffee; Excelsa; 600m
beans.listedNotes: Sweet, Nutty, Smooth, Wild character, Low acidity
beans.desc: A low-caf Excelsa native to South Sudan with its own personality: gentle and rounded, little sharpness, pleasant nuttiness and layered depth.
beans.priceBasis: 250g; shown sold out when checked (roastery on break until 17 Nov)

beans.name: HALF CAF Pretty Much Peru Christmas Blend
beans.producer: 50% decaf Peru Las Damas; 35% Peru Roiber Becerra (Finca Morales); 15% Colombia Luz Helena (Quindio)
beans.processFull: Washed + Swiss Water decaf (Las Damas); washed (Becerra); natural (Luz Helena)
beans.listedNotes: Sweet, Fruity, Dried fruit, Chocolate, Dark fruit, Floral
beans.desc: A holiday blend of two Peruvian coffees plus a special addition for a naturally sweet, fruit-forward cup, designed as a gentle Boxing Day lift.
beans.priceBasis: 250g; shown sold out when checked (roastery on break until 17 Nov)

beans.name: HALF CAF CALM Darker Blend
beans.producer: 50% decaf Peru Las Damas (COOPAFSI); 50% Brazil Fazenda Palmital (Catuai, Mundo Novo)
beans.processFull: Washed + Swiss Water decaf (Peru); pulped natural (Brazil)
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, Nutty, Stone fruit, Smooth, Full body, Low acidity
beans.desc: A darker-roasted half-caff with a hearty, weighty texture and gentle acidity. Brazilian beans bring cocoa and nutty undertones; the decaf Peruvian adds depth and a hint of stone fruit.
beans.priceBasis: 250g; shown sold out when checked (roastery on break until 17 Nov)

beans.name: Kenya Kiangothe
beans.producer: Kirinyaga; Kabare Farmers Cooperative, Kiangothe washing station; SL28, SL34, Ruiru 11, Batian; 1,700m
beans.desc: A washed Kenyan from a station on Mount Kenya's southern flanks, with mineral-rich soil and high elevation. Only ripe cherries are accepted, giving a juicy, straightforward cup for pour-over or espresso.
beans.priceBasis: 250g; shown sold out when checked (roastery on break until 17 Nov)

beans.name: Brazil Patricia Coelho
beans.producer: Mogiana; Santo Antonio; Patricia Coelho; Obata; 1,050-1,300m
beans.desc: A natural Brazilian from Patricia Coelho's family property in the Mogiana hills. A traditional profile: sugary and cocoa-toned, with soft cherry-like fruitiness brought out by drying.
beans.priceBasis: 250g; shown sold out when checked (roastery on break until 17 Nov)

beans.name: Fortis Green
beans.desc: Fortis Green suits drinkers who like a well-rounded, sweet, fairly classic brew. The recipe changes with each season's crop, choosing parts to balance sweetness, fullness, tartness and silkiness.

beans.name: Decaf de Cana
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, Pomegranate molasses, Candied pecan
beans.desc: A Huila, Colombia decaf offered for the eighth year. Rich, velvety body with milk chocolate, syrupy pomegranate sweetness and a lasting candied pecan finish.

beans.name: Evanete Peres
beans.producer: Cerrado Mineiro; Paraiso Estate (Evanete Peres Domingues); Mundo Novo; 958m
beans.desc: Returning for a fourth year from Evanete Peres, keeping the sweetness and smooth chocolatey richness fans love. This harvest shifts from tropical fruit to dark berries led by blackberry, with light acidity and a walnut finish.

beans.name: Barrinha
beans.producer: Mogiana; Fazenda Barrinha (Costa family); Mundo Novo; 850-1,100m
beans.desc: This year's Barrinha is a smooth, well-balanced cup with sweet, nutty notes, gentle dried-fruit acidity and a moreish biscuit-like sweetness.

beans.name: Santa Elisa
beans.listedNotes: Red apple, Plum, Caramel, Butter, Vanilla, Pecan
beans.desc: Returning for a third year, a single-variety H1 from Santa Elisa in Acatenango, Guatemala. Juicy plum and orchard fruit, buttery vanilla-like sweetness and a caramel finish with hints of pecan.

beans.name: Gundikhan Lot 3
beans.producer: Chikmagalur, Karnataka; Gundikhan Estate (Saif Ulla); Chandragiri; 1,300-1,400m
beans.desc: A lot the roasters say stands apart yet fits right in. Rich, sweet raspberry jam with juicy brightness and lively acidity, a buttery texture and a lingering biscuit finish.

beans.name: Lalesa (Black Honey)
beans.producer: Gedeb; Lalesa washing station (Ephtah Specialty Coffee); heirloom
beans.desc: A black honey lot from the Lalesa washing station in Ethiopia: sweet and layered with ripe blackberry, tropical sweetness, fragrant purple blossoms and a floral finish.

beans.name: Lalesa (Natural)
beans.listedNotes: Grilled nectarine, Wild strawberry, Milk chocolate
beans.desc: A natural Ethiopian from Lalesa, the last of that station's harvest. Sweeter and richer than many naturals, with cooked stone fruit, deep strawberry and smooth milk chocolate.

beans.name: Nguguini AA
beans.producer: Karatina, Kirinyaga; Nguguini Factory (Kibirigwi FCS); SL28, SL34, Ruiru 11; 1,700m
beans.desc: One of four Kenyans this season, balanced and refreshing: tangy lemon, light airy sweetness, ripe raspberry and a lingering green tea finish. The roastery's most intriguing Kenyan yet.

beans.name: La Chumeca 777
beans.priceBasis: Listing price, size not shown (likely 250g); unconfirmed

beans.name: Jorge Mira
beans.producer: El Jaragual, Amalfi, Antioquia; Jorge Mira; Caturra; 1,500m
beans.listedNotes: Passionfruit, Verbena, Buttermilk, Lemon zest, Mint, Tangerine
beans.desc: The fourth collaboration with Mi Café and Jorge Mira, a second release of this Caturra. Passionfruit leads, with a silky body, lemon zest and hints of mint and tangerine, without harsh acidity.

beans.name: Haru
beans.producer: Yirgacheffe; Hafursa Haru washing station; heirloom; about 2,000m
beans.desc: A washed Yirgacheffe the roaster sees as a highlight of a strong Ethiopian season. Layered and lively, with tart-sweet apricot and peach and a jasmine-like floral lift.

beans.name: The Cafe 89
beans.producer: La Frailesca, Chiapas; The Cafe 89 women producers cooperative (Jaltenango de la Paz); Typica, Penasco, Bourbon, Geisha
beans.desc: An easy-drinking, widely appealing organic Mexican, layered but soft and gentle. Sugared nuts and dried fruit lead; a comforting cup for a chilly autumn day.

beans.name: Type 25 Blend
beans.listedNotes: Seville orange, Dark chocolate, Hazelnut, Molasses
beans.desc: An award-winning favourite that works as espresso or filter, with or without milk, and popular with wholesale customers. Marmalade, dark chocolate and molasses; milk brings out caramel and milk chocolate.

beans.name: Type 6.1 Blend
beans.desc: A blend praised by Great Taste 2025 judges for an inviting aroma of orchard fruit with buttery, bready notes. Vivid and lush with crisp acidity; as espresso tangy and fruity, like Granny Smith apples.

beans.name: Type 5 Blend
beans.desc: A popular blend with bold, rich body and good balance. Cherry first, then dark chocolate that softens with milk, like a fudgy cherry brownie.

beans.name: Brazil (Swiss Water) Decaf
beans.desc: A naturally decaffeinated Brazilian, full-bodied with honey, caramel, dark cocoa and treacle. Works as espresso or slow French press for a silky, satisfying cup.

beans.name: Colombia
beans.producer: Racafe blend from Antioquia and Huila
beans.desc: A Colombian blend balancing gentle brightness and depth: green apple and orange preserve, then creamy caramel and toffee. For espresso, cold brew or filter; smoother and rounder with milk.

beans.name: Sumatra Mandheling
beans.producer: Koperasi Buana Mandiri; Catimor, Gayo 1, Timtim; 1,350m
beans.desc: A full-bodied single origin opening with juicy ripe pear sweetness softened by warm vanilla, with brown sugar richness and a faint malty finish.

beans.name: Less-Caff
beans.producer: 66% Brazil and Colombia, 33% naturally decaffeinated Brazil
beans.desc: Two-thirds Brazilian and Colombian beans with one-third naturally decaf Brazilian, lowering caffeine while keeping flavour. Blueberry, dried dates, caramel and cedar; for espresso or cafetière.

beans.name: Costa Rica Hermosa Honey
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate mousse, Clotted cream, Malted milk
beans.desc: A silky, naturally sweet honey-processed Costa Rican with full mouthfeel and mild acidity. Chocolate dessert, thick cream and malty biscuit; a cosy cup with a lasting finish.

beans.name: Kenya Thunguri AA
beans.listedNotes: Green apple, Jasmine, White grape, Peach
beans.desc: A fully washed single-origin Kenyan showing the region's lively flavours: green apple, jasmine, white grape and peach with sharp acidity and succulent sweetness. A clean, graceful weekend brew.

beans.name: Peru Los Amigos Del Oso
beans.desc: A washed Peruvian single origin showing clarity and personality: cranberry, black tea, orange and molasses with zesty citrus brightness and a full, smooth ending.

beans.name: Brazil Fazenda Cachoeira
beans.producer: Minas Gerais; Fazenda Cachoeira (Dbarbosa); Red Catuai
beans.listedNotes: Maple, Candied orange, Chocolate (alt: milk chocolate, nuts)
beans.desc: The roaster's premium medium-roasted coffee, sweet with shortbread and apricot-jam character in the meta text. The page is inconsistent on process (honey peaberry versus natural, Red Catuai) and on notes.

beans.name: The Gunpowder Blend
beans.desc: An intense, smooth, well-balanced signature blend of Brazil and Uganda, a dark roast with caramel, coconut and red berry afternotes.

beans.name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe
beans.producer: Yirgacheffe; Aricha Wubanchi washing station; lot Konga; heirloom
beans.desc: A lively washed coffee from the Yirgacheffe highlands (about 1,950-2,050m) processed at the Aricha Wubanchi washing station; zesty lemonade acidity, sweet apricot and tart pomegranate with a soft floral finish.

beans.name: The Captain's Blend
beans.desc: A dark roast for drinkers who want intensity without an oily, bitter cup; billed as mysterious, intense, brooding and dark, and the roaster's premium blend for those who know.

beans.name: Kenya Kakindu
beans.listedNotes: Berry, White sugar, Cola, Stone fruit
beans.desc: A juicy, bright Kenyan grown at 1,800-2,000m in volcanic soil with cool nights for slow ripening; sweet berry and stone fruit, a hint of cola and clean white-sugar sweetness.

beans.name: Colombia Sugarcane Decaf
beans.desc: The roaster's only decaf; it says the Colombian bean stands up well to the sometimes harsh decaffeination process and recommends it to anyone who needs decaf.

beans.name: Colombia Planadas
beans.producer: Planadas, South Tolima; 1,042 smallholders, 23 groups; Castillo, Caturra; 1,984-2,050m
beans.desc: A light roast grown near 2,000m with elderflower, berry and milk chocolate; the roaster credits the altitude. Medium, silky body with a bright, fruit-forward acidity, suggested for filter, V60, AeroPress and batch brew.

beans.name: Honduras Aguacatillo
beans.producer: Guinope, El Paraiso; Finca El Aguacatillo (Alix Yovani Ramirez); IHCAFE 90, Lempira, Pacamara; 1,600-1,650m
beans.listedNotes: Lime, Maple syrup, Nuts, Red apple
beans.desc: A sweet, balanced and approachable Honduran grown at about 1,600-1,650m (IHCAFE 90 and Lempira); bright lime acidity with red apple, maple-syrup richness and a gentle nutty finish.

beans.name: The Kraken Blend
beans.desc: An extra-dark roast: a heavy, powerful cup with deep dark chocolate, smoky edges and burnt-sugar bitterness, with acidity nearly absent.

beans.name: Mexico Ki-Saya
beans.producer: Chiapas; Caturra, Costa Rica, Marsellesa, Typica
beans.desc: A smooth, balanced, approachable Chiapas coffee with rich dark chocolate and hazelnut, creamy nougat sweetness and a bright touch of lemon.

beans.name: The Armada Blend
beans.desc: A premium, people-pleasing medium-roast blend of Brazilian, Ugandan and Colombian beans (30/30/40) that works with every brew method, especially filter; clean and bright with chocolate, dried fruit and sweet acidity.

beans.name: Maximum Charge Super Strong Coffee
beans.desc: A medium roast marketed as the UK's most caffeinated coffee, using single-origin Rwandan Robusta. Smooth, layered dark chocolate and toasted grain, avoiding the scorched bitterness common in strong coffees.
beans.priceBasis: Metadata/listing 'from' price, likely 250g; page displays a higher price (probably a larger size); unconfirmed

beans.name: Iron Bar Espresso Blend
beans.producer: 50:50 darker roasted Rwandan robusta and Ethiopian
beans.listedNotes: Roasted cacao nib, Caramel, Raisin, Fig, Pomegranate
beans.desc: The company's first roast designed for espresso: darker Rwandan Robusta with natural Ethiopian beans in equal parts. Dense, intense mouthfeel with cocoa nibs, caramel, raisin, fig and pomegranate, and a strong caffeine kick.

beans.name: Cannonball Blend
beans.desc: The roaster's signature high-caffeine blend of Brazilian Arabica and Rwandan Robusta: a medium roast, strong and bold but pleasant, with chocolate and nutty notes and about 50% more caffeine than regular coffee; the middle of its three blends for strength.
beans.priceBasis: Metadata/listing 'from' price, likely 250g; page displays a higher price (probably a larger size); unconfirmed

beans.name: Smooth Bore
beans.desc: The roaster's most mellow coffee, with nuts, sweetness and chocolate; Brazilian Arabica with a small share of Rwandan Robusta for body, suggested for espresso or cafetiere.
beans.priceBasis: Metadata/listing 'from' price, likely 250g; page displays a higher price (probably a larger size); unconfirmed

beans.name: Uganda Malidadi
beans.producer: Malidadi, Sironko, Mount Elgon; Norman Mukuru and smallholders; SL14, SL28, Nyasaland; 1,500-1,850m
beans.listedNotes: Blood orange, Black cherry, Black tea, Toffee, Chewy body
beans.desc: A washed blend of SL14, SL28 and heritage Nyasaland varieties from small growers in Sironko, led by Norman Mukuru, on Mount Elgon's volcanic slopes. Dried apricot, black tea, gentle citrus and a fuller, sweeter mouthfeel.

beans.name: Brazil Volcanic Fermentation Patricia
beans.producer: Espirito Santo do Pinhal, Mogiana; Patricia Coelho, Fazenda Santo Antonio; Mundo Novo; 1,050-1,300m
beans.listedNotes: Rum and raisin, Mango, Milk chocolate, Toasted almond
beans.desc: A microlot from third-generation farmer Patricia Coelho in Mogiana, Brazil, with an intensive fermentation: overripe cherries are mounded, yeast-treated and hand-turned for days. Rum, raisin, mango, milk chocolate and toasted almond.

beans.name: Guatemala Huehuetenango
beans.listedNotes: Green apple, Caramel, Milk chocolate, Floral
beans.desc: A washed Huehuetenango from smallholders on steep slopes up to 2,000 metres, where a sheltered microclimate slows ripening. Crisp green apple, caramel and milk chocolate sweetness, and subtle florals.

beans.name: Kenya Kirinyaga
beans.producer: Kirinyaga County; 1,500+ farmers via a co-op; Bourbon, K7, Ruiru 11, SL28, SL34; 1,500-2,000m
beans.listedNotes: Blackcurrant, Shortbread, Vanilla, Orange, Mulling spices
beans.desc: A fully washed AB from Kirinyaga County, Kenya, with fruity depth, wine-like brightness and a smooth, silky close. Classic blackcurrant and red berry; over 1,500 farmers contributed.

beans.name: Mexican Mountain Water Decaf
beans.desc: A washed single-origin Mexican decaf, vibrant and richly flavoured, presented as proof that decaf need not sacrifice quality.

beans.name: Colombia Dulima
beans.desc: Created in 2009, Dulima reflects central and southern Huila, Colombia, where volcanoes and mountains grow excellent coffee. Each lot is tasted at origin to keep quality steady; named after the Pijao word for the Tolima volcano, meaning Snow Queen.

beans.name: Costa Rica Tarrazu
beans.desc: Tarrazú is grown at the highest elevations of any Costa Rican region and prized for rich weight and layered flavour. This dark roast has strong, pronounced bitterness for adventurous palates and a devoted following.

beans.name: Two Brothers Blend
beans.producer: Peru Huabal; Brasil Sao Bernardo; Brasil Barrinha
beans.listedNotes: Digestive biscuit, Honey, Plum, Buttery body
beans.desc: A Brazil and Peru blend with a sugary, layered cup, rich buttery mouthfeel, biscuity notes reminiscent of a tea-time snack, honey and stone fruit.

beans.name: Shogun Blend
beans.desc: A blend for milk-based drinks, with a velvety, weighty, well-rounded mouthfeel of creamy chocolate, toasted malt and nutty praline.

beans.name: Supreme Blend
beans.desc: The original signature blend, in the line-up since the 1990s. Modelled on a classic Italian style with 10% Robusta for a hearty, low-acid cup with dark chocolate, molasses sweetness and hazelnut.

beans.name: North Street Blend
beans.producer: 50% Guatemala Huehuetenango, 50% Costa Rica Tarrazu (formerly Trishs Mix)
beans.desc: A blend of equal parts dark-roasted Guatemalan Huehuetenango and highly roasted Costa Rican Tarrazú, previously sold as Trish's Mix, a long-time customer favourite.

beans.name: Gibran Cervantes
beans.desc: From El Equimite in Veracruz, where Gibrán Cervantes grows coffee under native forest canopy beside fruit trees and wildlife using biodynamic methods. Misty mountain climate slows ripening and builds sweetness.

beans.name: House
beans.desc: The roastery's flagship espresso since 2010, from long-term producer partners and transparent seasonal lots. Roasted to show bright fruit while staying balanced and sweet: a juicy, moreish espresso.

beans.name: Daily
beans.desc: A blend for any hour and any brew method, smooth and well rounded as espresso or filter. A twist on a classic style with heavy mouthfeel, gentle acidity and a crisp aftertaste.

beans.name: Vista
beans.desc: The signature filter blend, highlighting coffees from farms owned by women. Mixes washed and natural lots from long-standing partners; lively ripe fruit balanced by syrupy sweetness, good with any method.

beans.name: Decaf
beans.listedNotes: Maple syrup, Poached pear, Chocolate brownie
beans.desc: A decaf from Colombia's Cauca mountains processed with leftovers from local sugarcane farming, giving a sweet, tropical character. Enjoyable at any hour as espresso or filter.

beans.name: Little Miracles Blend
beans.desc: A 100% Arabica blend grown at high altitude: smooth, gentle and mildly acidic, with chocolate, fruit and citrus. All profits go to a North East group supporting families of children with serious health conditions.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf SHG
beans.producer: Ocotepeque; Finca El Alto (Ludwin Daniel Aguilar); Pacas, Bourbon, Catuai; 1,370-1,475m

beans.name: Copan Specialty SHG
beans.producer: Celaque region (Copan, Ocotepeque, Lempira); Bourbon, Caturra, Catuai; 1,000-1,800m
beans.desc: The roastery's top seller, sourced from Honduras's Celaque region. Caramel and chocolate with a faint sweet, smoky edge, a firm rich body and gentle brightness; suits mornings or an afternoon lift.

beans.name: Lempira Specialty SHG
beans.producer: Lempira; El Remolino, Agua Fria (Anastacio Benitez Diaz); 1,850m
beans.desc: A high-altitude specialty lot from Lempira, Honduras, at about 1,850 metres. A lively, mid-weight cup of chocolate and citrus with a faint floral note at the front of the palate.

beans.name: La Paz Specialty SHG
beans.producer: La Paz, Comayagua, Intibuca; many varieties incl. Pacamara, Geisha; 1,100-2,200m
beans.listedNotes: Orange, Peach, Bright acidity, Velvety body
beans.desc: From La Paz, Honduras, where growers have won Cup of Excellence three times. Beans ripen gradually for a smooth, sweet body, with a lively, bright cup of citrus and stone fruit.

beans.name: Atlantic Blend
beans.desc: A two-bean blend named for the sea bordering Honduras and the Caribbean islands, for people wanting novelty without leaving their daily brew. Soft, sweet aroma.

beans.name: Microlot Jaguar
beans.producer: Los Pajuiles, San Miguelito, Intibuca; Jose Maximo Cantarero Bautista; 1,400m
beans.desc: Jose's Jaguar has become one of the roastery's top sellers: a robust, rich-bodied microlot with vibrant fruit and honey notes.

beans.name: La Odisea
beans.producer: San Pedro de Tutule, La Paz; Finca La Odisea (Selvin Umanzor); Lempira; 1,626m
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Brown sugar, Ripe fruits
beans.desc: Grown on a high-altitude farm in La Paz, Honduras, by a third-generation producer honouring his father's legacy. Honey and natural processing bring out distinctive flavours in a strictly high-grown specialty coffee.

beans.name: Capuchin SHG
beans.producer: Marcala, La Paz; El Cerquin del Portillo farms (Ana Lorena Melghen and Luis Rodolfo Argueta); Bourbon, Parainema, Icatu; 1,300-1,400m
beans.desc: A velvety, mellow Honduran with no harshness: caramel sweetness, nutty depth, faint fruit and a gentle chocolate finish. Low acidity and balanced body suit black or with milk.

beans.name: Colibri SHG
beans.producer: Capucas; COCAFCAL farming families; Catuai, Caturra, Icatu, Pacamara, Pacas; 1,500m
beans.desc: From farming families in Capucas, Honduras, who also keep bees. Honey-processed, tasting of pineapple, rum, apricot and papaya; dried slowly in solar units and turned for over two weeks.

beans.name: Guacamaya SHG
beans.desc: High-altitude, shade-grown specialty coffee picked at peak ripeness, washed and sun-dried in parchment. Bird Friendly certified and traceable to its cooperative.

beans.name: Microlot Puma
beans.producer: El Zarzal, Tambla, Lempira; Jose Cecilio Lopez Mejia; IHCAFE 90, Lempira, Catimor; 1,350m
beans.desc: From Jose's microlot beans, Puma has appealing caramel and fruit flavours for any time of day, with medium body and smooth texture.

beans.name: Pacific Blend
beans.desc: A specialty blend of carefully selected Arabicas with peach, dark chocolate and citrus, a sweet fermented aroma and balanced finish. Named for the Pacific Ocean south of Honduras.

beans.name: La Esmeralda
beans.producer: Marcala, La Paz; Finca La Esmeralda (Lili Penalva); Yellow and Red Catuai, Pacamara; 1,550m
beans.listedNotes: Jasmine, Sweet caramel, Brown sugar, Creamy body
beans.desc: A single-estate Honduran from a high-mountain farm that protects its environment. Honey and natural processing with slow patio drying give a creamy body and jasmine, caramel and brown sugar.

beans.name: El Espiritu Santo
beans.producer: Marcala, La Paz; Finca El Espiritu Santo (Max Penalva); Yellow and Pink Catuai, IHCAFE 90, Lempira, Parainema, Bourbon; 1,690m
beans.desc: Grown by Max Peñalva on his 5.5-acre plot in Marcala at 1,690 metres, from a multi-generation coffee family. Washed Arabica, punchy yet balanced, with floral, dark sugar and caramel notes.

beans.name: El Cerquin del Portillo
beans.producer: Marcala, La Paz; Finca el Portillo (Melghen and Argueta); Maragogipe; 1,300-1,400m
beans.desc: Grown by a family of five near Marcala from Maragogipe trees at Finca el Portillo, a scarce, low-yielding variety prone to pests. Washed, with medium body, citrus brightness, brown sugar and cream.

beans.name: La Pena
beans.producer: Marcala, La Paz; Finca la Penona (Melghen and Argueta); Icatu
beans.desc: A single origin from the Peñona section of a family farm in Marcala, Honduras. Washed Icatu giving a smooth, rich cup with blackberry, caramel and brown sugar.

beans.name: Stoked Trail Blend
beans.desc: Developed with Stoked Casual Wear, a husband-and-wife mountain biking team, as a natural lift before riding. Smooth and low in bitterness, sweet enough black, with caramel and chocolate.

beans.name: Microlot Saber
beans.producer: El Zarzal, Tambla, Lempira; Exequiel Lopez Lopez; IHCAFE 90, Red Catuai, Catimor, Parainema; 1,300m
beans.desc: The Saber blend has a full, velvety texture for a relaxed day indoors. Approachable and mellow with understated flavours and floral and chocolatey hints.

beans.name: Intibuca SHG
beans.producer: San Miguelito, Intibuca; Jose Erasmo Orellana Bautista; Lempira, IHCAFE 90; 1,100-2,000m

beans.name: Copan Specialty HG
beans.desc: Sourced from Honduras's Celaque region, a reliable top-selling house coffee with caramel and chocolate, a hint of sweet smokiness, a robust body and gentle acidity.

beans.name: Curiosities - Magnum Sidra
beans.producer: Tolima; El Vergel Estate (Elias and Shady Bayter); Borbon Sidra; 1,450m
beans.desc: A Colombian lot from El Vergel Estate in Tolima, tasting of mango, limoncello and jasmine. Sidra fermented in a mosto process using liquid by-products, then sun-dried and rested about a month.

beans.name: Curiosities - Jennifer Delgado Sanchez
beans.producer: La Union, Narino; La Loma; Jennifer Delgado Sanchez; Geisha
beans.desc: A lot the roasters see as a standout for clarity and refinement: gentle sweetness, lively acidity and a floral finish. Possibly their favourite of the year, brewed as pour-over.

beans.name: Curiosities - Maria Omaira
beans.producer: Cusillo Bajo, La Union, Narino; El Cuadradero; Maria Omaira; Geisha; 1,800-1,914m
beans.desc: Found at a tasting table in Nariño and bought with Plot. Sweet and softly tart, with stone fruit and passionfruit character.

beans.name: Decaf - Black Condor
beans.producer: El Vergel Estate (Elias and Shady Bayter); Red and Yellow Caturra
beans.desc: A very sweet, appealing single-origin decaf with hints of caramel, berry and vanilla, enjoyed as espresso or flat white and good with any brew method.

beans.name: Decaf - La Serrania
beans.producer: Pitalito area, central cordillera; community of local farmers; Caturra, Castillo, Colombia; 1,500-1,750m
beans.desc: A decaf, sweet and mellow with gentle acidity and hints of raisin, toffee and chocolate. Andean highland beans are handled as carefully as the regular range; caffeine is removed with a sugarcane-derived solvent.

beans.name: Decaf - Melao
beans.producer: Southern Huila smallholders; Pink Bourbon; 1,500-1,750m; decaffeinated at Descafecol
beans.processFull: Washed and honey; sugarcane EA decaf
beans.desc: Melao is a sweet, lively decaf of Colombian Pink Bourbon from small growers in Huila. Named for golden cane-sugar syrup and decaffeinated with sugarcane-derived ethyl acetate, keeping a rich, dessert-like character.

beans.name: Espresso - Black Condor
beans.producer: Gaitania, Tolima; Emmanuel Enciso and local farmers; Colombia, Castillo, Caturra
beans.desc: Very sweet, with pleasant woodland fruit and a touch of cocoa. Well rounded; enjoyed as espresso and in flat whites, and good however you brew it.

beans.name: Espresso - El Guayacan
beans.producer: San Ignacio and Jaen, northern Peru; smallholders via Caravela; Caturra, Bourbon, Catimor, Pache; 1,650-2,000m
beans.desc: A reliable, sweet, well-balanced Peruvian for espresso or slow brewing, picked ripe by small farmers near the Ecuador border, washed and sun-dried. Suits mornings and entertaining.

beans.name: Espresso - Misadhi PB
beans.producer: Kericho County; Sidney Kibet (Lot 20); Batian, Ruiru 11; 1,800m
beans.listedNotes: White chocolate, Almond, Black Forest gateau
beans.desc: A full-bodied Kenyan espresso with sweetness like black forest gateau and subtle almond and white chocolate. Works with or without milk and across brew methods.

beans.name: Espresso - San Ramon
beans.producer: Dipilto mountains; Finca San Ramon (Donald Efrain Roque Lopez); Pacamara, Catuai, Maragogype
beans.desc: A thrilling, very sweet Nicaraguan: crisp and lively, with rich cocoa, caramel and honey lingering and only a hint of acidity.

beans.name: Espresso - Sisterhood
beans.producer: Huehuetenango, San Antonio Huista; women smallholders; Caturra, Catuai, Bourbon; 1,550-1,650m
beans.desc: A roast for cooler months: full-bodied and sweet with cocoa, a subtle nutty note and lasting toffee apple. Good alone or with milk.

beans.name: Filter - Finca Morales
beans.producer: Nuevo Belen, Amazonas; Finca Morales (Roiber Becerra, Norcafe coop); Geisha; 1,900m
beans.desc: From Roiber Becerra's Finca Morales in Amazonas, Peru. A fruity coffee with lively acidity and floral aromas; he grows prized Geisha with agroforestry in the Norcafé cooperative, with fermentation adjusted to weather before solar drying.

beans.name: Filter - Finca Pacpa
beans.producer: Roblepampa, Amazonas; Finca Pacpa (Manuel Marlo Baca); Pacamara; 1,850m
beans.desc: A juicy coffee bursting with strawberry and nectarine, ending on jasmine. Works with any brew method, especially AeroPress or pour-over.

beans.name: Finca El Morito
beans.producer: El Diamante, Cajamarca; Faustino Flores; Marshell; 1,750m
beans.desc: A well-rounded coffee with medium body and gentle acidity. A jammy core finishing with honey, with raspberry ice cream, mango and chocolate; good with or without milk for espresso, cafetière or stovetop.

beans.name: Dimora - House Blend
beans.desc: A well-rounded house blend for any brew method, from two origins on opposite sides of the equator harvested at different times. Light roasting avoids bitterness; as espresso, milk chocolate and bright acidity, with honey notes in milk.

beans.name: Alba - Medium Roast
beans.desc: An Arabica blend from four tropical regions with a thick, velvety body from a moderate roast that keeps sweetness for milky drinks. Notes of nut butter, malt and caramel apple.

beans.name: Terreno - Dark Roast
beans.desc: A full-bodied espresso blend roasted intensely for smooth, silky crema. Deep roasting brings out hazelnut and cocoa with little sharpness; best as espresso and for white coffees and lattes.

beans.name: Sorella - Women's Collective
beans.producer: San Alberto highlands; EMURSA women collective (28 farmers); Colombia, Castillo; 1,600-1,800m
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate truffle, Granny Smith apple
beans.desc: A Colombian named for the Italian word for sister, from a women-led cooperative in San Alberto avoiding synthetic fertilisers and working towards organic certification. Dark chocolate and tart green apple.

beans.name: Seasonal Blend: Blackberry Jammin'
beans.desc: A limited autumn release mixing washed Kenyan peaberry with a natural Ugandan from the Rwenzori Mountains. Lively and fruity, deepening into brown sugar and mild warmth; creamier and sweeter with milk, for espresso or filter.

beans.name: Sereno - Decaffeinated
beans.priceBasis: Listing 'from' price, size not shown (likely 200g); unconfirmed

beans.name: Kamwangi AB
beans.producer: Kirinyaga; Kamwangi Factory, New Ngariama FCS; Batian, Ruiru 11, SL28; 1,600-2,000m
beans.desc: A lively, fruit-forward Kenyan: sweet red cherry with gentle vanilla, zesty grapefruit and a hint of liquorice. A clean washed profile suited to V60, AeroPress or cafetière.

beans.name: Kakindu Estate Peaberry
beans.desc: A Kakindu Estate lot, lively and refined with balanced structure. Deep black cherry sweetness with silky chocolate and zesty acidity; good as filter or fruity espresso.

beans.name: Coban
beans.producer: Coban, Alta Verapaz; smallholder family farms; 1,300-1,800m
beans.desc: A washed coffee from small-scale producers around Cobán, Guatemala: easygoing sweetness and crisp balance. Cherry meets roasted nuts and buttery caramel, with light cucumber-like freshness; suits filter or sweet espresso.

beans.name: Murambi Hill (Red Bourbon)
beans.producer: Bujumbura Rural; Migoti Hill washing station; Red Bourbon; 2,000m
beans.desc: A Burundian grown by smallholders on hillsides near Lake Tanganyika, hand-picked and processed at Migoti Hill washing station led by Zephyrin Banzubaze. Vivid and polished, with tangerine and black tea.

beans.name: African Moon (Uganda)
beans.priceBasis: Listing 'from' price, size not shown (likely 200g); unconfirmed

beans.name: Ratnagiri Estate
beans.desc: From Ratnagiri Estate, a forward-thinking Indian grower. The Hemavathi lot ferments four days with cultured yeast, then dries slowly. Juicy mango, almond-paste sweetness and candied citrus peel; for filter or espresso.

beans.name: Gelcha Kindu
beans.producer: Gedeb; Gelcha Kindu station (Gargari Gutity); Heirloom; 2,100-2,350m
beans.desc: An experimental Ethiopian: clean and nuanced with tropical fruit and botanical accents. Pineapple and passionfruit lead, with juniper and a Thai-basil-like herbal hint; anaerobic honey processing adds richness. Best as filter.

beans.name: No Stone Estate
beans.producer: Simao, Yunnan; No Stone Estate (Lu Sun); Catimor P3, P4; 1,300-1,500m
beans.desc: A Yunnan coffee from No Stone Estate, lively and citrus-forward. Fermented over 150 hours with an enzyme-rich liquid made from Buddha's hand citrus. Lemongrass, soft florals and a subtle ginger finish.

beans.name: Huila Decaf (Sugarcane)
beans.desc: A medium-roast decaf from a small Huila cooperative. Sweet, layered aroma of caramel and brown sugar; a smooth, rich cup with cocoa hints, sugarcane sweetness, creamy body and low acidity.

beans.name: Doghouse
beans.producer: Carmo de Minas; Santa Lucia; Catuai
beans.desc: Carringtons' everyday house coffee: a medium roast from a single Brazilian estate with chocolate and caramel. Built to be dependable, good as espresso black or with milk.

beans.name: Limited Release - Costa Rica
beans.producer: Santa Maria de Dota, Tarrazu; Microdota Mujer, Coopedota; Catuai, Caturra
beans.desc: A seasonal Costa Rican chosen for crisp definition, sturdy build and lively acidity. A light roast lets the bean's qualities come through sharply; for filter or a zippier espresso.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf
beans.desc: A medium-roast Colombian decaf chosen for harmony, natural sweetness and easy drinking. Caramel and apple in a light, tidy profile for espresso or filter.

beans.name: PB & J
beans.desc: Inspired by peanut butter and jelly: a light roast of 70% Brazilian and 30% Ugandan with cocoa-like richness and nuttiness, gentle fruit that lifts rather than tarts. Works with any brew style.

beans.name: Pawsome
beans.producer: 40% Guatemala Todosantarita; 40% Brazil Patricia; 20% Ethiopia Yirgacheffe
beans.listedNotes: Rich, Balanced, Gentle sweetness (no formal notes)
beans.desc: A dark-roasted espresso blend for a substantial, comforting cup with smooth, full mouthfeel. Ethiopian beans add soft sweetness; good black or with milk.

beans.name: Colombia Core
beans.producer: Suarez, Cauca; Cafe Granja La Esperanza (Juanambu); Castillo, Colombia, Caturra, Tabi
beans.desc: A medium-roast Colombian blend chosen for evenness, sweetness and approachability: chocolate, caramel and orange with a soft, calm character and light citrus brightness. For espresso or filter.

beans.name: Ethiopia
beans.producer: Haru, Yirgacheffe; G1 Haru; Dega, 74-112, Kudhume, Wolisho; 1,995-2,020m
beans.desc: A lightly roasted Ethiopian chosen for vibrancy, transparency and uplift, roasted for expressive, precise flavours as filter or espresso. Floral, grape and raspberry.

beans.name: Nicaragua - Single Origin
beans.producer: Dipilto, Nueva Segovia; Agua Sarca; Cafetos de Segovia; Red and Yellow Catuai
beans.desc: A nutty, chocolatey Nicaraguan single origin with easygoing sweetness. Sisters Martha and Ana run a family dry mill in Ocotal and experiment with fermentation and drying. Creamy macadamia, roasted peanuts and cereal sweetness.

beans.name: Ethiopia - Single Origin
beans.desc: An Ethiopian from the Sidama highlands at 2,000-2,100 metres, supplied by hundreds of smallholders. Cherries are sorted and dried on raised beds for weeks. Floral aromas, stone fruit, melon and a zesty orange lift.

beans.name: Tanzania - Single Origin
beans.desc: A Tanzanian for all-day drinking, pulled as espresso for milk drinks or brewed as smooth filter. Not flashy but balanced and well rounded; poured as espresso at the team's beach café through August.

beans.name: Riptide Espresso Winter Blend 2026/27
beans.producer: 70% Guatemala, 30% Brazil; Caturra, Catuai, Sarchimor, Yellow Bourbon
beans.desc: A winter house blend made with Riptide Espresso and Records in Poole, sold only by Carve. Guatemalan coffee gives a sweet, syrupy body and grapefruit; Brazilian adds chocolate and nutty depth. For espresso and filter.

beans.name: Venture Espresso Blend
beans.desc: The flagship blend of two South American beans from Brazil and Colombia: balanced tang, rich nutty notes, a touch of raisin sweetness and a chocolatey finish. Excels as espresso and in milk; suits any brew.

beans.name: Colombia - Decaf
beans.desc: A medium-roast decaf from Santander, Colombia, using the sugarcane process on a blend of varieties. Expect dark chocolate, caramel and nuts.

beans.name: Dahwe
beans.producer: Dahwe washing station, Gisagara; Maraho Trading Company; Red Bourbon; 1,630m
beans.desc: From the Dahwe washing station in Gisagara District, Rwanda, at 1,630 metres. Over 1,400 growers supply it, tending around 340,000 trees; in 2025 Muraho Trading Co. supplied 85,000 seedlings and helped with irrigation and roads.

beans.name: Finca Majahual
beans.producer: Los Naranjos Valley, Apaneca; Patric Murray and farmers; Bourbon
beans.desc: Grown on Patrick Murray's 90-hectare fourth-generation farm in the Los Naranjos Valley, western El Salvador, with coffee woven into the forest. Shade protects soil and wildlife; the farm backs a local school and a health and nutrition programme.

beans.name: Arsosala
beans.producer: Guji, Uraga; Arsosala washing station smallholders; heirloom and landrace
beans.desc: From a washing station in Ethiopia's Guji region at about 1,800 metres, opened in 2015 and working with about 1,200 small growers who earn a bonus for quality. This small batch uses only fully ripe cherries, processed separately.

beans.name: Antonio Gonzalez
beans.producer: Fraijanes, El Palmar; La Nueva Montana (Antonio Gonzalez); Yellow Catuai
beans.desc: From El Palmar in Fraijanes, Guatemala: Antonio's 16-hectare farm grows beans under Inga, grevillea and avocado shade. Selling natural and honey lots improves his income, funding fairer wages and helping growers who can't afford upgrades.

beans.name: Niguse Jilo
beans.producer: Halo Bariti, Yirgacheffe; Niguse Jilo; Kurume; 2,150m
beans.desc: Niguse Jilo farms at 2,150 metres in Yirgacheffe and leads the Bore Nageso group, applying specialty techniques; his income supports ten children. His 2022 coffee ranked in the top 40 at Cup of Excellence.

beans.name: Don Alfonzo
beans.producer: Aquiares Estate (Don Alfonzo Robelo); Red Obata; 1,100-1,400m
beans.desc: Don Alfonzo Robelo has run Aquiares Estate, one of Costa Rica's historic farms, since 1992, with a focus on sustainability and communities. A high-altitude washed Red Obatã, supported by estate youth, health and home ownership programmes.

beans.name: Kamwangi
beans.producer: Kirinyaga; Kamwangi washing station, Ngariama FCS; Batian, Ruiru 11, SL28
beans.desc: A Kenyan from a highland washing station on Mount Kenya's slopes, where small growers farm at 1,600-1,800 metres. Cool temperatures and volcanic soil slow ripening, building intricate, mature fruit flavours.

beans.name: Shoondhisa
beans.desc: Thirty-five small farmers from Shoondhisa supplied this lot, processed by Sookoo Coffee in Shakiso. Plots average about 2.5 hectares, often shared with food crops, and communal drying stations help growers without their own facilities earn fair prices.

beans.name: Mayra Solis
beans.producer: Tarrazu, Santa Maria de Dota; Alto El Vapor micromill (Mayra Solis); Catuai
beans.desc: Mayra Solís and her three children run the Alto El Vapor micromill on one of Tarrazú's highest farms, growing produce too, with much land protected. Bean Voyage, a women-focused programme, provides training, seed funding and market access.

beans.name: Las Lajas
beans.producer: Las Lajas micromill (Oscar and Francisca Chacon); Caturra, Catuai
beans.desc: Oscar and Francisca Chacón run a Costa Rican farm from their grandparents. After a 2008 earthquake they borrowed African-style raised beds and helped pioneer honey processing there. This black honey lot dries for weeks in greenhouse piles.

beans.name: Pedro Pastor
beans.producer: Curaren, Francisco Morazan; IHCAFE 90, Lempira, Parainema
beans.desc: Second-generation farmer Pedro Pastor grows this coffee in Curarén, Honduras, at 1,350-1,600 metres in a region of long dry spells. Growers protect water and soil by planting with native and shade trees.

beans.name: Magarciy
beans.producer: Santiago Atitlan, Lake Atitlan; Jose Ramirez and family; mixed varieties
beans.desc: Grown near Santiago Atitlán on Lake Atitlán by a family business named for José Ramirez's father, supporting small Tzutujil farmers under shade. It runs a roastery led by José's son and a café staffed by young local women.

beans.name: Kii
beans.producer: Gichugu, Kirinyaga; Kii Factory, Rungeto FCS; SL28, SL34, Ruiru 11, Batian
beans.desc: From small farmers in Gichugu, Kirinyaga, at 1,600-1,900 metres, where local cultivation dates to 1953 and a typical grower tends 400 trees on a third of a hectare. Processed at Kii Factory by the Rungeto Farmers Cooperative Society.

beans.name: Karogoto
beans.producer: Nyeri, Mathira; Karogoto Factory near Karatina; SL28, SL34, Ruiru 11, Batian
beans.desc: Grown by small farmers in Nyeri's Mathira area at 1,650 metres. About 1,250 members of Karogoto Factory near Karatina contribute, many of them women, each tending about 250 trees alongside maize and bananas.

beans.name: Gihere
beans.desc: Smallholders in Burundi's Ngozi region grow this at high altitude, hand-picking cherries for central processing at Gihere Washing Station, which gives growers access to investment, education and better infrastructure.

beans.name: Gakenke
beans.desc: Smallholders in Kayanza, Burundi farm plots of 1,650-1,950 metres, usually under half a hectare, with bananas, beans and root crops. Ripe cherries go to Gakenke washing station, which helps with funding, training and infrastructure.

beans.name: Elisabete Martins
beans.desc: Run by Elisabete Martins and family, who left 23 years in supermarkets in 2000 to move into coffee. Cherries are laid thinly to dry naturally in the sun, with regular turning for even drying and few flaws.
beans.priceBasis: Listing price, size not shown (likely 250g); unconfirmed

beans.name: Misspent Youth
beans.producer: Elisabete Martins, Fazenda Cachoeira (Brazil, Catuai); Mensur Abahika Jemal, Jimma (Ethiopia, 74110, 74112)
beans.desc: A blend of two naturals: Brazilian Catuaí from Elisabete Martins's family at Fazenda Cachoeira, and Ethiopian 74110 and 74112 from Mensur Jemal, whose 18-hectare Jimma farm joins the Tokuma farmer group.

beans.name: Legoman (Decaf)
beans.producer: Popayan; 65 growers via Cofinet; Caturra, Castillo, Colombia
beans.desc: A decaf from 65 growers in the Popayán region supplying a programme run by Cofinet, which has worked long-term with these farmers to prioritise quality.

beans.name: Latitude Espresso
beans.desc: A seasonal espresso of Ethiopian Sidama and a Guatemalan lot from Finca Santa Isabel. Crisp, tangy floral first, then juicy berry-like sweetness as it cools, finishing on caramel-toffee.

beans.name: Solitude Espresso
beans.producer: Finca San Lorenzo, San Cristobal Verapaz, Coban (Valdes family); Caturra, Catuai, Sarchimor; 1,550m
beans.desc: An espresso currently from one Guatemalan coffee with gentle acidity and deep sweetness: blackberry, plum and praline. From Finca San Lorenzo, a high-altitude farm near Cobán.

beans.name: Lakes Espresso
beans.producer: Ecoagricola (Flanzer family), Serra do Cabral, Minas Gerais; Yellow Catucai; 1,100m
beans.desc: An espresso currently featuring one Brazilian coffee from the Flanzer family in Serra do Cabral. Chocolate, dried fruit and nuts with a traditional roast profile.

beans.name: Lakes Filter
beans.producer: Ecoagricola (Flanzer family), Serra do Cabral, Minas Gerais; Yellow Catucai; 1,100m
beans.desc: A filter blend of a single Brazilian from the Flanzer family farm in Serra do Cabral. Same beans as Lakes Espresso but roasted more deeply, with chocolate, dried fruit and nut.

beans.name: Decaf
beans.producer: Pergamino blend of four lots, Huila, Cauca and Antioquia
beans.desc: A decaf of four Colombian lots from small farms in three regions, decaffeinated by the sugarcane method. Orange brightness, then cocoa and a toffee close; sweet with chocolate and caramel in milk.

beans.name: El Carmen
beans.desc: An anaerobic natural from a generational family estate at 1,300 metres in El Salvador's Apaneca-Llamatepec range. Juicy lychee, candy-like tropical sweetness and blood orange as it cools, with a long, refreshing finish.

beans.name: Santa Isabel
beans.desc: From a 300-hectare Guatemalan estate, washed and sun-dried. Starts like black tea, then hazelnut bitterness with juicy sweetness, finishing with apricot and bergamot as it cools.

beans.name: Brazil Cerrado
beans.producer: Cerrado and Alta Mogiana; Mundo Novo, Catuai
beans.desc: Grown in Brazil's Cerrado and Alta Mogiana areas at 800 to 1,200 metres, this naturally processed coffee has a smooth, weighty mouthfeel and little tartness. Flavours lean toward chocolate, caramel and nuts, suiting espresso and milk drinks.

beans.name: Colombia Tatacoa
beans.desc: Named after Colombia's Tatacoa Desert, this Huila blend reflects the region's resilience and vibrancy. Its beans grow in fertile soil under strong equatorial sun, sourced through the roaster's own Carcafe operation. Tasting notes lean toward chocolate, stone fruit and caramel.

beans.name: Decaf Colombia Popayan Reserve
beans.desc: Sourced from selected farms around Popayan, milled there, then decaffeinated in Caldas using a sugarcane-derived byproduct and water, avoiding high heat to preserve sweetness. Expect honey, vanilla and chocolate-milk notes with a full body.

beans.name: Union Espresso Blend
beans.desc: An espresso blend with a well-rounded profile and thick, velvety texture. Dark chocolate and caramel sit alongside bright, stone-fruit-like acidity. An even mix of a Brazilian natural and a Colombian washed coffee.

beans.name: Charlestown Espresso Blend
beans.producer: Cerrado (Brazil); Goroka, Eastern Highlands (PNG); Typica, Bourbon
beans.desc: The roaster's most popular espresso blend, named for the neighbourhood where it's roasted. Traditional and full-bodied, it stands up to milk. Cocoa, toffee and shortbread notes lead to a velvety, smooth finish.

beans.name: Ethiopia Lalesa
beans.desc: A standout Ethiopian lot from Gedeb, grown under shade at high altitude and hand-picked in the dry season. Cherries ferment nine days in sealed containers before sun-drying. Produced by Ephtah, supporting local families, a childcare centre and women farmers.

beans.name: Colombia Guava Banana
beans.producer: Tolima; El Vergel Estate (Elias and Shady Bayter); Red and Yellow Caturra; 1,350m
beans.desc: Grown by Elías and Shady Bayter at El Vergel Estate in Colombia. Selected cherries ferment in an airtight, oxygen-free setting before sun-drying, giving a full-bodied, layered cup with hints of banana, kiwi and raw cane sugar.

beans.name: Colombia El Indio
beans.desc: A pure Caturra microlot supplied by Cofinet. Only fully ripe fruit was harvested, hand-sorted and sun-dried on raised beds in controlled conditions. Look for blackberry, cherry and a wine-like edge.

beans.name: Edinson Argote SL28
beans.producer: Oporapa, Huila; La Quebraditas (Edinson Argote); SL28; 1,850m
beans.processFull: Double anaerobic washed, yeast inoculated, thermal shock
beans.desc: From La Quebraditas in Huila, where Edinson Argote uses a two-stage fermentation with temperature shocks and added yeast. This SL28 is his third batch with the roaster, with bright herbal, minty flavours evoking a cooling mojito.

beans.name: Jefferson Motta Pink Bourbon
beans.producer: Acevedo, Huila; Jefferson Adrian Motta; Pink Bourbon; 1,700m
beans.desc: Jefferson Adrián Motta of Acevedo, Huila, mixes classic and experimental methods. A natural process on his Pink Bourbon adds sweetness and layered character, giving a lively, wine-like cup best enjoyed black as filter.

beans.name: Fabric Filter Blend
beans.desc: A new seasonal filter blend of two washed African peaberries, one Kenyan and one Rwandan. Vivid blackcurrant and tangerine with a black tea finish; suits pour-over, AeroPress and batch brew.

beans.name: Catanduva
beans.producer: Patos de Minas, Minas Gerais; Marie Nakao; Catuai, Vermelho; 1,080m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: Brazilian coffee grown at 1,080 metres in Minas Gerais, rich, sweet and low in acidity. Third-generation producer Marie Nakao emphasises sustainability and regenerative methods. Medium-dark roasted, for espresso fans and newcomers to specialty filter.

beans.name: Finca La Colombia
beans.producer: Ciudad Bolivar, Antioquia; Finca La Colombia via Cafe Lumbus; Caturra; 1,800-2,050m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A full-bodied Colombian from an Antioquia farm, sourced directly from the grower. Raspberry, brown sugar and hazelnut notes, medium roasted for filter and espresso, with moderate brightness and smooth sweetness that works black or with milk.

beans.name: Eden Seasonal Espresso Blend
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A sweet, fruity espresso blend with toffee, honey and woodland fruit flavours. Roasted slightly darker than the single-origin espressos to keep sweetness and depth with little bitterness. The blend's makeup shifts through the year.

beans.name: Cumbres Decaf
beans.producer: Ciudad Bolivar, Antioquia; Cafe Cumbres; Caturra, Castillo; 1,500-1,700m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A naturally decaffeinated Colombian from Café Cumbres, a Cast Iron supplier for three years. Lively, sweet and well rounded rather than diminished, with brownie-like dark chocolate, biscuit and plum; good as espresso or filter.

beans.name: Unity Espresso Blend
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: The house espresso: rich and smooth with mellow acidity, built to taste consistent all year and holding up well in milk for a sweet drink. Roasted only for espresso, suiting black coffee and milk drinks.

beans.name: La Secreta
beans.producer: Antioquia; Finca La Secreta; Caturra Chiroso; 1,980m
beans.processFull: Anaerobic washed (meta text says lactic honey)
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: From Finca La Secreta in Antioquia, the roaster's third annual purchase from the farm; this year a washed Chiroso lot. Buttery body and floral character, with zesty tangerine aroma and tropical mango, passion fruit and lychee.

beans.name: La Reserva
beans.producer: Ciudad Bolivar, Antioquia; La Reserva (Carlos Pineda); Geisha; 1,800-2,000m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A Colombian Geisha from La Reserva, grown high so the land's character shows. A 96-hour anaerobic fermentation and careful honey process yield a graceful, layered cup with lively sweetness and floral, tropical fruit.

beans.name: Andy Llanos Geisha
beans.producer: Santa Rosa, Colasay, Cajamarca; Pluma Dorada (Andy Llanos Delgado); Geisha
beans.listedNotes: Elderflower, Chardonnay, Green apple, Blood orange
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A washed Geisha from Peruvian grower Andy Llanos, whose highland farm in northern Peru's Colasay region shows its potential. Submerged fermentation shapes a complex profile with lively acidity, tea-like body and floral notes.

beans.name: Marcelo Perez
beans.producer: Huehuetenango; Marcelo Perez Pablo (ASDEFLOR); Catuai, Pache, Typica; 1,700m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: Smallholder Marcelo Pérez grows this washed Guatemalan in Huehuetenango's high mountains, fermented in open clay tanks without water, then dried on beds and patios. Nectarine and plum with milk chocolate and hazelnut.

beans.name: Gicherori AA
beans.producer: Kibugu, Embu County; Gicherori Factory; SL28, SL34; 1,600-1,800m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: From Gicherori Factory, a community-led site in Kibugu taking cherries from about 1,200 smallholders on Mount Kenya's high slopes. Only the ripest are selected, washed and sun-dried, giving a bright, silky cup with a sweet, lingering finish.

beans.name: Pedro Moreno
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: The roaster's debut lot from Pedro Moreno, a pioneer of Santa Bárbara's specialty scene who built his farm from under a hectare and earned several Cup of Excellence podiums. A washed SL28 with lively fruit and crisp acidity.

beans.name: Cumaccha
beans.producer: Santa Rosa, Colasay, Cajamarca; Chacra Coffee smallholders; Typica, Caturra, Catimor; 1,700-2,000m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: Grown by smallholders in Cajamarca, opening with tropical mango and pineapple, then blueberry sweetness and a zesty rhubarb note as it cools. Bright but balanced acidity, soft rounded body and lingering fruity sweetness.

beans.name: Samusure
beans.producer: Nyamasheke, Lake Kivu; family farm; Red Bourbon; 1,800-2,000m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A washed Red Bourbon from Nyamasheke, Rwanda, grown at about 1,800-2,000 metres and dried on raised beds. Orange, nectarine and blackberry sweetness with a tea-like, smoky finish. Light-medium roast for filter or espresso.

beans.name: Halo Beriti
beans.producer: Gedeb, Yirgacheffe; Halo Beriti washing station; Typica, Heirloom; 1,900-2,300m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: From smallholders in Gedeb's Ethiopian highlands, fermented without oxygen then dried on raised beds. A juicy cup of strawberry, kiwi and tinned pineapple, with smooth texture and a lingering tropical aftertaste.

beans.name: Gaturiri AA
beans.producer: Kibugu, Embu / Nyeri; Barichu Farmers Cooperative; SL28, SL34; 1,600-1,800m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: Grown by about 1,500 smallholders in Nyeri's cool volcanic highlands, washed and sun-dried. Juicy berry, floral elderflower and zesty citrus, with lively acidity and a tidy, sweet finish.

beans.name: Aftermath
beans.producer: Alfenas, Minas Gerais; Huila; Red and Yellow Catuai, Caturra, Castillo, Bourbon
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, Maple syrup, Sugarcane, Florentine
beans.desc: A lively blend of a natural-process Brazil and a washed Colombia: chocolate-coated nuts, bright citrus peel and rich sweetness with a lingering, juicy complexity.

beans.name: Lucid Trance (Decaf)
beans.producer: Popayan (Colombia); Huehuetenango (Guatemala); Gesha, Caturra, Typica, Bourbon, Castillo
beans.listedNotes: Caramel fudge, Praline, Quince, Creme brulee
beans.desc: A decaf blend pitched as nothing like old decaf: a washed Colombian with caramel and praline and a high-altitude Guatemalan with quince and creme brulee, both sugarcane-decaffeinated.

beans.name: Maverick
beans.producer: Oaxaca (Mazatec families); Huila; Typica, Bourbon, Castillo, Tabi
beans.desc: The roaster's 'killer espresso blend': shade-grown Oaxaca coffee from Mazatec families with hand-picked coffee from small high-altitude Huila plots worked by women; dark chocolate, cherry and demerara sugar.

beans.name: Utopia
beans.producer: Nogales Farm (decaf lot); Las Planadas, Huila (Castillo)
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry milkshake, White peach, Acacia honey
beans.desc: A smooth blend pairing Nogales Farm's mosto-fermentation decaf with a washed Castillo from Las Planadas, Huila; strawberry milkshake and white peach with a lingering acacia-honey sweetness.

beans.name: One Piece
beans.desc: Boundary-pushing processing with effortless balance: Jairo Arcila's dragonfruit co-fermented Castillo with a syrupy Las Planadas Castillo; dragonfruit, bubblegum and celeste fig, expressive and clean.

beans.name: Ipanema
beans.producer: Two Brazilian lots; Yellow Bourbon, Red Catuai
beans.desc: Classic Brazilian sweetness with modern specialty character, blending a chocolate, hazelnut and caramel Brazil with a brighter citrus and red-fruit one; layered and approachable.

beans.name: Peach Black
beans.processFull: Peach and wine yeast co-ferment; natural
beans.desc: Two ideas of fruit in coffee: a peach co-fermented Colombian Castillo with a natural Ugandan lot from the Rwenzori Mountains; stone fruit, dark cherry and chocolate that start bright and turn richer.

beans.name: Third Rail
beans.producer: Bekele Kachara, Sidama; Gregorio Espinosa, San Antonio de Chinizo
beans.listedNotes: Ube ice cream, Forest honey, Pecan pie
beans.desc: Ethiopian fruit and floral intensity meets Latin American experimentation: a natural Sidama with a criomacerated Peruvian Catuai; ube ice cream, forest honey and pecan pie.

beans.name: Limited Release #04
beans.desc: A small boxed release of a natural Starmaya, a rare hybrid from El Salvador, chosen by longtime partner Tomas. Floral aromas, a nutty, creamy character and a sweet, lasting chocolatey finish.

beans.name: Revival Classic Blend
beans.producer: Fazenda Sertao and Mantiqueira (Brazil); Gaitania, Tolima (Colombia); Los Andes (El Salvador)
beans.desc: A velvety, cocoa-toned blend with deep character and lingering aftertaste, drawing on classic Italian espresso tradition. Works in domestic espresso machines and moka pots, pairing ethical, open sourcing with nostalgic café feel.

beans.name: Ranmore Signature Blend
beans.producer: Fazenda Sertao and Mantiqueira (Brazil); Gaitania, Tolima (Colombia); Los Andes (El Salvador)
beans.desc: The flagship blend: dark chocolate, caramel and walnut in a silky, rich cup. Roasted medium-dark as an everyday coffee for espresso, filter or cafetière.

beans.name: Brazil Fazenda Sertao
beans.desc: A dependable, hearty Brazilian single origin with sweet, cocoa-like, nutty flavour. Praline, hazelnut and chocolate bar notes, balanced and mellow black, with sweetness becoming more pronounced in milk.

beans.name: Guatemala Finca Medina
beans.desc: A washed Guatemalan tasting sweet like dark chocolate, with bright orange hints. Smooth and even, making it flexible whether brewed as filter or pulled as espresso.

beans.name: Colombia Finca Las Cruces
beans.producer: Quinchia, Risaralda; Finca Las Cruces (Esnayder Cuartas)
beans.desc: A medium-roast Colombian from the Cuartas-Alvarez family's Finca Las Cruces: sweet and lively, with chocolate, toffee and bright grape. Well suited to filter.

beans.name: Indonesia Mandheling
beans.producer: North Sumatra, Lake Toba highlands; smallholders
beans.desc: A deeply roasted Indonesian with flavours of rooibos, cosy spices and gentle tobacco. Strong, heavy body and soil-like character give way to a silky, easy finish.

beans.name: Uganda Bukonzo Dream
beans.desc: Grown at high elevation by small-scale Ugandan farmers and naturally processed. A lively, even cup with bright, juicy acidity, sweet berry-like flavours and a silky, tidy aftertaste.

beans.name: El Salvador El Cipres
beans.producer: Ilamatepec / Santa Ana volcano; Don Tomas; Bourbon; 1,600-1,700m
beans.desc: From El Salvador, with gentle tropical fruit, berry sweetness and a touch of cola. Sweet, even and well rounded, a versatile pick for filter and espresso.

beans.name: Ethiopia Guji Shakiso
beans.desc: A light-roast Ethiopian with subtle bergamot-like tea flavours and lively citrus brightness. Sweet, smooth texture, graceful and fragrant; suits drip filters and manual pour-over.

beans.name: Kenya Ngoe AB
beans.producer: Ngoe Farm, Murang'a / Nyeri (Dr Helen Gichohi); SL28, Ruiru 11, Batian
beans.desc: Dr Helen Gichohi grows this washed Kenyan at Ngoe Farm. A lively, juicy cup with red berry and citrus flavours, layered acidity and a silky, wine-like finish that lingers.

beans.name: Natural Decaf
beans.producer: Popayan, Cauca; producer group of ~75 growers; 1,700m
beans.desc: A Colombian decaf with mellow chocolate and malt, a sweet, even profile and crisp aftertaste. Decaffeinated by a sugarcane-based method, well suited to espresso or French press.

beans.name: Half Caf
beans.producer: Decaf component from Cauca producer group
beans.desc: Chocolate and caramel sweetness with a smooth, even finish. Equal parts Ranmore Signature Blend and naturally decaffeinated coffee, giving rich flavour with about half the caffeine of a standard cup.

beans.name: Odds & Ends Blend
beans.desc: A waste-cutting blend using coffee that would otherwise be discarded. Not freshly roasted, but still flavourful and good with any brew method; a mix of the roastery's specialty beans, roasted and combined.

beans.name: Donut Jam - Kenya
beans.producer: Muthuthi-ini factory, Kirinyaga; SL28, SL34, Ruiru 11; 1,560-1,650m
beans.desc: A washed Kenyan peaberry, the rounder single-seed bean, from farmers supplying the Muthigi-ini factory. Light roasted for a lively, juicy cup of raspberry jam, wafer biscuit and sweet pastry.

beans.name: Go Go Juice - Burundi
beans.desc: A light-roast natural red bourbon from many small Kayanza farmers in Burundi. Cherries are floated, sorted and dried slowly for weeks; the washing station supplies growers with seedlings and compost. Strawberry yogurt, iced sweets and chamomile.

beans.name: Static Cherry - Ethiopia
beans.producer: Megadu, Guji; Bette Buna; 74112, 74110, Wild Guji Megadu
beans.listedNotes: Cherry syrup, Orange wine, Um Bongo
beans.desc: An Ethiopian natural from Bette Buna's Megadu site in Guji. Cherries dry a day on covered beds, then ferment four days in sealed, oxygen-free containers, giving a deep, rich cup of cherry syrup and orange wine.

beans.name: Juicy Pants - Colombia
beans.producer: El Portal, Palestina, Huila; Yoiner Mosquera; Geisha; 1,700m
beans.desc: A light-roast natural Geisha from Yoiner Mosquera's farm in Palestina, Huila, settled by his grandfather in 1949. Yoiner left banking to run the estate after his father died. Mango, jelly beans and hibiscus.

beans.name: Fizzy Drop - Ethiopia
beans.desc: From the Worka Wuri washing station near Gedeb, grown high from heirloom varieties and sun-dried about two weeks. A juicy, floral cup with jasmine, lemonade and parma violet notes.

beans.name: Liquid Amber - Guatemala
beans.desc: A fully specialty-grade Guatemalan from producer Elmer Meléndez. Anaerobic natural processing gives a rich, indulgent profile layered with blackberry, port wine and dark chocolate.

beans.name: Waffle Wizard - Honduras COMSA
beans.producer: COMSA collective; Parainema, Lempira, Typica, Ihcafe 90; 1,250-1,700m
beans.desc: A washed Honduran from COMSA, a producer group founded in 2001 with over 1,500 farmers. Members focus on organic farming, hand-pick ripe cherries, then ferment, wash and dry them on raised beds.

beans.name: Highwire Coffee Blend
beans.desc: The roaster's flagship blend, built to work as espresso and as a smooth, satisfying filter. It pairs a Brazilian coffee with a Ugandan one, each roasted to bring out its best.

beans.name: Temple Arches Dark Roast Blend
beans.desc: A dark-roast blend giving the deep, full-bodied richness dark roasts are known for, without the usual harshness. It reflects the roaster's own distinctive take on dark roasting.

beans.name: CaraNut Swirl - Brazil
beans.producer: Fazenda Mio, Monte Santo de Minas (Freitas family); Bourbon, Catuai; 900-1,000m
beans.desc: From Fazenda Mió in Monte Santo de Minas, a high-altitude, women-led Brazilian estate focused on sustainability. Satellite imagery traces each lot, and a third of the land is preserved forest.

beans.name: Cola Comforts - Colombia
beans.producer: Northern Tolima; CDNT collective; Castillo, Colombia
beans.desc: Organically grown cherries are hand-sorted, pulped, fermented, washed and dried 10-18 days in curved greenhouses. The result is a tidy cup that reflects the strength of small farming families in Planadas.

beans.name: Mellow Moon - Colombia Decaf
beans.producer: Huila, Tolima; smallholders; Castillo, Caturra, Colombia; 1,500-1,700m
beans.desc: A sweet, balanced decaf from small farms in Huila and Tolima, decaffeinated with ethyl acetate, a compound found in ripe fruit. Beans are steamed and soaked to remove about 97% of caffeine; residue is below banana levels.

beans.name: Value Blend - Everyday Coffee
beans.producer: Lucky dip of lots incl. natural gesha, natural Maragogype, washed typica
beans.desc: A budget-friendly, zero-waste blend of leftover coffee from past roasts, some up to eight weeks old, including natural gesha, natural Maragogype and washed typica. An everyday coffee that still tastes good.

beans.name: Old Chapel Signature
beans.producer: Not shown (meta text says Uganda and Colombia)
beans.desc: The 2024 charity coffee, with profits going to Old Chapel Music CIC, a Leeds rehearsal studio that has helped launch bands and offers music education to disadvantaged people. Praline, chocolate and nougat.

beans.name: The Baron (Bruno's Pick): Fazenda Inhame
beans.producer: Fazenda Inhame, Campos Altos, Cerrado Mineiro (Fiorita Franco family); Catuai, Mundo Novo
beans.desc: A Brazilian espresso sourced through partner Bruno de Souza from Fazenda Inhame in Minas Gerais. Grown at high elevation, it offers chocolate and nut flavours with gentle sweetness, suiting milk or black.

beans.name: The Estate: Fero
beans.producer: Fero washing station, Sidamo (Ranger Coffee); mixed heirloom
beans.desc: Climpsons' flagship espresso, highlighting Ethiopia's finest traits: lively, even-keeled and intricate. Silky as black coffee, and in milk it tastes like a jaffa cake.

beans.name: Broadway Blend
beans.producer: Las Ranas, Santa Ana (El Salvador); El Durazno, Jalapa (Guatemala); Bourbon, Typica
beans.processFull: El Salvador pulped natural; Guatemala honey
beans.desc: A seasonal blend made for everyday drinking, the flat white choice at Broadway Market. Two Central American coffees combine into a sweet, balanced cup with dried-fruit richness and acidity.

beans.name: The Fields: Santa Cruz
beans.producer: Finca Santa Cruz, Chiapas (Jose Arguello); Bourbon, Typica
beans.desc: A natural from Finca Santa Cruz in Chiapas, Mexico, grown by third-generation farmer José Argüello, who experiments with varieties and processing. Cherries ferment in sealed tanks, then dry slowly over about three and a half weeks.

beans.name: The Decaf: La Plata
beans.producer: La Plata, Huila; Crecert women-led cooperative; Caturra, Castillo, Colombia
beans.desc: A decaf the roasters jokingly call a placebo, chosen for taste and a more eco-friendly process. With about one in five drinkers worldwide choosing decaf, they give it full attention, and it often outshines others in tastings.

beans.name: Finca Grevillea
beans.producer: Marcala, La Paz; Melvin Calix and Victorina; Parainema, Anacafe 14, Icatu
beans.desc: From Melvin, a third-generation Marcala farmer who works with his mother to restore neglected land after rust hit. A mostly Parainema natural, hand-picked and sun-dried 15-25 days, with a harvest complicated by cooler weather.

beans.name: Uraga
beans.producer: Uraga Raro washing station, Guji; 400+ smallholders; heirloom (Dega, Wolisho)
beans.desc: A washed Ethiopian from Uraga, vivid and fruit-forward, shining as filter and also suiting cold brew. Typical tasting notes include peach, caramel and jasmine.

beans.name: El Witano
beans.producer: El Coyegual, San Antonio Huista, Huehuetenango (Marvin Soliz); Caturra; 1,650m
beans.desc: Grown by Marvin Soliz on his family's farm in the Huehuetenango highlands. Slow-maturing in cool mountain air, this washed lot gives bright, fruity sweetness rather than the chocolate and nut Guatemala is known for.

beans.name: Village Organic
beans.listedNotes: Malted milk biscuits, Peanut butter, 80% dark chocolate

beans.name: Sundown
beans.listedNotes: Black cherry, Baker's chocolate, Earl Grey

beans.name: Mexico - Sierra Mazateca
beans.listedNotes: Orange peel, Dandelion and burdock, Maple syrup

beans.name: Brazil | Cafe Delas, COOPFAM
beans.producer: Poco Fundo, Sul de Minas; Cafe Delas female smallholders; Catuai, Mundo Novo, Topazio
beans.desc: A bold South American coffee from near Poço Fundo with full body, dark chocolate and caramelised sugar. Suits filter and single-origin espresso; part of each sale's profit funds gender-equality programmes for women farmers.

beans.name: Colombia | Planadas
beans.producer: Planadas, South Tolima; 1,042 growers in 23 groups; Colombia, Castillo, Caturra
beans.desc: A Planadas lot from Tolima in Colombia's Central Andes, a region the roaster has sourced from for five years. Local growers use time-honoured methods; past conflict left some areas underserved, and specialty markets are now opening doors.

beans.name: Decaf Colombia
beans.producer: Huila and Tolima; Castillo, Caturra, Colombia
beans.desc: A popular decaf that keeps plenty of flavour despite gentle, chemical-light decaffeination. Grown in Huila and Tolima, with chocolate, redcurrant and lime, and about 97-99% caffeine free.

beans.name: Guatemala | Magdalena Camaja Cafe Delas
beans.producer: Cubulco, Baja Verapaz; Magdalena Camaja Cafe Delas; Catimor, Caturra, Marsellesa, Parainema, Sarchimor
beans.desc: A washed Guatemalan from Magdalena Camaja with caramel-glazed apple, malt and cocoa. Part of a scheme sourcing only from female growers, with profits reinvested in gender-equality work and childcare and schooling during harvest.

beans.name: Guatemala | Blue Ayarza - Natural
beans.producer: Lake Ayarza, Santa Rosa; smallholders; Bourbon, Catuai, Pache, Anacafe14, San Ramon
beans.desc: A natural from growers around the Ayarza mill in Santa Rosa. The mill buys ripe cherries and processes them centrally, drying on a sunny hillside then in a mechanical dryer, improving acidity and avoiding rain damage.

beans.name: Indonesia | Cahayani Gayo
beans.producer: Gayo Highland, Aceh; Ara Cahayani Gayo co-op (~500 smallholders); Gayo 1, 2, 3
beans.desc: A wet-hulled Sumatran from a cooperative in Aceh's Gayo Highlands, with chocolate, lemonade and nut notes. Cherries are hand-picked, pulped, fermented overnight, sun-dried, hulled, dried further and hand-sorted.

beans.name: Papua New Guinea | Kongo B
beans.desc: From Kongo Coffee, a locally owned exporter in Simbu, Papua New Guinea, supporting small farmers since before 2000. Its Simbu Project pays 20% above market plus quality bonuses and funds local schools and roads.

beans.name: Peru | San Ignacio
beans.producer: San Ignacio; COOPAFSI; Bourbon, Catimor, Catucai, Caturra, Pache, Typica, Mundo Novo
beans.desc: From COOPAFSI, a cooperative founded in 1968 uniting sixteen committees of small growers across several districts. It helps them reach buyers and provides social and microfinance support, aiming for sustainable, internationally recognised farming.

beans.name: Rwanda | Huye Mountain
beans.producer: Huye District; David and Family Mill; Bourbon
beans.desc: Founded in 2012 by David Rubanzangabo, Huye Mountain supports over 1,300 growers with training and small loans for equipment and inputs. Cherries are hand-sorted, density-separated in water, then sun-dried on raised beds for three to four weeks.

beans.name: Rwanda | Sholi Single Mothers lot
beans.producer: Muhanga, Cyeza; Aba Sholi Women's Co-op; Bourbon; 1,800-2,000m
beans.desc: From an all-female collective within a co-operative started in 2008 by thirty women in Muhanga; it now has 721 members and supports local schools and healthcare. A high-grown washed Bourbon reflecting that community focus.

beans.name: Uganda | Rwenzori Mountains
beans.producer: Kalingwe, Rwenzori; Agri Evolve (350+ farms), Kisinga station; SL14, SL28, Catimor; 1,500-1,800m
beans.desc: Uganda has built a strong specialty reputation. The roasters visited the Rwenzori Mountains and have sourced here for five seasons; small growers on the southern slopes sell to a local station and are paid fairly.

beans.name: East Gate | Light Roast Blend
beans.desc: A light-roast blend of Brazilian, Colombian and Ugandan coffees with caramel, milk chocolate and stone fruit. Retains brightness and sweetness, suiting milky drinks while shining in cafetière or AeroPress.

beans.name: Jacob's Well | Medium Roast Blend
beans.producer: Ara Cahayani Gayo (Bener Meriah); Finca Buena Vista, La Entrada; Marsellesa
beans.processFull: Indonesia wet hulled; Nicaragua anaerobic natural
beans.desc: A medium-roast blend of two specialty coffees with bold body that holds up in milk. Walnut, caramelised toffee and dark cocoa, with a fuller, longer finish tempering the sweetness of the lighter blends.

beans.name: Solomon's Porch | Fairtrade Blend
beans.producer: Aba Sholi Kundwa women's co-op; San Ignacio; Planadas
beans.desc: Named for a temple gathering place open to everyone, a dependable daily blend of Fair Trade beans from Rwanda, Peru and Colombia, showing chocolate, nut and plum.

beans.name: Fireside | Dark Roast Blend
beans.desc: A blend for black coffee drinkers, built to shine alone since dark roasts can hide poor beans. 100% arabica from Brazil, Peru and Colombia, tasting of milk chocolate, almond and butterscotch.

beans.name: Brazil
beans.desc: A Brazilian that's a roastery favourite: moderate in strength and richness with a nicely harmonised flavour. Versatile across brew methods and pleasant at any time of day.

beans.name: Colombia
beans.desc: A Colombian showing the well-rounded, rich profile the origin is known for, with typical chocolatey, nutty notes. Easygoing and hard to brew badly, so use whichever method you like.

beans.name: El Salvador
beans.desc: An El Salvador with rich body, plenty of flavour and gentle acidity, capturing the origin's mellow sweetness. Recommended as a strong choice for flat whites.

beans.name: Honduras Abeja Honey
beans.desc: A honey-processed lot from the Capucas collective in Honduras, grown at one of the country's highest elevations among local beekeepers and their hives. Only 100 bags were produced, so it sells out quickly.

beans.name: India
beans.desc: A single origin packed with spice, smoke and dark chocolate, a roastery favourite. India was among the first origins shipped to the UK. Suited to a leisurely weekend brew in a French press.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf
beans.roastNote: "Rainbow roast" mix of light, medium, dark
beans.desc: A decaf for those going caffeine-free, made with the Swiss Water method from South American beans. Roast levels range light to dark, so it suits any brewing approach. Honey, walnut and dark chocolate flavours.

beans.name: The Every Day Blend
beans.desc: A robust blend of the roaster's favourite coffees from South America, India and East Africa. Versatile enough for a bold morning brew or an after-dinner espresso.

beans.name: The Morning After Blend
beans.desc: Equal parts East African and Indonesian beans for a sharp, citrusy jolt aimed at groggy mornings. Good for recovering from a late night and makes a strong Americano.

beans.name: The Weekend Blend
beans.desc: A blend of quality beans from South America, India and East Africa for unwinding after a busy week or a relaxed weekend brunch. Chocolate, smoke and hazelnut flavours.

beans.name: Yorkshire Blend
beans.desc: Blended from South American, Indian and central African beans, with bold cocoa, smoke and hazelnut flavours for any time of day. Each sale also supports Herriot Hospice Homecare, which provides free end-of-life care at home.

beans.name: Fairtrade Italian Espresso
beans.desc: An espresso blend of 100% Fairtrade arabica from Brazil, Colombia, Ethiopia and Sumatra. Brazil and Colombia give generous crema and even flavour, Ethiopia a citrus lift, Sumatra body. Small-batch roasted, with almond, malt and cocoa notes.

beans.name: Fairtrade Peruvian
beans.producer: Puno, Tambopata and Inambari valleys; CECOVASA; Tipica, Caturra, Catimor; 800-2,000m
beans.desc: A Fairtrade single-origin arabica from Peru made for slow mornings. Gentle nut and toffee notes finish with a sugary, milky cocoa sweetness; smooth yet full-bodied and comforting.

beans.name: Fairtrade Brazilian Super Crema
beans.desc: An everyday blend of Fairtrade arabica and robusta from a Brazilian cooperative in Minas Gerais. Small-batch roasted, with nutty, caramel and dark chocolate notes, smooth body and lively acidity, suited to many brew methods.

beans.name: Fairtrade Honduran
