beans.desc: A Fairtrade single-origin 100% Arabica from a Honduran cooperative with over 700 members who gain fair pay and community support. Balanced and smooth, with hints of nuts and caramel, especially in milk.

beans.name: Fairtrade South American House Blend
beans.desc: A house blend of Fairtrade Brazilian and Honduran beans, roasted in small batches. Brazil brings a zesty edge, Honduras robust nuttiness and a velvety finish. Nut, toast and spicy liquorice notes.

beans.name: Fairtrade Colombian
beans.processFull: Handpicked, fermented, dried on beds and patios
beans.desc: A classic dark-roast Colombian, sweet and fruity in the Medellín style. 100% Arabica, low in acidity, from smallholder farms through local cooperatives and sourced with ethics and sustainability in mind.

beans.name: Fairtrade Ethiopian Sidamo
beans.desc: A Fair Trade Ethiopian from high-altitude Sidamo, where farmers intercrop with shade trees. A bright, fruity medium roast with citrus hints, small-batch roasted for freshness.

beans.name: Fairtrade Organic Swiss Water Peruvian Decaf
beans.desc: A Fairtrade organic decaf with nutty peanut and chocolate notes and subtle citrus, decaffeinated by the chemical-free Swiss Water method. From the Cenfrocafe co-op in northern Peru, where Fairtrade helped growers build processing facilities and go organic.

beans.name: Brazil Fazenda Pinhal
beans.desc: A mixed-harvest Brazilian dried with the cherry around the bean, giving the sweetness Brazil is known for. Bright fruit over creamy cocoa, ending in toasted nuts. Medium roast makes it smooth and balanced, especially as espresso.

beans.name: Colombia ACC - Attia Castillo
beans.producer: Piendamo, Cauca; ACC co-op community lot
beans.desc: A distinctive honey-processed Colombian with zesty lime and tart green apple, dark chocolate notes and a crisp, bittersweet finish reminiscent of tonic water. Light roast suits pour-over; medium suits espresso and cafetière.

beans.name: Colombia Atunkaa Sugarcane Decaf
beans.producer: Piendamo, Cauca; ACC; sourced by Siruma
beans.desc: A naturally processed sugarcane decaf from a small association in Piendamó, Cauca. Caffeine is gently removed with ethyl acetate at Descafecol, preserving sweetness. Balanced and easy-drinking with apple, lemon and milk chocolate.

beans.name: Costa Rica Los Cipreses Geisha
beans.producer: West Valley; Los Cipreses (Max Salazar); Geisha

beans.name: Guatemala La Bolsa
beans.producer: La Libertad, Huehuetenango; Finca La Bolsa; Caturra, Bourbon
beans.desc: A washed Guatemalan from La Bolsa farm at 1,800 metres, grown from Caturra and Bourbon. Juicy blackberry and bright apple lead into mellow caramel and milk chocolate, with black tea adding structure and a sweet finish.

beans.name: Ethiopia Guji G1 Fruit Jam
beans.desc: A lively natural from Megadu in Guji with cherry, blueberry and ripe mango, crisp acidity, thick sweetness and a dark chocolate finish. A 120-hour low-oxygen fermentation intensifies the fruit. Medium suits espresso, lighter suits pour-over.

beans.name: Kenya Gatomboya
beans.producer: Gatomboya washing station; SL28, SL34, Ruiru 11
beans.desc: A washed Kenyan of SL28, SL34 and Ruiru 11: bright, citrusy and sweet, with pink grapefruit, baked apple and smooth toffee. Medium roast suggested for espresso, lighter for fruity pour-over.

beans.name: Black Gold No.3
beans.producer: Fazenda do Salto, Sul de Minas (Catuai); Finca Serbia, Ilamatepec (Bourbon)
beans.desc: The roaster's first blend and the heart of the business: an award-winning seasonal espresso designed for wide appeal and served daily in their café. Roasted past first crack for a lively, chocolatey, biscuity taste.

beans.name: Candle Light No.1
beans.desc: A house espresso whose bean origins rotate through the seasons to keep its character consistent. Deep dark chocolate with a faint hint of toffee, for those who prize richness.

beans.name: Anthracite No.2
beans.producer: Rwenzori Mountains; SL14, SL28; Agri Evolve
beans.desc: A natural-process espresso with juicy, fruit-forward character, aiming for flavours you wouldn't normally link with coffee. Lively and layered, with fruit, blossom and wine-like notes; a three-star Great Taste Award winner.

beans.name: The Union No.4
beans.desc: The roaster's first blend designed for filter, refined over months of tasting at its Ammanford roastery. Sourced from Uganda's Mount Elgon, with gentle sweetness, mid-weight body and notes of blackcurrant, orange and cocoa.

beans.name: Drifft No.6 Half Caff
beans.producer: Muungano, South Kivu (decaf); Fazenda do Salto (natural)
beans.desc: A half-caff blend of beans from two farms: smooth and balanced with about half the caffeine, for a calm, steady day without jittery peaks or crashes. The name mixes Welsh heritage with a nod to a drift mine entrance.

beans.name: Jenkin Jones Decaf No.5
beans.producer: Simbu / Eastern Highlands; smallholders; Typica, Bourbon
beans.desc: A decaf named for a Welsh coal figure, blending beans from Simbu and the Eastern Highlands of Papua New Guinea. Water-based decaffeination; limestone soils add structure and volcanic earth richness. A mellow, polished cup.

beans.name: Catanduva
beans.producer: Fazenda Catanduva, Cerrado Mineiro (Marie Nakao); Catuai, Bourbon; 1,000m
beans.desc: A natural from a third-generation Brazilian family farm in the high Cerrado at about 1,000 metres, whose grandparents emigrated from Japan. Orange, molasses and cashew chocolate notes.

beans.name: Nguguini PB
beans.producer: Kirinyaga; Nguguini factory, Kibirigwa; SL28, SL34, Ruiru 11, Batian; 1,600m+
beans.desc: A lively Kenyan peaberry washed lot from a cooperative-linked factory in Kirinyaga above 1,600 metres. Sweet blackcurrant, gentle chamomile and zesty tamarillo, with bright acidity and a long, tidy aftertaste.

beans.name: El Oso
beans.desc: A Peruvian grown high in San Ignacio by an organic cooperative that helps protect spectacled bear forest. Blackberry, cacao nibs and agave; sweet and lively as filter, thick and fruity as espresso.

beans.name: Unearthed Vol 3 - Orange Bourbon
beans.processFull: Washed, yeast inoculation and thermal shock
beans.desc: The third Unearthed release, a single origin from Edinson Argote's Quebraditas farm in Huila, Colombia. Positioned as a homage to scarce coffees, blending story, terroir and craft for adventurous newcomers and experts alike.

beans.name: Matazano
beans.producer: Finca El Matazano (Elvin Castillo); Lempira, Ihcafe 90; 1,400-1,450m
beans.desc: From a 5-hectare Honduran farm at about 1,450 metres, shaded by timber and fruit trees, produced by national cupper Elvin Castillo. Cherries rest a day and a half, then dry ten days on raised beds, giving a sweet, clear, layered cup.

beans.name: Finca Serbia
beans.producer: El Congo near Lake Coatepeque (Fernando Lima); Bourbon; 1,000m
beans.desc: From a farm founded in 1930 near El Salvador's Santa Ana volcano, on nutrient-rich volcanic soil. Cedar, oak and balsam shade help against intense sun, and rust-resistant varieties spared the estate the 2012 outbreak.

beans.name: Deep Winter
beans.producer: Cerro San Juan, Nayarit; Grupo Terruno Nayarita; Bourbon, Catuai
beans.desc: A warming seasonal coffee with chocolate, caramel and brown sugar notes, grown by cooperative farms on volcanic slopes near Cerro San Juan in Nayarit, Mexico. A smooth, sweet option for chilly days.

beans.name: Candy Cane
beans.desc: A festive seasonal coffee, lively and cheerful, with juicy citrus, mellow sweet pear and cosy wine-like warmth. Zesty brightness meets tender fruit and soothing spice for a joyful holiday cup.

beans.name: House Blend
beans.origin: Brazil and others (Cerrado Mineiro, Bahia, Santa Rosa)
beans.desc: A modern take on a traditional house-style blend whose recipe shifts with the seasons while staying silky, chocolatey and indulgent. Cocoa, sweet citrus peel and toffee; works with or without milk.

beans.name: Brazil
beans.listedNotes: 65% cocoa milk chocolate, Tropical fruit, Shortbread
beans.desc: Bahia's high-elevation growers have ideal conditions but wet harvest weather makes drying hard, so many truck their cherries about 50 km to the drier Caatinga. The fruit ferments briefly in the enclosed truck, giving a fruity, sweet cup.

beans.name: Colombia El Buho EA Decaf
beans.origin: Colombia (page region field says Minas Gerais, Brazil)
beans.producer: Near Caparao National Park; Catuai, Pache, Bourbon
beans.listedNotes: 65% cocoa milk chocolate, Ripe cherry, Toffee

beans.name: Guatemala
beans.producer: Santa Rosa, Ayarza mill; Catuai, Pache, Bourbon
beans.listedNotes: Ripe citrus, Toffee, 65% cocoa milk chocolate
beans.desc: A washed Guatemalan from a central cherry mill in Ayarza that pays extra for ripe fruit from many local growers, easing the consistency problems of small-farm processing. Producer Francisco Nájera, 30, with under a hectare, is one of them.

beans.name: Papua New Guinea Arufa AX
beans.desc: Grown in Jiwaka Province, this natural starts as cherries from the Kindeng mill. Monpi selects the best and sun-dries them for a month before hulling. Bright acidity and full body with dark berries, honey, stone fruit and caramel.

beans.name: Ethiopia Worka Sakaro
beans.producer: Worka Gedeb; Worka Sakaro washing station; Heirloom
beans.listedNotes: Wild blueberry, Red grape, 65% cocoa milk chocolate
beans.desc: A top-tier small-batch Ethiopian from the Worka Sakaro processing site in the Worka community, Gedeb. Its natural-process cherries underwent an extended three-day fermentation sealed in vacuum bags.

beans.name: Ethiopia Tigst Boru Kochere
beans.listedNotes: Peach crumble, 65% cocoa milk chocolate, Dried apricot
beans.desc: A premium fully washed Kochere lot from the Worka Gedeb region, made from heirloom varietals and ranked among the roaster's top lots.

beans.name: The Battersea Blend
beans.producer: Typica, Bourbon, Batian, SL28, Catuai, Ruiru 11, Pache
beans.desc: An award-winning blend of Malawi, Guatemala and Papua New Guinea for a lively, harmonious brew. Juicy citrus, mango and blueberry, softened by deep chocolatey richness and a buttery biscuit finish.

beans.name: Ethiopia Supernatural
beans.desc: An Ethiopian with lush, jam-like stone fruit alongside floral and chocolate hints and a rich, smooth mouthfeel. Cherries dehydrate slowly in deep beds within partially permeable enclosures, deepening fermentation for a sweeter, more layered cup.

beans.name: Tanzania Ibero PB
beans.desc: From Tanzania's Jipemoyo district, washed using traditional methods and a Great Taste winner. A berry-led tang of blackcurrant and gooseberry settles into a creamy toffee finish.

beans.name: Heritage Blend
beans.producer: Sumatra Lintong; Monsoon Malabar; Santos Mantiqueira
beans.desc: Blended by roasters Jason and Eric to mark founder John Green's retirement after 45 years in the trade. Three origins give earthy depth, gentle spice and natural sweetness; medium-dark, warm and smooth with walnut and biscuit.

beans.name: Cafe Creme
beans.desc: The company's signature espresso, based on a recipe founder John Green found about forty years ago. Versatile and easy to pull, giving a robust shot that suits milk. The best seller, always roasted fresh.

beans.name: Brazilian & Costa Rica 80/20
beans.desc: A smooth yet sophisticated blend of Brazilian Daterra beans from Petit Soleil with all-Arabica Costa Rican. Deep cocoa and treacle with a lively sparkle; an Italian-style espresso for cafés and home machines.

beans.name: Hamburg Roast
beans.desc: Roasted a little darker than medium, blending Brazil, India and Ethiopia. Balanced acidity, chocolate and caramel, and a smooth, full body make it good for espresso and an excellent flat white.

beans.name: Mocha Italian
beans.desc: A popular café-style espresso without robusta, for a distinctly Italian character. 100% Arabica from Colombia, Mysore and Ethiopia: full body, low acidity, clean finish, chocolate and caramel; good with milk.

beans.name: Italia Creme
beans.desc: An espresso blend of nine parts Arabica to one part Indian cherry Robusta, giving a rich, aromatic cup with full body, creamy texture and golden crema. Balances intensity, aroma and bitterness.

beans.name: Papua New Guinea
beans.producer: Aiyura Valley, Eastern Highlands; Sero Dan Bebes, Besser farm
beans.desc: From Sero Dan Bebes' 40-hectare Eastern Highlands farm, where cool air, volcanic soil and slow ripening add complexity. Blue Mountain and Typica trees grow under native Casuarina shade. Suits many brew methods, best as espresso.

beans.name: Ethiopian Yirgacheffe
beans.desc: Grown chemical-free by Yohanes Ageze and family on their 4-hectare farm in Idido. Only ripe red cherries are hand-picked and hand-sorted, then dried on raised beds for two weeks.

beans.name: Ethiopian Sidamo
beans.listedNotes: Sweet, Floral, Full body, Low acidity
beans.desc: A washed Sidamo from southern Ethiopia, grown high with ample rain and fertile soil. Full body, sweet layered flavours, gentle acidity and a flowery scent; versatile for filter, espresso or milk, and the boss's favourite.

beans.name: Guatemala (Black Honey)
beans.desc: A Guatemalan processed by the Black Honey method, leaving fruit residue on the beans as they dry. Sweeter and richer, with berry, citrus and caramel, full silky body and bright acidity.

beans.name: Rwanda
beans.producer: Rebero lot, Kinini washing station (633 farmers); Bourbon; 1,973-2,250m
beans.desc: A Rebero lot from 633 farmers supplying the Kinini washing station on north-facing slopes above 1,973 metres. Cherries arrive the day they're picked and are repeatedly fermented and soaked before drying, giving a crisp cup.

beans.name: Andean Sisters - Peru
beans.desc: Grown on small farms in Peru's Cajamarca highlands. Smooth and balanced with chocolate and nutty notes and gentle brightness; good as espresso, in milk drinks or as filter.

beans.name: Decaf (Colombia)
beans.desc: One of the roaster's favourite decafs, equally good as espresso or filter, with low acidity and full, rich body. Caffeine is removed with steam and a solvent, then re-steamed and roasted, leaving no chemical trace.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf (Peru)
beans.desc: A decaf using the organic, chemical-free method first developed in Switzerland in the 1930s. A concentrated green-coffee liquid draws out only the caffeine, so the beans keep their original taste.

beans.name: Liberatrix - Gran Colombia
beans.desc: The long-standing flagship blend that launched the roaster's coffee journey. Large, high-grown Colombian beans with Brazilian give a round, full-bodied cup with caramel, a zesty citrus finish and suitability for nearly any brew method.

beans.name: Regina - Santos
beans.desc: A blend of two Brazilian varieties: Oberon for creamy, nutty chocolate and Yellow Bourbon for sweet, fruity character. A smooth, low-acid cup with a pleasing finish, suited to press or filter.

beans.name: Mellow Mare - Mexico Mountain Water Decaf
beans.listedNotes: Cocoa, Praline, Brown sugar, Orange marmalade
beans.desc: A decaf from Veracruz processed at Descamex with Pico de Orizaba mountain water, removing caffeine without chemicals. Gentle, rounded body with sweet cocoa, light caramel and juicy fruit.

beans.name: Ethiopia - Yirgacheffe G2
beans.listedNotes: Forest fruits, Brown sugar, Citrus, Floral
beans.desc: A washed Yirgacheffe medium roast and team favourite: forest fruit, brown sugar and citrus, floral aroma and bright, juicy acidity. Suits filter and makes a distinctive espresso.

beans.name: Mexico - El Jaguar
beans.desc: A lush, silky Mexican with bittersweet cocoa and caramelised sugar flavours and a zesty citrus finish. Works as filter or strong espresso.

beans.name: Guatemala - Huehuetenango SCA 83+
beans.desc: A sweet, even-keeled Guatemalan with hints of ripe strawberry, rich chocolate and bright tropical fruit. Grown in frost-sheltered, clay-rich highlands; brews cleanly through filter or as espresso.

beans.name: Ethiopia - Guji
beans.desc: A wild, complex Guji with jammy blueberry, bright honey and zesty bergamot. Juicy and tea-like as filter, richly layered as espresso. Whole sun-dried cherries from high-altitude smallholders add intense fruitiness.

beans.name: Kenya - Gachika SCA 87
beans.producer: Gachika factory, Kimaratia FCS, Kiambu; SL28, SL34, Batian, Ruiru 11; 1,600-1,800m
beans.desc: A lively, layered Kenyan and roasters' favourite with juicy cherry, sweet aroma and crisp acidity. Works as pour-over and espresso.

beans.name: Colombian Bucaramanga
beans.desc: A Colombian from Bucaramanga, known for a rich, smooth character and layered flavour. A balanced, easygoing cup with cocoa-like warmth and subtle nutty sweetness that lingers.

beans.name: Ethiopian Yirgacheffe
beans.desc: A Yirgacheffe hand-harvested from small local farms, then washed and dried with care. Its fruity character suits all brew methods; the roaster recommends a morning filter to show its natural purity.

beans.name: Peruvian Tunki
beans.desc: An organic coffee from Peru's high Tambopata Valley, farmed by hand without chemicals by Quechua and Aymara families. Smooth and rich with chocolate, berry and nutty tones.

beans.name: Breakfast Favourite
beans.desc: A smooth, well-balanced blend with a long finish, moderate body and little spice. A bestseller roasted in large daily batches, good in milky drinks or black via paper filter, cafetière or drip.

beans.name: Guatemala El Fogon
beans.desc: A Guatemalan arabica with an easygoing, widely appealing cup: gentle spice, silky cocoa and faint berry scents. Softer body suits many methods, and the roastery uses it in three of its five blends.

beans.name: Costa Rican Tarrazu Valley
beans.desc: A Tarrazú coffee that's sweet, clean and beautifully balanced, especially for filter and AeroPress. The roaster credits strict national standards and supervised exports for its quality.

beans.name: Monsoon Malabar
beans.desc: An Indian coffee named for a slow drying process: beans rest in airy west-coast barns where damp monsoon sea winds swell them. Small-batch roasted, with espresso recommended.

beans.name: Everyday Espresso
beans.desc: An espresso blend for café-style taste without the harshness of robusta. 100% arabica from Brazil, Guatemala and Colombia, suited to espresso machines, filter or AeroPress, and to lattes and cappuccinos.

beans.name: Old Brown Java
beans.desc: Indonesian beans that once served as ship ballast. Aged green for at least two years, they deepen in flavour and lose acidity. A polarising, earthy, spicy cup with a long finish.

beans.name: Sumatra Mandheling
beans.desc: A Sumatran with blue-tinted, glossy beans grown on volcanic soil. A deep, intense cup with robust character and complexity, leaning toward cocoa, earth and warm spice.

beans.name: Italian Stallion Blend
beans.desc: An Italian-style blend of deeply roasted beans with robusta for those craving strength. Thick, velvety crema and deep cocoa character, holding up in lattes and cappuccinos with an extra caffeine lift.

beans.name: Nepalese Mount Everest - Nuwakot (Washed)
beans.desc: A single-estate Nepalese lot from Lekali Coffee Estate in Nuwakot, grown under shade and harvested mid-season. Washed with glacial meltwater, dry fermented, double-soaked and shade-dried for a layered, smooth, balanced cup.

beans.name: Roaster's Choice - Seasonal Crop
beans.desc: A rotating selection chosen by the roastery team: a mix of exceptional coffees that its roasters themselves drink most, each with its own character.

beans.name: Colombian Swiss Water Decaf
beans.desc: A Colombian decaf from the Bucaramanga region: smooth and clean with rich chocolate, gentle nutty sweetness and a well-rounded finish. Swiss Water decaffeination keeps the flavour intact.

beans.name: Mexico Siltepec El Jaguar
beans.producer: Chiapas; small producers; Catuai, Bourbon, Caturra; 1,250-1,350m
beans.desc: A long-time bestseller from a cooperative of small farmers growing at high elevation in Siltepec, Mexico. Roasted for a smooth, chocolate-forward cup without bitterness.

beans.name: Galapagos San Cristobal Hacienda El Cafetal
beans.desc: Grown in the Galápagos Islands, about 1,000 km off South America. Output is small, about half from volcanic San Cristóbal. A fragrant cup with caramel, chocolate, tobacco and spice.

beans.name: Nicaragua Blueberry & Pineapple Candy
beans.producer: Hacienda Santa Luz, La Bastilla; H3
beans.desc: A lively, experimental Nicaraguan with bold, fruit-led character: confectionery-like sweetness, a crisp, refined tang and layered berry and tropical notes from inventive processing.

beans.name: Kenya Kisii Estate Peaberry
beans.producer: South West Kenya near Lake Victoria; peaberry
beans.desc: A Kenyan peaberry from the south-west near Lake Victoria, an area of well-organised cooperatives. Washed and sun-dried, with blackcurrant and stone fruit, lively acidity and richness without harsh notes.

beans.name: Nicaraguan Jinotega - Community Project
beans.desc: A silky, lively Nicaraguan from Jinotega with milk chocolate and nutty flavours, brightened by gentle apricot sweetness, from small-scale growers favouring eco-minded methods.

beans.name: Ecuador Loja Co-operative
beans.desc: A freshly harvested Ecuadorian from a farmers' co-operative of small producers in Puyango, Loja. Zesty brightness, juicy body and notes of stone fruit and chocolate.

beans.name: Indonesia Kalossi Toraja Grade 1
beans.desc: A rare coffee grown on volcanic soil near Mount Sesean in Sulawesi, raised by ten Toraja families in small home gardens and processed by hand. Distinctive aroma, rich creamy body and subtle spice.

beans.name: Decaf Roaster's Choice - Seasonal Crop
beans.desc: A rotating decaf selected by the roastery team, who drink their favourites from the range themselves, with each month's crop bringing its own character.

beans.name: Sumatra Wahana Estate Rusana Natural
beans.desc: Dried inside the cherry, this Sumatran has a sweet brown-sugar character with rich spiced molasses notes, a lingering aftertaste and substantial mouthfeel.

beans.name: Colombia Finca Sofia Screen 19
beans.producer: Belen de Umbria, Risaralda; 30 small producers
beans.desc: Back in stock: a large, rich bean with heavy body, sweet banana toffee pie flavours and a silky finish, supplied by thirty small farmers in Colombia's western Andes.

beans.name: Zambia Keteshi Estate Mbuni Natural
beans.desc: A Zambian with a lively citrus-like tang that gives way to rich, liquor-tinged fruit as the brightness mellows. Full-bodied, typical of premium African beans, and a current house favourite.

beans.name: Peru Queromarca Community
beans.producer: Queromarca, Callayuc, Cajamarca; Aromas del Valle co-op (22 farmers)
beans.desc: A versatile cup with crisp profile and mild brightness: milk chocolate, gentle candied citrus and toffee. Good as filter and as espresso.

beans.name: Colombia Finca Las Mercedes La Isla
beans.producer: Southwest Antioquia; Finca Las Mercedes (Guerra family)
beans.processFull: Washed; double fermentation (25h anaerobic, 25h aerobic); African beds
beans.desc: A Finca Las Mercedes Caturra from high-altitude western Colombia, hand-picked and double-fermented before drying. Lively and sweet with plum and lemon, silky texture and clean finish.

beans.name: El Salvador Finca El Borbollon Red Bourbon
beans.producer: Santa Ana; Alvarez family; El Borbollon mill; Red Bourbon
beans.desc: Bright, lively acidity with full body and deep, rich flavour: milk chocolate and a hint of stone fruit. In milky espresso drinks it stays layered yet smooth, with caramel sweetness leading.

beans.name: Brazil Nossa Senhora da Aparecida Natural
Guatemala Finca El Platanillo Gesha Natural
beans.desc: A Gesha prized for quality, with berry and tropical fruit flavours and a sweet finish. Silky and lively; best as filter or cafetière, though a short ristretto also works.

beans.name: Mystery Coffee Mark 18
beans.desc: The roaster praises this coffee's estate and quality but keeps its origin, identity and flavour secret. The low price is subsidised, mimicking blind tasting and protecting farms from having produce sold cheaply under their names.

beans.name: Sweet Bourbon Espresso Blend
beans.origin: Not shown (Bourbon base with Asian coffees)
beans.desc: An espresso built to enhance crema and sweetness, using Bourbon beans as the base with unusual Asian coffees. Toffee, chocolate and almond with a sweet finish; the roastmaster often prefers it for lattes and cappuccinos.

beans.name: Mahogany Roast Malabar Hit
beans.producer: Monsoon Malabar base; Java Lingtong; Sidamo; Ipanema
beans.desc: Related to the Jampit Hit but darker and different in personality. Indian Monsoon Malabar gives full body and dark chocolate, malty, slightly spicy notes, mixed with three other origins. A dark roast for espresso or milk.

beans.name: Mahogany Roast Jampit Hit
beans.desc: A darker blend centred on full-bodied Java Jampit. Ethiopian Yirgacheffe adds blackcurrant fruit and acidity, Brazilian pulped natural a creamy texture. The deep roast stays mellow, with chocolate and citrus-tinged spice.

beans.name: Brighton Lanes Espresso Blend
beans.desc: Created for a Brighton café wanting less sharpness: deep, full flavour for espresso, filter, AeroPress and cafetière. 100% arabica from Brazil, Peru, India and Kenya, with smooth chocolate notes and mild acidity.

beans.name: Hill and Valley Espresso Blend
beans.desc: Created by a longtime friend of the Roastmaster, Charlie the Coffeeman, who favours bold Sumatran character. A quick, forceful roast draws out caramel and treacle that hold up in milk. The shop's top-selling dark espresso.

beans.name: Mediterranean Mocha Espresso
beans.desc: A distinctive, smooth, full-bodied espresso with subtle chocolate notes and rich crema, good straight or in milk drinks and long popular with cafés and home brewers.

beans.name: Mahogany Roast Sucker Punch Hit Decaf Blend
beans.desc: A darker, fuller decaf for drinkers wanting intensity: Swiss Water Sumatra with CO2-decaffeinated Ethiopian Sidamo. Sweet chocolate notes and a smoky, bold finish from its mahogany roast.

beans.name: Colombia Swiss Water Decaf
beans.desc: A Colombian decaffeinated by Swiss Water: beans soak in water with dissolved coffee compounds for about twelve hours, removing nearly all caffeine while preserving flavour. Nutty and sweet.

beans.name: Sumatra Swiss Water Decaf
beans.desc: A Sumatran decaffeinated by the chemical-free Swiss Water method, soaking about twelve hours to remove almost all caffeine. It copes well with the process, keeping its bold, earthy richness.

beans.name: Ethiopia Swiss Water Decaf
beans.desc: An Ethiopian Swiss Water decaf: premium beans steeped in caffeine-free liquid so the stimulant leaves and taste remains. Lively, zesty and flowery with traces of green tea and a light close.

beans.name: Costa Rica Swiss Water Decaf
beans.desc: A Costa Rican Swiss Water decaf, soaked about twelve hours in coffee-enriched water to remove nearly all caffeine. A crisp, tidy cup with full body, chocolatey hints and a lasting aftertaste.

beans.name: Guatemala El Hato CO2 Decaf
beans.producer: Finca El Hato, Santa Rosa (Verena de Rasch); 1,200-1,450m
beans.desc: Restocked decaf the roastery considers a match for its caffeinated coffees: a fully washed lot from El Hato in Santa Rosa. Candied citrus and mango, ending on caramel; smooth and very drinkable.

beans.name: Guatemala Swiss Water Decaf
beans.desc: A Guatemalan decaf made by soaking top beans in pure water about twelve hours, removing about 99% of the caffeine. Typical Guatemalan character: well rounded, lively acidity and delicate floral notes.

beans.name: 1984 Espresso Blend
beans.desc: The first product Coffee World released, dating from 1984 and still popular. Modelled on traditional Italian espresso, bold and sweet, like a cocoa drink with roasted nuts.

beans.name: Supremo Blend
beans.desc: Named for the Colombian Supremo bean at its core: gentle, silky and rich, with moderate, coating tartness giving way to chocolate biscuit and brown sugar. Versatile across brew styles.

beans.name: Fairtrade Artisan Blend
beans.desc: The best-selling espresso blend, 100% Fairtrade. Rich and soothing, with sweetness like smooth dark chocolate and caramel-dusted hazelnuts, for drinkers wanting a robust cup with gentle acidity.

beans.name: Blue Mountain Blend
beans.desc: Inspired by Jamaica's celebrated Blue Mountain coffee, offering similar appeal: rich, full body with thick caramel, bitter cocoa, subtle herbal undertones and cooked red fruit. Tasting it beside the real thing is suggested.

beans.name: Continental Blend
beans.desc: The deepest-roasted, sturdiest blend in the range, 100% Arabica from lower-elevation Brazil and Guatemala. Mellow sweetness and low acidity with bold, bittersweet dark cocoa and treacle, heavy-bodied with a punchy finish.

beans.name: House Blend
beans.desc: A signature everyday blend and longtime favourite, recommended as a silky, rich filter brew with cocoa, sweetness and gentle citrusy brightness evoking a fruit-and-nut chocolate.

beans.name: Brazil Brigadeiro
beans.producer: Mantiqueira de Minas; Santa Caterina (Marco Valerio Inacio Silva)
beans.desc: A single Brazilian farm's Arara coffee from a producer who keeps reinvesting in his land. Full and sweet, with cocoa, toasted nut and dried fruit balanced by fruit and acidity; suits espresso and filter.

beans.name: Brazil Minas Gerais
beans.desc: A Minas Gerais coffee; the region, whose name means 'General Mines', produces more than half of Brazil's coffee, and many farms have turned to modern irrigation to boost yield and quality.

beans.name: Colombia
beans.desc: From mountainous Bolívar, Colombia, grown at 1,200-2,600 metres in volcanic soil with heavy rain and a warm climate. Washed, medium roasted, with milk chocolate, caramel and green apple.

beans.name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe
beans.desc: An Ethiopian, from the country often seen as coffee's original home. Growers farm much as they did centuries ago, with some plants wild among forest trees and others cultivated in gardens.

beans.name: Mengesha Derso
beans.desc: A natural lot from Gedeo farmer Mengesha Derso on volcanic soil, one of the traceable single-farmer lots made possible by direct cooperative ties. Jasmine, lemon candy and apricot.

beans.name: Mexico Decaf
beans.desc: Small-scale growers in northern Chiapas, Mexico, deliver harvests to buying stations in San Cristóbal de las Casas and Yajalón. Farms sit at 900-1,100 metres, mostly planted with varieties that yield sizeable, smooth-textured beans.

beans.name: Guatemala
beans.desc: A Huehuetenango coffee: hot, dry Oaxacan air meets cool mountain breezes, creating microclimates that shield cherries from frost as they ripen slowly, adding sweetness and the region's chocolatey flavour.

beans.name: Honduras
beans.desc: From San Andrés in Lempira, a lesser-known Honduran area with volcanic soil and high farms. Growers process beans on their own land, so each lot reflects their choices. Spiced berry and rich dark chocolate.

beans.name: Uganda Masaba
beans.desc: A Ugandan from Masaba, contributing to the Friends of Mothers Initiative, which works to reduce gender-based pay inequality in Uganda's coffee trade with over 200 women across seven villages.

beans.name: Kenya Ruiru AA Mills Estate
beans.desc: A washed Kenyan from Sasini's 65-hectare Kiambu farm; the largely Kenyan-owned company provides housing, education and fair wages. Tangy blackcurrant, creamy butterscotch and a lively morello cherry finish.

beans.name: Burundi Shikankoni
beans.desc: Burundi has been a notable specialty producer since 1962. This year the roastery chose two favourite Bourbon lots from Shikankoni Hill, grown by smallholders and processed at partner mills.

beans.name: La Chumeca
beans.producer: San Pablo de Leon Cortes, Tarrazu; Beneficio La Chumeca
beans.desc: A light-roast Costa Rican from a family-run operation in Tarrazú founded in 2014 by Martín Ureña. Four farms supply it, with experienced pickers and regenerative methods. Honeydew, papaya and floral notes.

beans.name: Block Party
beans.desc: A blend that's sweet, tart and well balanced for filter, espresso or flat whites. Its sweetness comes from Paraná, Brazil, where volcanic soil, small family farms and cool seasons slow ripening, giving a rich, creamy cup.

beans.name: Amatillo Bioreactor
beans.producer: Pueblo Nuevo Vinas, Santa Rosa; Finca Amatillo
beans.desc: From a family farm between two Guatemalan volcanoes, fermented in a controlled bioreactor to encourage microbial activity. A lively, complex cup with rich tropical fruit and ripe banana, softened by orange-like sweetness.

beans.name: Jamaica Blue Mountain
beans.desc: A rare coffee from high in Jamaica's Blue Mountains, above 2,000 feet, with its own trademark. A regulator oversees every batch with strict quality checks.

beans.name: Y Fenai Rum Infused Coffee
beans.desc: A collaboration with Anglesey Rum Co: smooth, full-bodied speciality coffee with warm Anglesey rum character, named for the Menai Strait and roasted fresh in north Wales. For gifts, after-dinner sipping or everyday enjoyment.

beans.name: Porth yr Aur
beans.desc: An award-winning Huila single origin from careful farmers using fresh cultivation and processing methods. Medium-dark roasted: smooth and rich, balancing sweetness with depth.

beans.name: Castell Bach
beans.desc: A festive blend roasted medium in North Wales, with hints of dark fruit, zesty citrus and cocoa. Beans are grown at 1,500-2,000 metres, and it's sold only over Christmas while supplies last.

beans.name: Dros'r Aber
beans.producer: Kamwangi wet mill, Kirinyaga (New Ngariama FCS); Batian, Ruiru 11, SL28, SL34; 1,750m
beans.desc: A Kenyan Arabica from a cooperative of about 1,500 growers in the Kirinyaga highlands, carefully sorted, washed and dried. Roasted for filter to give a lively, fruity cup, though it also suits espresso.

beans.name: Segontiwm Decaf
beans.desc: The roaster's award-winning decaf from Mexican beans, decaffeinated by a chemical-free mountain water method that preserves flavour. Medium-dark roasted, good for espresso and cafetière.

beans.name: Twthill
beans.desc: A smooth, medium-roast Indian blend designed for espresso. Sweet and balanced, holding up black or with milk.

beans.name: Don Jose Colombian Supremo - Medium
beans.desc: A smooth, evenly balanced medium roast of 100% Arabica from high-altitude Colombia, hand-picked and roasted in Britain to highlight natural sweetness. Caramel and milk chocolate with a light citrus lift.

beans.name: Don Jose Colombian Supremo - Medium-Dark
beans.desc: For lovers of intensity, roasted a little longer to draw out more chocolate and caramel. A fuller, layered cup with a subtle smoky edge that stays mellow and easygoing.

beans.name: Don Jose Colombian Supremo - Dark
beans.desc: A dark-roast Colombian Arabica with a bold, smoky punch and hearty mouthfeel. Cocoa richness, sweet treacle and toasted nuts finish smooth and lingering; strong but velvety.

beans.name: Dona Ester Sugar Cane Decaf
beans.desc: A single-origin Colombian decaf, chosen and roasted to bring out its aroma and decaffeinated by the natural sugar cane process, keeping the full, rich body of a premium coffee.

beans.name: Cafe Colco Premium Signature Blend
beans.origin: Colombia / Honduras / Brazil (plus Ethiopian per description)
beans.desc: A premium blend, hand-roasted in Britain from top-quality beans. Gentle and mellow, hearty and full-bodied, aimed at drinkers wanting a smoother, less acidic cup.

beans.name: Cafe La Vida Premium House Blend
beans.desc: A UK-roasted blend with a gentle, rounded taste for those preferring a softer cup. Beans are carefully chosen and hand-roasted to bring out aroma, giving a full-bodied coffee for connoisseurs and everyday drinkers.

beans.name: Espresso Comercio Premium Signature Blend
beans.desc: A house roast for espresso drinks, combining top-grade robusta with Colombian Supremo Arabica: robusta adds boldness and body, Arabica smoothness and sweetness. Developed for trade clients and valued for its crema and punchy balance.

beans.name: Los Mejores
beans.desc: A mix of two Colombian grades: one adds lively, lighter sweetness, the other deep chocolatey richness. Blending medium-dark and dark roasts for a sturdy, easygoing coffee from family-owned, eco-conscious farms.

beans.name: Santico - Ethiopian
beans.desc: A single-origin Ethiopian Arabica from fertile highlands where climate and soil shape flavour. Hand-picked and grown with traditional, eco-friendly methods.

beans.name: Tio Lucas - Brazilian
beans.desc: A Brazilian single origin of 100% Arabica Bourbon from high elevations: a sweet, aromatic, smooth and balanced cup suited to pour over, French press and cold brew.

beans.name: Paola - Vietnamese
beans.desc: A single-origin Vietnamese robusta roasted to highlight earthy, woody, peppery character. Potent and hearty with chocolatey, nutty fragrance and slight bitterness at the end; darker roasts hit harder, lighter ones are softer.

beans.name: Catracho - Honduras
beans.desc: A Honduran Bourbon from mountain slopes with mineral-rich volcanic soil: layered but gentle and balanced, with dark cocoa, roasted nuts and fruit. For seasoned drinkers and newcomers.

beans.name: Cafe Excelso - Colombian
beans.desc: A Colombian with smooth chocolate, gentle caramel sweetness and cosy toasted nut undertones. Balanced acidity and a long, rich finish.

beans.name: All Day Blend (Half Caff)
beans.desc: Equal parts arabica and Swiss Water decaf, for a morning boost without overdoing it. Pleasantly sweet for any hour, with reduced caffeine to help avoid disrupted sleep.

beans.name: Ambush Forest
beans.desc: Grown on forest farms in Ethiopia's Oromia mountains at 1,900-2,300 metres with minimal human involvement. Presented as an energy boost for celebrations and a reminder of gratitude; its flavour is unlike other origins.

beans.name: Aurora Blend (Limited Edition)
beans.desc: A blend created to celebrate women around the world, pairing a gentle Peruvian coffee with a rich Indonesian one, as a tribute to female farmers and a gift or treat.

beans.name: Luna Blend (Limited Edition)
beans.desc: A seasonal take on Aurora: Indonesian Gayo and Peruvian Café Femenino from women producers plus Ethiopian Yirgacheffe for floral aromas and fruity notes. Medium-light roasted, balanced and clean, celebrating spring.

beans.name: Bolivia Finca Los Rodriguez
beans.producer: Samaipata, Santa Cruz; Fincas Los Rodriguez
beans.listedNotes: Dulce de leche, Green apple, White grape
beans.desc: The Rodriguez family's story began about 35 years ago when former banker Pedro Rodriguez followed his passion for coffee and became a leading figure in Bolivian specialty coffee. His family now runs an export firm and twelve farms.

beans.name: Brazil Fazenda Miaki - Yellow Bourbon
beans.desc: Brazil is a major grower that also keeps much of its crop at home, ranking second in consumption after the US. This Fazenda Miaki offers peach and spicy hot chocolate flavours.

beans.name: Brazil Peaberry
beans.desc: A peaberry from neighbouring farms near Cabo Verde, Minas Gerais, at 950 metres with distinct seasons. In peaberries the seed fails to split in two, thought to channel extra nutrients and boost flavour.

beans.name: Brazil Serra Negra
beans.desc: From Fazenda da Lagoa, where coffee is a way of life across generations. A few selected arabica types are grown sustainably, blending a two-century heritage with modern on-site research.

beans.name: Coffeelink Espresso Blend
beans.desc: A classic everyday espresso from three continents. The roaster partners with honest growers and roasts meticulously for crema, bold taste and a caffeine lift.

beans.name: Colombia Caturra de Altura
beans.desc: A Caturra, a natural Bourbon hybrid developed in São Paulo State, grown in Huila, Colombia. Mineral-rich soils and Andean microclimates give a juicy, fruity, complex character.

beans.name: Colombia Huila
beans.desc: Huila combines high altitude, varied soils and dedicated growers; its farmers often win Cup of Excellence recognition, and it is becoming Colombia's largest producing region. A chocolatey cup worth trying.

beans.name: Colombia Supremo Noble (Oro de Suarez)
beans.desc: A Colombian Supremo, the top size grade, bigger than Excelso. Western and northern harvests run October-November, southern main crop April-June, and smallholders usually wash and dry on their farms.

beans.name: Colombian Geisha
beans.desc: A blend pooling tiny harvests of rare varietals such as Gesha from growers partnering with Osito Coffee. Lots were too small to sell alone, so they were combined as Divino Niño after grading and cupping.

beans.name: El Salvador Finca Castelgazzo
beans.producer: Montecristo / Trifinio; Castelgazzo; Kenya, Bourbon, Pacamara, Geisha
beans.listedNotes: Honey, Red berries, Stone fruit, Milk chocolate
beans.desc: From a farm set up in 1995 by Mario and La Geña Cristiani on the edge of Montecristo National Park in cloud forest. Now run by their daughters, combining coffee, forestry, conservation and community growth.

beans.name: Costa Rica Tarrazu
beans.desc: A Costa Rican Strictly Hard Bean lot roasted until it takes a dark chocolate tint and its oils rise, giving a bolder, heavier brew ideal for espresso.

beans.name: Coffeelink Espresso Blend Dark Roast
beans.desc: A classic dark roast espresso blending coffees from three continents. The roaster picks trustworthy growers and roasts carefully for espresso at any hour.

beans.name: Dark Roast of the Month
beans.desc: A monthly dark roast: dark roasts typically taste smoky, chocolatey and bold, with glossy oils creating a silky, smooth body. Suited to those wanting intense, strong flavours.

beans.name: Decaf Cinnamon Blend
beans.desc: A caffeine-free version of the roaster's Christmas blend, offered year-round: a spiced decaf with warm cinnamon to share with people you care about.

beans.name: Decaf Ginger Blend
beans.desc: A decaf from the Christmas line blending ginger with nutty notes. A toasty, spiced fragrance for festive gatherings, caffeine-free, to share with family and friends.

beans.name: Decaf Nutmeg Blend
beans.desc: A Christmas-themed decaf blend with ginger and nutty notes and a warm, spicy aroma that makes December mornings feel festive, caffeine-free for everyone to share.

beans.name: Decaf Pumpkin Blend
beans.desc: Originally a Halloween favourite, now sold year-round as a decaf so people can enjoy its warm, pleasing character without caffeine.

beans.name: Dominican Republic Barahona
beans.desc: Grown on the Dominican Republic's southwestern Caribbean coast. Alternating rain and sun cause repeated flowering, so pickers revisit each tree several times. Organic methods, with producers investing in healthcare, schools and water.

beans.name: El Salvador Finca San Antonio
beans.producer: Los Ausoles; Malacara B and Las Mercedes farms
beans.desc: From the Chantuc company, founded in 1979 by Emma Alvarez and now run by her children. Workers get meals, housing and steady employment. Beans come from two old plantations under shade trees, fed with compost-based products.

beans.name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe Grade 2
beans.desc: A top seller and the base of the All Day blend, from Yirgacheffe in Sidamo. Lively, sparkling brightness with floral and citrus notes, and an aroma worth buying for alone.

beans.name: Ethiopian Guji Grade 1
beans.desc: A Guji lot bought direct from the grower. Honey, jasmine and bright citrus, with cardamom and nutmeg notes; its lively acidity may not suit everyone but may appeal to Kenyan coffee fans.

beans.name: Ethiopian Illubabor Forest Anaerobic Grade 1
beans.desc: From forest farms in Ethiopia's Illubabor Zone, anaerobically fermented in a sealed, vented tank. The roaster suggests a long pour rather than espresso or moka.

beans.name: Ethiopian Yirgacheffe Grade 1 (Hand Picked & Washed)
beans.desc: An Ethiopian Yirgacheffe sourced directly via a long-time charity partner and a bestseller seen as a good all-day coffee. Wet processing gives lively sparkle, with bright floral and citrus notes.

beans.name: Finca La Verona
beans.producer: El Arenal, Matagalpa; Finca La Verona
beans.desc: A Nicaraguan farm that grows many varieties and keeps them separate after harvest. Pulped coffee ferments anaerobically in airtight tanks; hand-picked cherries dry at a separate facility, then are sorted as regional or microlot.

beans.name: Guatemala Los Volcanos
beans.desc: From Antigua, a Guatemalan valley ringed by mountains, with nutrient-rich volcanic soil and cool climate. Bourbon cherries are washed and sun-dried at a mill owned by the Zelaya family.

beans.name: Christmas Blend (Guji Grade 1 with Cinnamon)
beans.desc: A cinnamon-infused blend added after the Christmas Blend's success, using beans bought direct through an Ethiopian charity partner. This Guji is fragrant and mellow, milder than Yirgacheffe.

beans.name: Orange Blossom Blend
beans.desc: A bright, fruit-forward summer blend, excellent for cold brew and iced Americanos. Gentle, tea-like mouthfeel leaves lingering sweetness.

beans.name: Honduras Honey Process (Microlot)
beans.desc: Honduras is emerging as a specialty leader, with growers experimenting with processing, some offering several methods from one farm. Coffee is central to its economy alongside minerals, tropical fruit and sugar cane.

beans.name: Indian Mysore Nuggets AAA
beans.desc: India has exported fine coffee for over 150 years and ranks fifth worldwide for Arabica. Karnataka grows about four-fifths of the crop, and its large, top-quality Mysore Nuggets are compared to gold.

beans.name: Indonesia Queen Gayo Grade 1
beans.desc: Chocolate, nut and fruit flavours from an all-female cooperative in Aceh. Ketaira belongs to Café Femenino, a programme supporting women growers, using foundation grants for leadership training and a community hub.

beans.name: Italiano Vero Blend
beans.desc: A blend suited to classic Italian-style espresso served straight, also good in milk. Robust yet bold with smooth flavour notes, a tribute to Italy's role in coffee culture.

beans.name: Rocket Fuel Blend
beans.desc: Made for groggy mornings, mostly Tanzanian robusta with Ethiopian arabica adding smooth, cocoa-like sweetness. Works with any method and especially in milky drinks.

beans.name: Jamaican Blue Mountain
beans.desc: A Cup of Excellence-winning Jamaican, a sliver of the island's crop and one of the world's costliest. Grown in cool, misty, rainy highlands with free-draining soil; also the base of Tia Maria liqueur.

beans.name: Jamaican Blue Mountain Peaberry
beans.desc: A scarce Jamaican peaberry honoured with Cup of Excellence, grown on the misty Blue Mountains slopes. Highly sought worldwide and the flavour base of Tia Maria liqueur.

beans.name: Kenya AA
beans.desc: Acidic soil suits Arabica here. Most production is from small and mid-sized farms that wash beans on-site and sun-dry on raised beds. Beans are size-sorted and auctioned weekly, with two harvests a year.

beans.name: Kongo Papua New Guinea
beans.desc: Grown in Simbu, Papua New Guinea's third-largest coffee province, via Kong Coffee. Y grade covers about 65% of national exports from small village farmers, traditionally with a rich, fruity body that suits blends.

beans.name: Light Roast Blend of the Month
beans.desc: Light roasts give vivid brightness, sharp acidity and a gentle tea-like sweetness, with shorter roasting letting natural flavours shine. Each month's pick may be single origin or a blend; best as filter, pour-over or cafetière.

beans.name: Maragogype
beans.desc: Oscar Jimenez runs Nuevo Pacto in Jinotega, Nicaragua, where forest shade protects soil and creates a microclimate. Mostly hardy Catimor with a smaller share of large-bean Maragogype, all washed.

beans.name: Mexican Terruno Nayarita Reserve
beans.desc: Opening the bag releases berry sweetness and nutty butter. A medium-bodied cup finishing smoothly with baker's chocolate, candy-like sweetness and bright berry and orange acidity. Grown by about 260 cooperative farmers around Cerro San Juan; fully traceable.

beans.name: Mexico El Triunfo Biosphere Reserve Premium
beans.desc: The El Triunfo reserve sits where two ecological zones meet, supporting abundant wildlife and about 12,000 residents. A 663-member cooperative grows shade coffee under layered native trees and replanted with resistant varieties after the 2012 rust outbreak.

beans.name: Noss Noss Blend
beans.desc: A tribute to cultural traditions and coffee's Arabic roots, best as espresso. Arabica and Robusta, with its concept from a Moroccan drink, roasted several times a week to stay fresh.

beans.name: Old Brown Java
beans.desc: From Java, where coffee once matured on long sea voyages as ballast on spice ships to Europe. Exposure to wood and brine gave a sturdy, earthy flavour, best slowly savoured.

beans.name: Peru 121 Project
beans.desc: Part of importer DR Wakefield's 1-2-1 scheme pairing individual growers with roasters. An organic, Fairtrade-certified Peruvian grown under shade and washed traditionally, mostly picked in August at peak ripeness.

beans.name: Peru Cafe Femenino
beans.desc: The Café Femenino Foundation awards grants to women in coffee regions worldwide. Peru's small farms, often under three hectares, are organised into carefully run cooperatives.

beans.name: Premium Espresso Blend
beans.origin: Ethiopia / Colombia / Peru / Honduras / El Salvador
beans.desc: A premium blend of five high-grade coffees from Ethiopia, Colombia, Peru, Honduras and El Salvador. The roaster extends roasting time and samples each batch to hit the intended profile.

beans.name: Pumpkin Spice Blend
beans.desc: A Halloween-themed coffee mixing pumpkin spice with a seasonal dark roast and mellow, cocoa-tinged single origins. Medium-dark, works with any brew method and suits lattes.

beans.name: Rwanda Kinini AA Microlot
beans.desc: A microlot from trees above 2,000 metres, processed at Kinini washing station where 633 farmers deliver. Ferments five to twenty hours after pulping, then sun-dries about two weeks. Smooth dark chocolate, lemon and fudge.

beans.name: Rwanda Lake Kivu
beans.listedNotes: Toffee caramel, Red berry, Citrus, Clove
beans.desc: A Rwandan from Lake Kivu grown high in volcanic soil: rich, creamy toffee and caramel with bright berries and citrus, clove and cinnamon warmth, and a full body that lingers.

beans.name: Sidamo Dara Grade 1 (Washed)
beans.desc: Ethiopians treat coffee as a cherished ritual. Sidamo's fertile soil, steady rain and ideal temperatures yield outstanding beans; wet processing gives this one bright apricot, jasmine and caramel.

beans.name: Signature Espresso Blend
beans.desc: A tailored classic espresso of Colombian, Brazilian, Ethiopian and Indian beans: sweet, rich and harmonised in taste, acidity and scent, holding up in milky drinks with chocolatey notes.

beans.name: Spiced Ginger Blend
beans.desc: A holiday blend of premium Ethiopian coffee with ginger, meant to bring people together. Nutty ginger flavour and a warm, spicy aroma for festive mornings.

beans.name: Spiced Nutmeg Blend
beans.desc: A Christmas blend of the newest single origin with a sprinkle of nutmeg, for sharing. Ginger and nutty flavours and a warm, spicy aroma.

beans.name: Sumatra Lintong Grade 1
beans.desc: A Sumatran with distinctive taste, mild sourness, heavy mouthfeel and rustic, soil-like notes. Traditional wet-hulled, grown in full sun without chemical inputs mostly by small-scale farmers.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf - Colombian Excelso
beans.producer: Suarez; Cafe Granja La Esperanza; Caturra, Typica; 1,700m
beans.desc: Swiss Water decaf using water, heat and timing to strip caffeine while preserving the bean's character. This Excelso grade is smaller than Supremo but tastes sweeter, with smooth, rounded body and subtle caramel.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf - Brazil Cerrado
beans.desc: Brazil has pushed sustainability through stronger forest-protection laws, with many estates setting aside conservation land. Standard lots taste nutty and caramelly, creamy, while newer methods reveal sweetness, citrus and brightness.

beans.name: Winter Espresso
beans.producer: Ethiopia: Telila Washing Station, 8 women smallholders in the Kecho Anderacha kebele. Guatemala: El Anonal, Huehuetenango (Orlando Antulio Martinez Samayoa and Gesler Gudemny Martinez Lopez)
beans.desc: A festive, espresso-only blend of honey-processed Ethiopian coffee (JARC 74110 and 74112, from Telila Washing Station) and a washed Guatemalan field blend of Bourbon, Typica, San Ramon and Caturra from El Anonal. The roaster likens the Ethiopian half to fruit-flavoured Turkish delight and describes the cup as sweet and richly textured, made for Christmas drinks. The Guatemalan producers replanted with rust-resistant varieties after a leaf rust outbreak and trialled Gesha and Pacamara in 2015.

beans.name: Red Brick
beans.producer: Ethiopia: Telila and Atoma washing stations, Jimma, about 97 smallholders via Addis Exporter. Costa Rica: La Lia Micromill (Luis and Oscar Monge) and Don Oscar Micromill (Alejandro Jimenez), Tarrazu
beans.processFull: Ethiopia washed; Costa Rica white honey
beans.brew: Espresso. Roaster's recipe: 19g in a 20g VST basket, 94-94.5C, 28-32 seconds, 1:2 ratio (developed on a Victoria Arduino Black Eagle)
beans.desc: The roaster's seasonal espresso blend, built on the idea of good neighbours: 47% washed Ethiopian lots from Addis Exporter's Telila and Atoma stations (JARC 74110 and 74112) and 53% white-honey Costa Rican lots from two neighbouring Tarrazu micromills (Catuai and Caturra). The components change with each harvest, and the aim is to emphasise fruit and sweetness: yellow plum, smooth butterscotch and orange, with a silky, lightly floral Ethiopian edge.

beans.name: La Cidra
beans.producer: La Cidra farm, Renato Sanchez and family; exported by Beneficio San Vicente. Region not shown
beans.desc: A washed Honduran espresso (Catuai and IHCAFE90, 2026 harvest) from Renato Sanchez and his family, with plum, caramel and praline plus stonefruit and dark chocolate. For 2026 Renato built raised drying beds for tighter quality control, his daughter Alejandra worked a season at exporter Beneficio San Vicente to learn its quality methods, and the family is working on soil quality and biodiversity.

beans.name: San Martin
beans.producer: San Martin farm, owned by Lizbeth Venegas, co-owner of Puente Tarrazu Micromill, Costa Rica
beans.desc: A washed Costa Rican Gesha, the third release in the roaster's Costa Rican special projects series, named after the farm of Lizbeth Venegas, co-owner of Puente Tarrazu Micromill. It shines as an espresso with blackberry, floral sweetness and a decadent, creamy, silky texture. Square Mile has bought from this mill since its early days and regularly uses it in Red Brick.

beans.name: Sweetshop
beans.producer: Ethiopia: Dambi Uddo Drying Station, Guji, via Sookoo Coffee. Costa Rica: El Higueron, Mario Araya (Los Cuarteles micromill, Araya family), Tarrazu
beans.processFull: Ethiopia natural; Costa Rica red honey
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry, Creamy body, Florals, Bergamot (Bookkisa); Jammy, Candy-like (El Higueron)
beans.desc: A playful, fruit-driven espresso, 50% natural Ethiopian Bookkisa (Gibirinna 74110 and Serto 74112) and 50% red-honey Costa Rican El Higueron (Catuai). The roaster says it is aiming for as much fruit and fun as possible rather than balance or tradition. Bookkisa brings strawberry, a creamy mouthfeel, then florals and bergamot; El Higueron adds jammy, candy-like notes.

beans.name: Decaf Espresso
beans.producer: La Cidra farm, Sanchez family, southwestern Lempira; exported by Beneficio San Vicente
beans.desc: A decaf version of La Cidra (Catuai and IHCAFE90, washed) roasted for espresso, with raisin, fudge and orange. The page describes southwestern Lempira as drier than Santa Barbara, with more remote, larger farms, and says Beneficio San Vicente's slow, careful drying improves shelf life and flavour; the roaster first bought La Cidra in 2022.

beans.name: Don Cayito
beans.producer: Don Cayito farm, Diego Calderon and family, Los Angeles Micromill, Dota, Tarrazu
beans.desc: A natural Typica from Dota, Tarrazu, in small 175g bags, with a blueberry-led profile of fresh and dried berries, cherry, peach and white flowers and a velvety mouthfeel. It comes from one of the roaster's foundational Costa Rican relationships: Diego Calderon's family mill at Los Angeles Micromill, from a farm the founding green buyer first visited about a decade ago.

beans.name: Shortcut
beans.desc: A no-decision filter option for people who love juicy, sweet specialty coffee but sometimes want to skip choosing: complex, sweet, high-grown washed lots picked by the roaster. The page gives no origin, producer, variety or roast and marks it coming soon.

beans.name: Shoondhisa
beans.producer: Guji; smallholders via Sookoo Coffee, processed at Suke Drying Station
beans.desc: A natural Guji lot (Gibirinna 74110 and Serto 74112) bought by the roaster since 2023 from Sookoo Coffee, who grow, process and export it. The late 2026 harvest reached the station into February; cherries are dried whole in a thin layer for four to five days, then thickened for two more weeks, which develops the nectarine, honey and lychee character. Suggested for afternoons or brunch.

beans.name: El Trapiche Santa Rosa 1900
beans.producer: Santa Rosa 1900 micromill, Santa Rosa Arriba de Leon Cortes; Kevin and Efrain 'Macho' Naranjo; 1,700-1,900m
beans.desc: A washed Red and Yellow Catuai from father and son Macho and Kevin Naranjo at 1,700-1,900m, named after the traditional mill used to press sugarcane juice. Baked apple, honey and nougat with caramelised sweetness, bright acidity and a full, lush body; the roaster usually buys honey-process lots from this family, so a washed lot is new. Pitched as classic Costa Rica for breakfast or weekends.

beans.name: The Filter Blend
beans.producer: Guatemala: Paya', Huehuetenango (Nery Pablo Lopez; Cooperative El Sendero). Rwanda: Rebero, Kinini Washing Station, Rulindo
beans.desc: A seasonal, adaptable everyday filter blend using the same idea as Red Brick: 50% Guatemalan Paya' (Caturra and Bourbon) and 50% Rwandan Rebero (BM139, BM71, Bourbon Jackson), both washed. Sweet, balanced and medium-bodied, with red apple, praline and sultana; its components are subject to change.

beans.name: Half Caff
beans.producer: Honduras: La Cidra, Lempira (Renato Sanchez). Costa Rica: Santa Rosa 1900 micromill, Tarrazu (Naranjo family)
beans.processFull: Washed; Honduras component ethyl acetate decaf
beans.desc: A 50/50 filter blend of ethyl-acetate decaf La Cidra from Honduras and washed El Trapiche Santa Rosa 1900 from Costa Rica, bringing two family-run farms into one cup. Forest fruit, milk chocolate and almond, with crisp apple and a creamy mouthfeel from El Trapiche and persimmon-like acidity and syrupy depth from La Cidra. Pitched as a mid-afternoon pick-me-up.

beans.name: Decaf Filter
beans.producer: La Cidra farm, Sanchez family, southwestern Lempira; exported by Beneficio San Vicente
beans.brew: V60 or French press. Roaster suggests 70g coffee per litre of water; for V60 agitate the bloom, then use low agitation
beans.desc: A light-roast decaf La Cidra (Catuai and IHCAFE90, washed) with raisin, fudge and hazelnut, dried fruit and toffee and a dulce de leche-like sweetness. The ethyl acetate process softens the coffee's sharp pomegranate acidity. The page says the next decaf will be Union San Pedro from Oaxaca, Mexico.

beans.name: 01 Brazil + Guatemala
beans.listedNotes: Maple syrup, Bakewell tart, Plum, Hazelnut

beans.name: 02 Brazil + Rwanda
beans.listedNotes: Orange zest, Stewed apple, Sweet almond

beans.name: Article
beans.desc: Workshop's flagship house blend, dependable and steady in every cup, with familiar dark chocolate, maple syrup and raisin notes. Built to shine across all brew methods for a timeless, pleasing daily coffee.

beans.name: Legacy
beans.producer: Calca (Manuel Patilla Carrasco); Uraga, Guji (Raro Boda)
beans.desc: A blend of rotating harvests from the roaster's longest-standing growers, rich and layered, with spiced baked goods, caramel-like sweetness and dark berry fruit. Suits any preparation method.

beans.name: Pillar
beans.desc: A coffee with rich mouthfeel, layered sweetness and gentle acidity. Treacle, crushed cocoa bits, liquorice root, a hint of spice and sugared nuts; pairs especially well with dairy-based drinks.

beans.name: Slow Brew
beans.desc: A filter blend of Colombian coffee with brown sugar and gentle apple and Ugandan coffee bringing citrus, smooth sweetness and bright aromas. Lively, fruity and full of character, especially brewed slowly.

beans.name: Reset Half Caff
beans.listedNotes: Roasted almonds, Sweet raspberry, Milk chocolate
beans.desc: A half-caff blend for late-day work, using roughly half decaf beans for afternoons and evenings when a full hit feels unnecessary. The Colombian beans are from Huila, with a La Plata lot chosen for decaffeination.

beans.name: Sipi Tangwen
beans.desc: A small batch of Sipi Tangwen from Mount Elgon, Uganda, designed for filter: crisp, sweet and citrusy. Smallholders grow it at high altitude in volcanic soil, supported by a co-op.

beans.name: Maidy Bocanegra Pink Bourbon
beans.producer: Bruselas, Pitalito, Huila; Finca Los Limones; Pink Bourbon
beans.desc: Maidy Bocanegra returns with a standout Pink Bourbon from her Huila farm. Cherries are hand-picked, rested, depulped, briefly fermented, washed and slowly dried on mesh for a fruity, richly sweet cup.

beans.name: Danche
beans.desc: A fresh new-season Ethiopian from Chelbesa, a long-standing team pick prized for its intensely floral and powerful character.

beans.name: Bulaago
beans.desc: An espresso from Bulaago, Uganda: smooth and silky with bright citrus-like fruit, quince and fresh pine, honey-like sweetness lingering through a clean finish. Grown by Mount Elgon smallholders and picked as a standout reserve lot.

beans.name: La Colorada Gesha
beans.producer: Villa Maria, Iquira, Huila; Eduardo Anacona; Gesha
beans.desc: A Gesha, one of two releases from Eduardo Anacona's Finca La Colorada in Colombia. Bright, fizzy pink lemonade quality, delicate flowers and juicy, mature berry flavours.

beans.name: Migoti
beans.desc: A fresh Burundi from a Rubanda lot where over a thousand small growers bring ripe cherries to the Migoti station. Layered fruit and rich cocoa with a tidy, defined finish from carefully handled Red Bourbon.

beans.name: Gakuyu-ini
beans.desc: A lively, striking Kenyan from the Gakuyu-ini washing station, chosen for composure, strength and crystal-clear character. Only a small number of bags were secured, as it was too good to pass up.

beans.name: Chakra
beans.desc: A year-round Peruvian. Workshop has bought from Peruvian growers for about a decade and has partnered with the Valle Inca association since 2018. Shaped by organic methods and attentive harvesting and processing.

beans.name: El Nevado
beans.producer: Huila; about 24 smallholders via Caravela; Caturra, Castillo
beans.desc: A lively yet smooth single-origin Colombian with toasted sugar, almond paste and warm fruit. Roasted to suit every brew method, a versatile home-brewing favourite.

beans.name: Madegi
beans.desc: Madegi, whose Amharic name means growth, celebrates Workshop's Ethiopian sourcing since 2011, mostly through Snap Coffees over the past eight years, and how that partnership has matured.

beans.name: La Plata Decaf
beans.producer: San Sebastian, La Plata, Huila; 7 farmers
beans.desc: A decaf given as much attention as the caffeinated coffees: a rich, well-rounded Colombian with currant- and prune-like fruity sweetness ending on bittersweet cocoa and toasted nuts. Roasted for any brew method.

beans.name: Evergreen
beans.desc: Grown high in Nueva Segovia, Nicaragua: a layered coffee with plum, fudge and chocolate-biscuit sweetness, roasted to work across every brewing style.

beans.name: BS1 Espresso
beans.desc: An easy, sweet espresso for flat whites and cappuccinos that also works straight: milk chocolate richness, sticky caramel and a bright red-fruit finish. Grown by smallholders near Buesaco with the Procaal cooperative handling drying.

beans.name: Cruise Control
beans.desc: A single-farm Brazilian from Daterra Estate in Cerrado Mineiro: dependable and sweet with a rich, cocoa-like body, honey and hazelnut. Works black or with dairy and plant milks.

beans.name: Jumpstart
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Nut praline, Maple syrup
beans.desc: Triple Co's first house blend, built to energise tougher mornings. Mellow and smooth, with rich silky body and little sharpness, and designed to taste great with milk.

beans.name: Mixtape
beans.desc: A 50/50 fruity espresso blend highlighting coffees the team especially enjoys. More adventurous than the everyday range, with a lively, liqueur-like character; components change with the seasons.

beans.name: Slow Burn
beans.desc: A half-caff blend for the calm after a lively fire: warm, steady and long-lasting. Suits flat whites, iced coffee, afternoon espresso or batch filter, giving energy without a crash.

beans.name: Colombia Sugarcane Decaf
beans.desc: A decaf from the same growers as BS1, aiming to taste much like regular coffee. Decaffeinated with sugarcane-derived ethyl acetate to protect the bean's flavours, then steamed to remove leftover solvent.

beans.name: Shop Filter
beans.producer: Santa Ana Volcano, El Borbollon mill
beans.desc: A washed El Salvador from farms supplying the El Borbollon mill, run by the Alvares family, mostly on the Santa Ana volcano. Patio-dried and hand-sorted, with sweetness, plum flavours and a nutty close.

beans.name: Burundi Vyiza
beans.producer: Vyiza washing station, Ngozi; Red Bourbon 1800m
beans.desc: A returning favourite from Vyiza station in Ngozi, northern Burundi, at 1,800 metres, run as a shared community project (the name means 'good things' in Kirundi). Slow-dried over weeks for sweet, liquor-like richness.

beans.name: Birthday Party - Tanzania
beans.desc: An SL28 from Glenmalure on Ngila Estate in northern Tanzania, near a cloud forest where wildlife such as elephants roams. Hand-sorted, pulped, fermented 12 hours, then dried on raised beds over eight to thirteen days.

beans.name: Nicaragua La Picona
beans.producer: Finca La Picona, Nueva Segovia; Maracaturra 1250m
beans.desc: From a nine-hectare farm in Las Manos, Dipilto, Nicaragua, owned by Martha Lucía Albir Sotomayor and shaded by native trees. The rare Maracaturra variety gives a lively, layered cup with medium body and molasses-like sweetness.

beans.name: Ethiopia Buku Abel
beans.desc: A Buku Abel lot from a high-altitude Guji village. Smallholders' cherries are hand-picked, sorted and dried outdoors on raised platforms. Sourced via SNAP Specialty Coffee, a partner since 2022.

beans.name: Peru San Ignacio
beans.desc: A washed Peruvian from San Ignacio smallholders with caramel sweetness, citrusy pomelo and an herbal finish. Moist valleys and steady rain ripen cherries slowly and evenly for clean, sweet cups.

beans.name: Colombia Gaitania
beans.producer: Gaitania, Planadas, Tolima; Nasa Wesx community; Caturra
beans.desc: An organic microlot from the Nasa Wesx community in Tolima, Colombia. The Caturra ferments 50 hours in low oxygen, then dries on raised beds under temperature control, drawing out juicy red grape, a rum-like body and sweetness.

beans.name: Papua New Guinea - Elimbari
beans.producer: Chuave, Mount Wilhelm; smallholders via Kongo
beans.desc: A mellow-acidity coffee with earthy, black-tea-like notes from Chuave district in Papua New Guinea's central highlands, grown by smallholders on Mount Wilhelm's slopes. Pulped, fermented and tarp-dried before Kongo's mill sorts and exports it.

beans.name: Brazil Rancho Grande Estate
beans.producer: Sul de Minas; Rancho Grande farm, José Carlos Reis
beans.roastNote: Roast level not stated; 'developed for sweetness and balance'
beans.desc: A Brazilian from a family farm in Sul de Minas, made for easy, comforting drinking. Milk chocolate leads, with roasted nuts, a soft round body and little acidity. Suits espresso, milk drinks and filter.

beans.name: Dark Sugars
beans.roastNote: Roast level not stated; 'developed for body, sweetness and milk performance'
beans.listedNotes: Heavy dark chocolate, Subtle spice, Medium sweetness
beans.desc: A seasonal espresso blend built to hold up in milk while keeping sweetness and structure. Brazilian and Indonesian coffees combine for a heavy, chocolate-led cup with full body and a long finish.

beans.name: Bond Street Espresso Blend
beans.roastNote: Medium roast developed for body and sweetness
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, Roasted nuts, Strawberry sweetness
beans.desc: A seasonal espresso of Brazilian and Ethiopian beans. The Brazilian brings chocolate, nuts and a silky body; the Ethiopian adds sweet, strawberry-like fruit. Balanced and rounded, made for espresso and milk drinks.

beans.name: Rwanda Musozi Washed Lot 4
beans.listedNotes: Blackberry, Black tea, Raspberry, Orange, Brown sugar, Bright fruit
beans.desc: A seasonal single origin from Rwamatamu Coffee in Nyamasheke, grown high in mineral-rich volcanic ground. Fully washed, with fruit-led brightness, natural sweetness, clean acidity and a smooth, balanced body for espresso or filter.

beans.name: Kenya Ngunguru AA
beans.listedNotes: Redcurrant, Lemon, Grapefruit, Bergamot, Dark chocolate
beans.desc: A seasonal Kenyan from the Ngunguru area, grown high on volcanic soil. Ripe cherries are hand-picked and washed at local stations. Juicy fruit brightness, citrus lift and a little dark chocolate with a medium, lively body.

beans.name: Funky Weekend Blend
beans.roastNote: Medium roast developed for chocolate, body and funk
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, Roasted nuts, Red fruit, Winey funk
beans.desc: A seasonal espresso blend pairing a creamy, chocolate-heavy Brazilian with a lively, wine-like fermented Colombian that adds red fruit and bold character. Sweet and chocolate-led with an edge, aimed at lattes and flat whites.

beans.name: Colombia ReForest Project
beans.producer: Northern Tolima / southern Caldas; Reforest Project cherry, processed at El Vergel Estate
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, Chocolate, Sugar cane, Roasted almond, Light orange finish
beans.desc: A sweet, balanced, lively Colombian from a reforestation-led scheme in northern Tolima and southern Caldas, where farms prioritise environmental care and help neighbouring growers. Caramel, chocolate and almond with a light orange finish.

beans.name: Colombia El Silencio
beans.producer: Piendamó, Cauca; Robinson Rivera, El Silencio
beans.desc: A seasonal natural from Robinson Rivera's farm in Piendamó, Cauca. Robinson, a grower for over twenty years, picks very ripe cherries that are sorted, rested in silos, fermented and dried, giving a fruity, sweet, layered cup.

beans.name: Rwanda Musozi Natural Lot 3
beans.desc: A seasonal natural from Rwamatamu Coffee in Nyamasheke. Natural processing gives juicy, fruit-forward sweetness and a lively body, with blackberry, apricot and a floral hint. Expressive yet approachable, for espresso or filter.

beans.name: Ethiopia Guji Megadu Kickstart
beans.roastNote: Roast level not stated; 'developed to highlight sweetness, body and fruit clarity'
beans.listedNotes: Peach, Bergamot, Dark chocolate, Vanilla, Honey, Berries
beans.desc: A sweet, balanced coffee from Bette Buna's own Guji farm. A short oxygen-free stage before natural drying adds body and depth while keeping the classic Ethiopian natural character: familiar, but richer.

beans.name: Ethiopia Lalesa
beans.producer: Gedeb; Lalesa washing station (Ephtah Specialty Coffee); smallholder producers
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry, Blueberry, Peach, Black tea, Milk chocolate
beans.desc: A natural Ethiopian from the Lalesa washing station in Gedeb, grown high. Ripe berries, soft peach and gentle black tea over a rounded milk chocolate sweetness; fruity without being tart. Filter brewing suits it best.

beans.name: Ethiopia Gotiti
beans.producer: Gedeo Zone, Gedeb; Gotiti washing station; smallholder producers
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry, Blueberry, Peach, Milk chocolate (headline); Strawberry laces, Blackberry, Apricot, Orange zest, Honey, Jasmine, Thyme, Floral tea (detail)
beans.desc: A single origin from the Gedeb district of southern Ethiopia, grown high and washed after harvest. Lively and fruit-led, with floral touches and natural sweetness; the roaster calls it clean, layered and elegant, for filter or espresso.

beans.name: Indonesia Team Pegasing CM
beans.producer: Pegasing, Sumatra; Hendra and family (farm and washing station)
beans.desc: From Hendra and his family's farm and washing station in Pegasing, Sumatra. Instead of standard wet-hulling they experiment with carbonic maceration, giving bright fruit sweetness and a smooth body for filter or espresso.

beans.name: Guatemala Finca Filadelfia
beans.producer: Antigua Valley; Dalton family, Finca Filadelfia
beans.roastNote: Roast level not stated (roast profile listed as Filter)
beans.desc: A tidy, sweet, clean Guatemalan typical of the Antigua Valley. The Dalton family has grown coffee on the farm for more than 160 years, and the roaster praises their steady commitment to quality.

beans.name: Pour Star Martini
beans.producer: Huila; no producer or farm named
beans.processFull: Anaerobic fermentation with passionfruit, yeast and natural flavouring
beans.listedNotes: Passionfruit, Tropical fruit, Subtle sweetness, Smooth body, Bright juicy character
beans.desc: An experimental Colombian from Huila fermented with passionfruit, giving vivid, powerful tropical fruit with a silky mouthfeel and restrained sweetness. Suited to filter and espresso.

beans.name: Colombia Frozen Berries
beans.roastNote: Roast level not stated; 'developed to highlight fruit intensity and sweetness'
beans.listedNotes: Blueberry, Raspberry, Blackberry, Plum, Red fruits, Strawberry
beans.brew: Filter (page says it can also be enjoyed as espresso)
beans.desc: An experimental Huila microlot from the Wild Collection, fermented alongside dried forest fruits for depth and sweetness. Bold and juicy with a syrupy body and long finish; best as filter.

beans.name: Colombia Simply Red
beans.producer: Huila; no producer or farm named
beans.desc: An experimental Huila lot made by co-fermentation, leaning into red berries: lively and fruity with tangy brightness, a smooth body and gentle sweetness. Suits filter and espresso.

beans.name: Panama Janson Geisha Micro Lot 803 Honey
beans.producer: Janson Family Estate (Janson Coffee), 1,700 masl; Geisha
beans.listedNotes: Honeyed sweetness, Caramelised sugar, Sticky toffee pudding, Ripe stone fruit, Delicate florals
beans.desc: A limited-release honey-process Geisha from Panama's Janson family estate: syrupy and sweet with caramel and toffee-like notes, ripe stone fruit and delicate flowers, aimed at clarity and sweetness.

beans.name: Panama Janson Geisha Lot 1015
beans.producer: Janson Family Estate (Janson Coffee), 1,700 masl; Geisha
beans.listedNotes: Sweet, Pink florals, Raspberry, Dried cherry, Syrupy dessert-like body, Long juicy finish
beans.desc: A limited-release natural Geisha from the Janson family estate: sweet with pink florals, raspberry and dried cherry over a syrupy, dessert-like body and a long, juicy finish.

beans.producer: Janson Family Estate (Janson Coffee), 1,700 masl; Geisha
notes: Not yet published (page says tasting notes are updating)

beans.desc: A limited-release Geisha from Panama's Janson family estate, a producer known for expressive coffees. Each micro lot is grown and processed with care for clarity, natural sweetness and delicate floral and fruit character.
