beans.producer: Janson Family Estate (Janson Coffee), 1,700 masl; Geisha
beans.listedNotes: Clarity, Florals, Sweetness (roast aim, not formal tasting notes)
beans.desc: A limited-release Geisha lot from Panama's Janson family estate, roasted to bring out clarity, florals and sweetness for an elegant, aromatic cup.

beans.name: CGLE Competition Series Laurina
beans.producer: Café Granja La Esperanza, Cerro Azul farm
beans.roastNote: Roast level not stated (roast profile listed as Filter)
beans.listedNotes: White peach, Orange blossom, Honey, Mandarin, Black tea, Cane sugar
beans.desc: A graceful, finely balanced Colombian Laurina offering bright citrus, gentle stone fruit and floral notes. Smooth sweetness carries into a neat, tea-like aftertaste that lingers.

beans.name: CGLE Competition Series XO Geisha
beans.producer: Café Granja La Esperanza, Cerro Azul farm; Geisha
beans.roastNote: Medium-light (per user; page lists roast profile as Filter)
beans.listedNotes: Jasmine, Tropical fruits, Peach, Honey, Bergamot, Silky tea-like finish
beans.brew: Espresso (per user; page's brewing text is cut off and its roast profile says Filter)
beans.desc: An elegant, very expressive Colombian Geisha from Cerro Azul farm, XO-processed. Jasmine, ripe tropical and stone fruit and honey lead into a lingering tea-like finish. Made in tiny batches for competitors and enthusiasts.

beans.name: Milan
beans.producer: Ethiopian Mocha; Indian Monsoon Malabar; regions and producers not shown
beans.listedNotes: Smoky roasted almond, Caramelised demerara sugar, Chocolate, Nutty
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, flat white, latte, cafetiere, AeroPress
beans.desc: Hawkins' best-selling 100% Arabica blend of Brazil, Kenya, Colombia, Ethiopian Mocha and Indian Monsoon Malabar, pitched as the starting point in the range and the blend most cafe and home customers reorder. Smooth, sweet and clean-finishing with smoky roasted almond, caramelised demerara, chocolate and nut notes and no harshness or bitterness; works as espresso and holds up in flat whites and lattes.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: Cafe Selva
beans.listedNotes: Toffee, Butterscotch, Sweet acidity, Smoky, Spice, Full body
beans.brew: Filter, cafetiere, AeroPress; espresso (whole beans); milk drinks
beans.desc: The Fairtrade and Soil Association Organic blend, roasted medium-dark and rated 4/5 for strength. Full-bodied and smooth with toffee, butterscotch, sweet acidity and smoky spice; works as espresso and in milk drinks and is pitched at cafes serving it all day, with filter suggested for a smoother cup.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: Colombia
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, Dark chocolate, Orange, Hazelnut, Vanilla, Red apple
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, pour-over, cafetiere, AeroPress; milk
beans.desc: A single-origin medium roast from Huila, rated 3/5 for strength: sweet and dependable with caramel and dark chocolate up front, a soft orange note and a clean finish. Aimed at drinkers who want a single origin that is not sharp or bright; suits espresso, milk drinks and cafetiere.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: Colombian Decaf
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, Dark chocolate, Orange, Hazelnut, Vanilla, Red apple
beans.desc: Single-origin Huila decaf, decaffeinated with water only, pitched as decaf that tastes like real coffee: smooth and medium-bodied with chocolate and sweetness and none of the flatness common in decafs. Aimed at people cutting caffeine and served in the evening by its care home and hotel customers; works as espresso, filter, cafetiere or with milk.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: High Mountain Blend
beans.desc: Listing only (the product page would not load): chocolate and nut with a bright, fruity edge.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: Mocha Mysore
beans.producer: Mysore-Coorg (India); Ethiopian Mocha; producers not shown
beans.desc: A medium-roast blend of Ethiopian Mocha and beans from India's Mysore-Coorg region, rated 2/5 for strength: mellow and gentle with plenty of chocolate, some nuttiness and no sharp edges or strong acidity. Suggested for cafetiere and filter, for drinkers who find Milan too strong, or for a quieter afternoon cup.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: After Dinner Blend
beans.desc: Listing only (the product page would not load): chocolate, butterscotch, sweet acidity and a smoky note.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: Brazil Mogiana
beans.producer: Mogiana, on the Sao Paulo / Minas Gerais border; producer not shown
beans.desc: A single-origin medium roast from Mogiana, on the Sao Paulo / Minas Gerais border: mild with a soft body and gentle chocolate and nut flavours, subtle fruity hints and no sharp acidity. Described as an easy all-day coffee that many cafes keep alongside their main blend; works as espresso, cafetiere, with milk or on its own.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: Breakfast Blend
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, Butterscotch, Sweet acidity, Smoky, Light body
beans.desc: The lighter morning coffee in the range: Colombian Huila with a little Kenyan, roasted medium and rated 3/5 for strength. Bright and clean with chocolate, butterscotch and enough acidity to wake you up without harshness, a light body and a smoky edge; works as filter or espresso and suits milk better than heavier blends. The page suggests 92-96C water.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: Continental Blend
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, Cocoa, Nutty, Molasses, Burnt caramel, Smooth
beans.brew: Espresso, cafetiere, filter, AeroPress; milk drinks
beans.desc: The darker option for drinkers who find Milan too mild, rated 4/5: South American Arabica roasted longer and darker for body, chocolate and cocoa, nuttiness, molasses and burnt caramel with a roasted finish. Popular with cafes wanting a stronger blend for milk drinks; suits espresso, cafetiere, filter and AeroPress, and Flying Scotsman is the darker step beyond it.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: Costa Rica
beans.listedNotes: Crisp acidity, Creamy body, Citrus, Sweet chocolate
beans.brew: Filter and pour-over; lighter espresso; milk drinks
beans.desc: A single-origin light roast from Tarrazu, rated 2/5 for strength: clean, bright and easy to drink, with crisp acidity, soft citrus, a touch of chocolate sweetness and a creamy body. Recommended as filter or pour-over to bring out the brightness; can be pulled as a lighter espresso and is also suggested for lattes and flat whites.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: Flying Scotsman
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Nutty, Cocoa, Molasses, Burnt caramel, Smooth
beans.brew: Espresso, moka pot, cafetiere, drip filter
beans.desc: The company's darkest, boldest coffee, rated 5/5: South American Arabica roasted longer and darker for body, plain chocolate, cocoa, molasses and burnt caramel with a roasted finish and no fruit or brightness. Cafe customers use it as a second blend for a stronger cup; suits espresso, moka pot and cafetiere, with well-textured milk.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: Java
beans.producer: Ijen Plateau, East Java; producer not shown
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Toasted nuts, Subtle herbal notes
beans.desc: A single-origin medium roast from the Ijen Plateau in East Java, at medium strength: dark chocolate, toasted nuts and subtle herbal notes, with the herbal side more noticeable in filter than espresso. One of the older single origins and a popular choice for customers who want something different from South American beans; the page suggests trying it black.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: Kenya AA
beans.producer: Murang'a; AA grade (hand-sorted); producer not shown
beans.desc: A single-origin Kenya AA from Murang'a (AA is the top bean-size grade, hand-sorted before leaving the farm): bright and citrusy with blackcurrant, berry, lemon and jasmine. Recommended as filter or pour-over; it also works as espresso, sharper and more vivid, for customers who want more character than a house blend.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: Kenya Peaberry
beans.listedNotes: Blackcurrant, Cherry, Chocolate, Plenty of acidity
beans.desc: A single-origin medium-roast Kenya Peaberry from Nyeri; peaberries are a single round bean rather than the usual pair, which the page says tends to give a more concentrated cup. Blackcurrant, cherry and chocolate with plenty of acidity at medium strength; best as filter or pour-over, or a sharper, fruitier espresso, for drinkers wanting more intense Kenyan character than the AA.
beans.priceBasis: 250g regular price (size not tied on the page); unconfirmed

beans.name: Cerrado, Brazil (Decaf)
beans.producer: Cerrado, Minas Gerais; blend from hundreds of family farms, assessed by a five-person team at a Patrocinio lab; about 900m; Catuai, Mundo Novo
beans.processFull: Natural and pulped natural; sugarcane decaf
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, French press, AeroPress, moka pot (grind-matched; omni roast)
beans.desc: A decaf from Cerrado in Minas Gerais, Brazil's main Arabica region and its first with an official designation of origin. Catuai and Mundo Novo cherries grown at about 900m are dried whole or partly pulped, then decaffeinated with sugarcane to keep body and sweetness. Described as rich and comforting: melted chocolate up front, fudge in the middle and a raisin-like sweetness on the finish. 43 reviews, about 88% five-star.

beans.name: El Indio, Colombia (Decaf)
beans.producer: Planadas, Tolima; about 175 smallholder families; up to 2,150m; Caturra
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, French press, AeroPress, moka pot (grind-matched; omni roast)
beans.desc: A natural-process Caturra from about 175 families in Planadas, southern Tolima, grown up to 2,150m in volcanic soil, then sugarcane decaffeinated to keep its sweetness. Sweet, fruity and full-bodied: dark chocolate first, then tart rhubarb and juicy pineapple. Partners have trained growers in natural processing since 2019, and most now process at least 80% of their harvest this way. 17 reviews.

beans.name: Grown Organic*, Peru (Water Decaf)
beans.producer: Various (smallholders selling to local co-ops, most farming under one hectare); 1,200-1,600m; Bourbon, Catimor, Caturra, Pache, Typica
beans.processFull: Washed; Mountain Water decaf (water from Pico de Orizaba, Mexico)
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, French press, AeroPress, moka pot (grind-matched; omni roast)
beans.desc: Peruvian smallholder coffee from steep Andean slopes at 1,200-1,600m, washed and sun-dried, then decaffeinated by the Mountain Water process (removes up to 99% of caffeine without chemicals). The page says it is Fairtrade certified and grown organically, though Craft Decaf is not organic certified. Toasty pecan, soft vanilla sponge sweetness and a zesty lemon icing finish; positioned as a smooth, sweet everyday decaf. Lightly roasted to protect the beans.

beans.name: Eastern Highlands, Papua New Guinea (Decaf)
beans.producer: Eastern Highlands; Sem Manmeri Kopi community lot from many smallholders; 1,600-1,850m; Blue Mountain, Bourbon
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, French press, AeroPress, moka pot (grind-matched; omni roast)
beans.desc: A community lot called Sem Manmeri Kopi ('People's Coffee' in Tok Pisin) from smallholders in PNG's Eastern Highlands, grown at 1,600-1,850m in volcanic soil. Only the ripest cherries are hand-picked, then washed and sun-dried to keep a bright profile through sugarcane decaffeination. Chocolate and caramel with lemon curd freshness; reviewers call it smooth, balanced and not bitter.

beans.name: Popayan, Colombia (Decaf)
beans.producer: Meseta de Popayan, Cauca; about 65 farmers via import partner Cofinet; 1,700m; Caturra, Castillo
beans.processFull: Fully washed; sugarcane decaf (about 97% of caffeine removed)
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, French press, AeroPress, moka pot (grind-matched; omni roast)
beans.desc: A fully washed Caturra and Castillo from the Meseta de Popayan in Cauca at about 1,700m, bought through Cofinet, which works with about 65 farmers there. Decaffeinated with sugarcane (ethyl acetate from fermented sugarcane), which the page calls the only completely natural method. Cinnamon sweetness and smooth dark chocolate with a rose finish, with a raw sweetness from the washed process.

beans.name: Bensa Bombe, Ethiopia (Decaf)
beans.producer: Bensa Bombe, Sidamo; about 650 smallholders (about 3 hectares each) via exporter Tariku Kare; 1,990-2,150m; Heirloom
beans.processFull: Natural; sugarcane decaf (97% of caffeine removed)
beans.listedNotes: Orange lolly, Caramel brittle, Red berries
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, French press, AeroPress, moka pot (grind-matched; omni roast)
beans.desc: A natural Ethiopian heirloom lot from about 650 smallholders at 1,990-2,150m in Sidamo, hand-picked and dried whole on raised beds, exported by Tariku Kare, which the page says supports local communities with school supplies, household financial help and farmer training. Sugarcane decaffeinated. Sweet and sticky: bright orange lolly, then lingering caramel brittle and a faint red berry finish.

beans.name: Half Caf - Popayan, Colombia
beans.producer: Meseta de Popayan, Cauca; about 65 farmers via import partner Cofinet; Caturra, Castillo
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, French press, AeroPress, moka pot (grind-matched; omni roast)
beans.desc: Craft Decaf's first half caf, from the Meseta de Popayan in Cauca: half sugarcane-decaffeinated and half caffeinated, both washed Caturra and Castillo. Meant for balanced morning cups or an afternoon pick-me-up, with chocolate, biscuits and butterscotch. Reviewers praise the flavour and the balanced caffeine level.

beans.name: FEDERACION CAMPESINA Espresso Roast
beans.producer: Cauca; Federación Campesina del Cauca (2,000+ rural families); 1,700m; Caturra, Colombia, Typica
beans.desc: A Fairtrade-certified espresso roast of Caturra, Colombia and Typica from the Federación Campesina del Cauca, which sources from more than 2,000 rural families who avoid toxic agrochemicals and conserve native seeds, soil and water. Grown at 1,700m and fully washed; berry-forward as espresso with chocolate, blackberry, redcurrant and grape, balanced acidity and a smooth, lasting aftertaste.

beans.name: SUGAR CANE DECAF
beans.processFull: Washed; sugarcane (ethyl acetate) decaf, at least 97% caffeine removed, done in Manizales
beans.desc: A single-origin Huila decaf from Garzón, decaffeinated at a plant in Manizales with ethyl acetate made from Colombian sugarcane molasses: the beans are steamed, repeatedly washed until at least 97% of caffeine is gone, steamed again, vacuum dried and cooled. Almond, panela and a bright orange acidity.

beans.name: FEDERACION CAMPESINA Filter Roast
beans.producer: Cauca highlands; Federación Campesina del Cauca; 1,700m; Caturra, Typica
beans.desc: The filter roast of the Federación Campesina Cauca coffee: 100% Arabica, Caturra and Typica, fully washed at about 1,700m and Fair Trade from origin. Balanced with lively acidity, a full body and a smooth, lingering aftertaste, with chocolate and sweet fruit.

beans.name: OXFORD BLEND
beans.producer: 50% Finca El Porvenir, Albán, Cundinamarca (natural; Caturra, Tabi, Colombia); 50% Federación Campesina del Cauca (fully washed; Caturra, Typica); 1,600-1,700m
beans.listedNotes: Sweet, Balanced, Chocolate (espresso); Caramel, Chocolate, Almond (with milk)
beans.desc: A two-process Colombian blend, half natural coffee from Hacienda El Porvenir and half fully washed coffee from the Federación Campesina del Cauca, meant to show the strengths of both. Sweet and balanced with hints of chocolate as espresso; with whole milk it turns smooth and full-bodied, with caramel, chocolate and almond.

beans.name: FINCA EL PORVENIR
beans.producer: Albán, Cundinamarca; Finca El Porvenir, Orlando Fierro; 1,600m; Caturra, Tabi
beans.listedNotes: Honey, Vanilla, Dried peach (aroma); Roast cacao, Chocolate finish
beans.desc: A red-honey coffee from a small Andean farm run by Orlando Fierro, uncle of the roaster's co-founder Milly. In red honey processing the cherry is partly pulped but the sticky mucilage stays on while drying, giving a syrupy body with more intensity than washed coffees and a richer character than naturals; balanced acidity, creamy body, roast cacao and a chocolate finish.

beans.name: Finca Tamaná Natural Process (Filter Roast)
beans.producer: Huila; Finca Tamaná, Elías Roa and his wife; 1,750m; Castillo, Colombia
beans.desc: A natural-process Castillo and Colombia from Elías Roa and his wife at Finca Tamaná in Huila, at 1,750m; the page says leading roasters and coffee houses favour their coffees and give feedback on improving production. Peach, nutty and dried fruit notes.

beans.name: Finca Tamaná Natural Process (Espresso Roast)
beans.producer: Huila; Finca Tamaná, Elías Roa and his wife; 1,750m; Castillo, Colombia
beans.desc: The espresso roast of the Finca Tamaná natural lot from Elías Roa and his wife in Huila (Castillo and Colombia, 1,750m), with peach, nutty and dried fruit notes.

beans.name: Half Caff Blend
beans.producer: La Falda, Garzón (Huila) and Inza (Cauca); decaf half is the Sugar Cane Decaf; 1,000-1,900m; Caturra, Castillo, Colombia, Typica
beans.processFull: Washed; decaf half by the sugarcane method
beans.listedNotes: Almond, Raw cane sugar, Hazelnut, Berries
beans.desc: A half-caffeinated blend of the roaster's sugarcane decaf with a washed coffee from Inza, Cauca, where smallholders dry their crops at the farm of Jesús Volvera, which shields the beans from unpredictable rain. Positioned as an everyday energy source with less caffeine; almond, raw cane sugar, hazelnut and berries.

beans.name: EL LATINO BLEND
beans.producer: Several small farms; no region named
beans.desc: A blend of the harvests of several small Colombian farms, designed for espresso and described as sweet and balanced.

beans.name: El Indio Microlot Natural Process (Filter Roast)
beans.producer: Planadas, Tolima; several family farms; 1,500-2,150m; Caturra
beans.desc: A limited-edition natural Caturra from family farms in Planadas, Tolima, some from indigenous communities who work with local cooperatives to improve farming and master natural processing. The roaster credits the natural process for the sweet, fruity character.

beans.name: El Indio Microlot Natural Process (Espresso Roast)
beans.producer: Planadas, Tolima; several family farms; 1,500-2,150m; Caturra
beans.desc: The espresso roast of the El Indio natural microlot from Planadas, Tolima: Caturra from several family farms, sweet and fruity thanks to natural processing.

beans.name: Café Sofía Espresso Roast
beans.producer: Antioquia, Risaralda and Valle del Cauca; Santa Teresita mill; 1,500m; mix of Arabica varieties
beans.listedNotes: Milk caramel, Mandarin, Creamy toffee, Chocolate chip cookie
beans.desc: A blend of washed Arabicas from three Colombian regions, graded and sorted at the Santa Teresita mill and roasted for espresso; rich aroma and pleasant acidity with milk caramel, mandarin, creamy toffee and chocolate chip cookie.

beans.name: CABALLERO ESPRESSO Special Edition
beans.producer: Huila; Finca Tamaná, Elías Roa and his wife; 1,750m; Papayo
beans.listedNotes: Fruity, Red wine, Red and black berries
beans.desc: A special edition of the roaster's classic Gentleman's Espresso using Papayo, a large-beaned variety named for its papaya-like shape, natural-processed at Finca Tamaná in Huila by long-term partner Elías Roa; a balanced espresso shot with natural-process sweetness and a rich, fruity aroma.

beans.name: Foundation Beans: Cafe Vida Washed, Costa Rica
beans.producer: Central Valley; imported by Cafe Imports via Oxcart Coffee; 1,200-1,800m; common Costa Rican varieties (Caturra, Catuai, Bourbon, Villa Sarchi and others)
beans.roastNote: Filter or espresso roast (chosen at purchase)
beans.listedNotes: Rounded sweetness, Mellow acidity, Full mouthfeel
beans.desc: The roaster's Foundation tier: a washed Costa Rican that shows the country's rounded sweetness, mellow acidity and full mouthfeel, from Cafe Imports' Oxcart sourcing programme, which works with the same micromills each year.

beans.name: Discovery Beans: Aceh Gayo Natural, Indonesia
beans.producer: Pegasing District, Aceh, Sumatra; Asman Gayo Mill (Asman Arianto); 1,300-1,650m; Ateng, Bor Bor, Catimor, Timor
beans.roastNote: Filter or espresso roast (chosen at purchase)
beans.desc: A natural-processed Sumatran that the roaster rarely sources, since wet-hulled lots tend to taste earthy and herbaceous; this one keeps the body and bold fruit of Indonesian coffee with blackcurrant, a spiced finish and a winey depth.

beans.name: Rare Beans: Gara Agena Natural, Ethiopia
beans.producer: Karamo, Bura, Sidama; Gara Agena washing station (Testi Coffee, Faysel Abdosh Yonis); 2,235-2,350m; Ethiopian heirloom
beans.roastNote: Filter or espresso roast (chosen at purchase)
beans.desc: A natural heirloom lot from Gara Agena, a steep hillside site at about 2,250m above the Geta River, overseen by Testi Coffee's Faysel A. Yonis, who has traded coffee since he was a schoolboy; rich, ripe, blueberry-like fruit.

beans.name: Gesha Beans: El Cerro Washed, Peru
beans.producer: El Corazón, Chirinos, Cajamarca; El Cerro farm, Yulisa Carhuallocllo Arévalo; 1,875-1,950m; Gesha
beans.processFull: Washed with 72-hour dry fermentation in tanks
beans.desc: A washed Gesha from Yulisa Carhuallocllo, who learned coffee from her father (second at Peru's first Cup of Excellence in 2017) and won Best of Cajamarca in 2023 and again in October 2025 with 90.25 points; dry-fermented for 72 hours in tanks with no added water. Floral with fruity sweetness and a tea-like finish.

beans.name: SOLO
beans.producer: Huehuetenango; smallholders via the Regional Select Programme; 1,400-2,200m; Bourbon, Catimor, Caturra, Maragogype, Pache
beans.listedNotes: Molasses sweetness, Gentle berry acidity, Syrupy body
beans.desc: A seasonal single-origin Guatemalan from Huehuetenango smallholders selling through a collective programme that rewards quality and keeps value in the region: molasses sweetness, gentle berry acidity, a heavy syrupy body and a long finish.

beans.name: TRIO
beans.producer: 34% Araku Valley (India), 33% Mchana AB (Kenya), 33% Mount Sunzu (Zambia)
beans.listedNotes: Complex fruit, Floral aromatics, Good acidity, Sweet syrupy body
beans.desc: A seasonal espresso blend from the Discovery range that pairs washed African coffees with an Indian one for lively acidity and a sweet, syrupy body, curated for consistency season to season on a clean house espresso base.

beans.name: Decaf Beans: Rwanda Sugarcane Decaf
beans.producer: Smallholders; region not shown; 1,500-2,000m; Red Bourbon, Jackson, Mibirizi, BM139
beans.desc: A washed Red Bourbon from Rwanda decaffeinated with sugarcane, keeping the stewed fruit and spice flavours typical of Rwandan coffee; the roaster's first Rwandan decaf, following an earlier Ethiopian one.

beans.name: Dos Pueblos (house espresso blend)
beans.producer: 67% Minas Gerais (Association of Producers of the Volcanic Region, via Vequis); 33% Udessa, Yirgacheffe (Mulugeta Tsige Exporters); 800-2,400m; Ethiopian 74158, Kurume, Dega
beans.processFull: Brazil natural; Ethiopia washed (48h tank fermentation)
beans.desc: The house espresso blend: a 67% natural Brazilian from smallholders of the Volcanic Region, adding milk-chocolate, caramel and a smooth medium body, with 33% washed Ethiopian microlot from Udessa for fruit-forward acidity. Sweet, smooth and balanced, for use alone or with milk.

beans.name: Caña Decaf
beans.producer: Huila; smallholders via Café Imports; Castillo, Caturra
beans.processFull: Pulped, fermented, washed; sugarcane (ethyl acetate) decaf
beans.listedNotes: Hazelnut praline, Milk chocolate, Caramel sweetness
beans.desc: A sweet, rich Huila decaf from smallholders, with caffeine removed using ethyl acetate derived from sugarcane fermentation, applied to steamed green beans in repeated tank cycles. Works as espresso or filter; harvested June-August 2024 and landed in the UK in November 2024.

beans.name: Blueberried
beans.producer: Edinson Argote, Quebraditas farm (Colombia); Mustefa Abakeno, Beshasha washing station, Jimma (Ethiopia, 2,040m); Caturra, Heirloom
beans.processFull: Colombian blueberry and wine-yeast co-ferment; Ethiopian washed
beans.desc: A Colombian Caturra co-fermented with ripe blueberries and wine yeast, blended with a washed Ethiopian heirloom for citrus brightness and structure. Concentrated blueberry sorbet and grape soda character.

beans.name: Gley Diaz
beans.producer: Nueva York hamlet, Amazonas; Gley Diaz, smallholder; Geisha
beans.processFull: Washed; 18-24h fermentation, dried on raised beds in covered tunnels (about 25 days)
beans.desc: The first lot from Gley Diaz, who grows Geisha on small family plots in the cloud-forested highlands of Amazonas, introduced via export partner Collective Bean. Clean, refined and elegant with apricot, wildflower honey and soft florals.

beans.name: Rumudamo
beans.producer: Sidama; Rumudamo station (Daye Bensa), about 600 smallholders; up to 2,200m; Heirloom
beans.processFull: Natural; dried whole on raised beds 3+ weeks
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry, Tropical, Floral, Jasmine as it cools
beans.desc: A sweet, floral natural from Daye Bensa's Rumudamo station, which placed second and third at Ethiopia's first Cup of Excellence in 2020 and funds preschools and processing classes for farmers' children. Layered strawberry and tropical fruit turning to jasmine as it cools.

beans.name: Nafkot
beans.producer: Gedicho, Yirgacheffe; Nafkot Admasu, 2-hectare farm; 2,170m; Heirloom
beans.listedNotes: Peach iced tea, Wild berries, Tropical fruit
beans.desc: Grown by Nafkot Admasu under native enset trees on her own 2-hectare farm with its own processing station. Part of the Ama Commitment Project (Ephtah Coffee) for female producers; bought via Covoya. Peach iced tea, wild berries and tropical fruit.

beans.name: Bookkisa
beans.producer: Bookkisa kebele, Shakiso, Guji; Sookoo Coffee (Ture Waji); 2,000-2,150m; Gibirinna 74110, Serto 74112
beans.desc: A clean, fruit-forward natural from smallholders delivering to the Bookkisa washing station run by family-owned Sookoo Coffee, dried in thin layers and turned at least six times daily. Two Jimma Research Centre selections; blueberry, honey and raspberry.

beans.name: Sumatra Mandheling
beans.listedNotes: Very full flavour, Heavy low notes
beans.desc: A washed Arabica Sumatra Mandheling described as very full in flavour without burnt characteristics. The dense bean needs about 14 minutes of roasting; heavy, low notes.

beans.name: Colombia Excelso Fairtrade
beans.desc: A medium-roasted washed Colombian, balanced and lemony with mild acidity and gentle body; presented as a good introduction to speciality coffee.

beans.name: Jersey Blend
beans.desc: A classic washed Arabica blend from Central America, sold as a taste of Jersey to enjoy anywhere.

beans.name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe (Hama Co-operative)
beans.producer: Yirgacheffe; Hama Co-operative (from URL and tags)
beans.desc: A medium-roast washed Yirgacheffe with pronounced fruit balanced by gentle underlying sweetness, presented as a good representative of the region.

beans.name: Morning Coffee
beans.desc: A morning blend described as smooth and easy to drink, a good start to the day.

beans.name: Old Brown Java
beans.desc: A coffee aged for three years for a smooth, heavy flavour; the roast removes off-flavours picked up during maturing so it stays lively. Aimed at people unsure about dark roast who want something on the darker side.

beans.name: Bologne Espresso Blend
beans.producer: Daterra estate (Brazil Arabica); Sethuraman estate (southern India Robusta)
beans.listedNotes: Low acidity, Full body, Smooth (description only)
beans.desc: A medium-roast Arabica and Robusta blend that mimics a classic European coffee style: low acidity, full and smooth body.

beans.name: Brazil Daterra Santa Colomba (Medium Roasted)
beans.producer: Daterra Farm; Cerrado (Minas Gerais) and Mogiana (São Paulo)
beans.listedNotes: Gentle acidity, Caramel finish, Delicate sweetness
beans.desc: A medium roast from Daterra Farm with soft acidity and a caramel-toned finish; as espresso it is light and delicately sweet, suiting cappuccinos. The roaster has bought from this farm for years.

beans.name: Bourbon Dark Espresso Blend
beans.desc: One of the shop's most popular espresso coffees, also good in a cafetiere: Sumatran and Brazilian Arabica with speciality Indian Robusta for a heavy, smooth and rich cup.

beans.name: Heritage Blend
beans.roastNote: Dark Java with much lighter Malabar
beans.desc: An espresso blend created in 2021 by shop manager Josh from two aged heritage coffees, Malabar and Java. Pairing darker Java with much lighter Malabar gives a deep, rich coffee, especially good as cappuccino.

beans.name: Coopers Red Packet (coffee and chicory)
beans.desc: A ground blend of 70% robusta and 30% chicory reviving the Jersey tradition of Breton farmers stretching coffee with roasted chicory.

beans.name: Kenya AA
beans.processFull: Washed; extra 8-16h soak in clean water, sun-dried
beans.desc: A washed blend from Nyeri smallholders, processed with recirculated river water and a Kenyan-style extended soak before sun-drying; deep dark chocolate and red fruit.

beans.desc: A boozy, fruit-forward natural Catimor from Banka Farm in Yunnan at 1,800m, roasted to order in London.

guides.why: Clean and clear: brings out florals, fruit and acidity.
steps: Rinse the paper filter with hot water and tip the water away.
Add the coffee and gently level the bed.
Pour about 40 g of water to wet all the grounds. Wait 30–40 seconds while it bubbles (the bloom).
Pour slowly in small circles up to 150 g by 1:15.
Keep pouring to 250 g by about 1:45, then give the dripper a gentle swirl.
Let it drain. Aim to finish between 3:00 and 3:30. If it runs faster, grind finer; if slower, grind coarser.

guides.why: Forgiving and versatile: works for nearly any coffee.
steps: Rinse the filter in the cap and set the AeroPress on your mug.
Add the coffee, then pour all 220 g of water.
Stir three times, put the plunger in loosely to stop dripping, and wait until 2:00.
Swirl gently, then press down slowly for about 30 seconds.
For a stronger cup, use 18 g of coffee. For a softer, less bitter cup, use water a few degrees cooler.

guides.why: Rich and full-bodied: suits chocolate, nutty and caramel notes.
steps: Add the coffee to the press and pour all 500 g of water.
Leave it for 4 minutes without stirring.
Break the crust on top with a spoon and scoop off the foam.
Wait another 4–5 minutes so the fine particles sink.
Press the plunger only to the surface of the coffee, then pour gently. Leave the last bit in the pot.

guides.why: Concentrated and sweet: ideal for milk drinks and chocolatey coffees.
steps: Weigh 18 g of coffee into the basket and level it.
Tamp firmly and evenly.
Lock in and start the shot straight away.
Stop at 36 g in the cup (a 1:2 ratio). Aim for 25–30 seconds.
Sour or thin? Grind finer. Bitter or harsh? Grind coarser. Light roasts often taste better at 1:2.5.

guides.why: Strong and bold: a stovetop take on espresso-style coffee.
steps: Fill the base with just-boiled water up to the valve.
Fill the basket with coffee and level it without pressing down.
Screw it together using a tea towel, as the base will be hot.
Heat on a medium-low flame with the lid open.
When the coffee turns pale and starts to sputter, take it off the heat and run the base under cold water to stop it.

guides.why: Very clean and tea-like, thanks to its thick filter. Great for sharing.
steps: Place the filter with the thick, three-layer side towards the spout and rinse it well.
Add the coffee and pour 60 g of water to bloom. Wait 45 seconds.
Pour in slow circles to 300 g.
Once it drops a little, pour to 500 g.
Aim to finish at 4:00–4:30. Remove the filter and give the coffee a swirl.

podTips.Nespresso Original: Ristretto (25 ml) for intensity 9+, espresso (40 ml) for most, lungo (110 ml) for light, fruity capsules.
podTips.Nespresso Vertuo: The machine reads the barcode and sets the cup size, so just pop it in.
podTips.Dolce Gusto: Use the strength lever: fewer bars for brighter capsules, more for darker ones.
podTips.Tassimo: The machine reads the barcode. Descale regularly, as it strongly affects taste.
